Àmọ́ àwọn àìsàn mìíràn lè rí bí kọ́lẹ́rà, nítorí náà ìdánwò yàrá (lab test) nìkan ló lè fi ẹ̀rí hàn ohun tó ń ṣẹlẹ̀ gan-an.

Ohun Àkọ́kọ́: Má Jẹ́ Kí Ara Ènìyàn Gbẹ

Gbígbẹ ara ni ohun tí ó ń pa ènìyàn jù lọ nínú kọ́lẹ́rà. Ènìyàn kì í kú nítorí kòkòrò àrùn fúnra rẹ̀, ṣùgbọ́n nítorí pé ara pàdánù omi àti iyọ̀ jù. Nítorí náà, ohun àkọ́kọ́ tí ẹbí gbọ́dọ̀ ṣe ni láti bẹ̀rẹ̀ sí fún aláìsàn ní omi àti iyọ̀ padà sínú ara lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀, kí wọ́n tó dé ilé ìwòsàn.

Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) ni ohun tó ṣe pàtàkì jù lọ. Tí àpò ORS bá wà, è ṣe é pọ̀ mọ́ omi mímọ́ gẹ́gẹ́ bí wọ́n ṣe kọ sórí àpò náà. Tí ORS kò bá sí, ẹ lè ṣe ọ̀kan fún ìgbà díẹ̀ ní ilé: è fi ṣúgà ìwọ̀n ṣíbí kékeré mẹ́fà tí ó kún àti ìdajì ṣíbí kékeré iyọ̀ sínú lítà omi mímọ́ kan (omi tí ẹ ti sè tàbí tí ẹ ti lo chlorine ṣe). Èyí jẹ́ fún ìgbà pàjáwìrì, kì í ṣe aṣeyọrí ORS tó dára. Ẹ máa fún aláìsàn ní kéré-kéré, ṣùgbọ́n ẹ máa fún un ní ìgbà gbogbo, ẹ má dáwọ́ dúró. Àgbàlagbà tí ara rẹ̀ ti gbẹ gidigidi lè nílò ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ lítà láàárín àwọn wákàtí àkọ́kọ́. Fún ọmọdé tí ó ṣì ń mu ọmú, ẹ máa tẹ̀síwájú fífún un ní ọmú pẹ̀lú ORS.

Ẹ máa wò fún àwọn àmì wọ̀nyí tí ó fi hàn pé gbígbẹ ara ti pọ̀ jù: ojú ti rì sínú, tí ẹ bá fa awọ ẹ̀yìn ọwọ́ kò padà sí ipò rẹ̀ kíákíá, ọkàn ń lu kánkán ṣùgbọ́n aláìlágbára, ènìyàn ń sùn kiri tàbí kò lè dáhùn, kò lè mu omi mọ́, kò sì tọ̀ tàbí ìtọ̀ rẹ̀ ṣókùnkùn púpọ̀. Tí ẹ bá rí èyíkéyìí nínú àwọn wọ̀nyí, ẹ gbé aláìsàn lọ sí ilé ìwòsàn lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀, nítorí wọ́n nílò omi inú iṣọ́n (drip/IV fluid). Ìyẹn jẹ́ pàjáwìrì.

Ẹ Sọ Fún Àwọn Aṣojú Ìlera

Ẹ má dúró de èsì ìdánwò yàrá kí ẹ tó sọ fún àwọn aṣojú ìlera. Tí ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ènìyàn bá ń ṣe ìgbẹ́ gbuuru àti èèbì ní àgbègbè kan ní àkókò kan náà, ìyẹn ti tó fún ìfitóníléti. Ẹ pe ilé ìwòsàn tó sún mọ́ yín, ẹ̀ka ìlera ìjọba ìbílẹ̀, tàbí olùṣọ́ àrùn àjàkálẹ̀ àrùn (disease surveillance officer). Ẹ sọ fún wọn iye ènìyàn tó ti ṣàìsàn, ibi tí wọ́n wà, ìgbà tí àìsàn náà bẹ̀rẹ̀, àti bóyá ohun kan wà tí gbogbo wọn lo papọ̀, bíi kànga kan, ìṣọ̀ omi kan, oúnjẹ kan, tàbí àpéjọ kan.

Tí ẹ bá ṣe ìfitóníléti ní kíákíá, àwọn aṣojú ìlera yóò lè wá dán omi wò, fi ẹ̀rí àìsàn múlẹ̀, mú ORS àti omi drip wá, àti bẹ̀rẹ̀ ìgbésẹ̀ tó yẹ.

Ẹ Dáàbò Bo Omi Yín

Kọ́lẹ́rà máa ń tàn kálẹ̀ ní pàtàkì nípasẹ̀ omi àti oúnjẹ tí ìgbẹ́ ẹni tí ó ní àrùn ti bà jẹ́. Omi tí gbogbo ènìyàn ń lo papọ̀ tí ó ti di àìmọ́ ni ohun tó ń fà á jù lọ nínú àjàkálẹ̀ àrùn kọ́lẹ́rà.

Ẹ ṣe omi gbogbo kí ẹ tó mu. Ẹ sè omi tí yóò fi gbóná hùhù fún ìṣẹ́jú kan ṣáájú kí ẹ tó lò ó. Tí ẹ kò bá lè sè é, ẹ lo chlorine, bíi omi bleach tàbí tábúlẹ́ẹ̀tì ìmọ́tótó omi tó wà lọ́jà, kí ẹ sì tẹ̀lé ìlànà tó wà lórí àpò rẹ̀. Tí ẹ kò bá ní chlorine, tí ẹ kò sì lè sè omi, ẹ lè lo ọ̀nà SODIS: ẹ fi omi kún igo ìkékeré oníhà méjì tó mọ́, ẹ fi sí ibi tí oòrùn ti ń tàn sára rẹ̀ tààrà fún wákàtí mẹ́fà. Èyí kì í ṣe ohun tó pé pátápátá, ṣùgbọ́n yóò dín ewu kù.

Ẹ fi omi tí ẹ ti ṣe pamọ́ dáadáa. Ẹ fi sínú ohun èlò tó mọ́, tó ní ìdérí, tí ẹnu rẹ̀ kéré. Ẹ má fi ọwọ́ tàbí ife bọ̀ sínú omi náà. Ẹ dà á jáde, tàbí ẹ lo ohun èlò tó ní tapu.

Ẹ dáwọ́ lílo orísun omi tí ẹ fura sí dúró fún mímu, sísè oúnjẹ, fífọ oúnjẹ, tàbí fífọ eyín títí tí àwọn aṣojú ìlera yóò fi wá dán an wò, tàbí títí tí ẹ yóò fi ní omi mímọ́ mìíràn.

Ilé Ìgbọ̀nsẹ̀ Àti Ìmọ́tótó

Fífọ ọwọ́ kì í ṣe ohun ìyàn, ó jẹ́ dandan. Gbogbo ènìyàn nínú ilé gbọ́dọ̀ fọ ọwọ́ pẹ̀lú ọṣẹ àti omi lẹ́yìn tí wọ́n bá lo ilé ìgbọ̀nsẹ̀, lẹ́yìn tí wọ́n bá fi ọwọ́ kàn aláìsàn tàbí ohunkóhun tí ìgbẹ́ tàbí èèbì rẹ̀ ti kàn, ṣáájú kí wọ́n tó sè oúnjẹ, ṣáájú kí wọ́n tó jẹun, àti ṣáájú kí wọ́n tó bọ́ ọmọ lọ́wọ́. Tí ọṣẹ kò bá sí, eérú lè ṣiṣẹ́ díẹ̀, ṣùgbọ́n ọṣẹ dára jù.

Ẹ sọ ìgbẹ́ àti èèbì nù ní ọ̀nà tó tọ́. Gbogbo ìgbẹ́ àti èèbì aláìsàn gbọ́dọ̀ wọ inú ilé ìgbọ̀nsẹ̀. Tí aláìsàn kò bá lè dé ilé ìgbọ̀nsẹ̀, ẹ fi garawa tàbí ohun èlò mú u, ẹ fi omi chlorine (0.2% chlorine) sí, ẹ dúró ìṣẹ́jú ọgbọ̀n, lẹ́yìn náà ẹ dà á sínú ilé ìgbọ̀nsẹ̀. Ẹ má dà ìgbẹ́ tí ẹ kò tíì ṣe mọ́tótó sínú gọ́tà, odò, tàbí ilẹ̀ pẹ̀tẹ́lẹ̀.

Ẹ fọ ibi tí ìgbẹ́ tàbí èèbì ti kàn mọ́. Ẹ fi omi chlorine 0.2% fọ aṣọ ìbùsùn, aṣọ, àti ilẹ̀ tí ìgbẹ́ tàbí èèbì ti kàn. Àwo, ife, àti ṣíbí tí aláìsàn lò, ẹ fọ wọ́n lọ́tọ̀ pẹ̀lú omi mímọ́ àti ọṣẹ tàbí chlorine.

Yíyàgbẹ́ sí ìta gbọ́dọ̀ dáwọ́ dúró pátápátá. Tí àwọn ènìyàn kan nínú àdúgbò ṣì ń yàgbẹ́ sí ìta, ìyẹn ti di ewu ńlá fún gbogbo ènìyàn báyìí. Ẹ nílò ètò ilé ìgbọ̀nsẹ̀ pàjáwìrì lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀.

Ààbò Oúnjẹ

Ẹ sè oúnjẹ dáadáa, kí ẹ sì jẹ ẹ́ nígbà tí ó ṣì gbóná. Kòkòrò àrùn kọ́lẹ́rà máa ń kú nígbà tí oúnjẹ bá gbóná. Ẹ má jẹ ẹfọ́ tàbí èso tí ẹ kò bá lè bó (peel). Ẹ má jẹ oúnjẹ tí ó ti pẹ́ ní ìwọ̀n oòrùn yàrá, ní pàtàkì nígbà tí ojú ọjọ́ bá gbóná. Ẹ yẹra fún oúnjẹ tí wọ́n ta lójú pópó tàbí oúnjẹ àpéjọ nígbà àjàkálẹ̀ àrùn àyàfi tí ẹ bá mọ̀ pé wọ́n ṣe é dáadáa.

Ẹ fọ ibi tí ẹ ń gbé sè oúnjẹ pẹ̀lú omi mímọ́ ṣáájú kí ẹ tó bẹ̀rẹ̀.

Bí A Ṣe Lè Tọ́jú Aláìsàn Ní Ilé

Tí aláìsàn bá ṣì lè mu omi, tí gbígbẹ ara rẹ̀ kò sì lé jù, ẹ lè máa tọ́jú rẹ̀ ní ilé pẹ̀lú ORS nígbà tí ẹ ń retí tàbí láàárín àwọn ìbẹ̀wò ilé ìwòsàn. Ẹni tí ó ń tọ́jú aláìsàn gbọ́dọ̀ yà àwọn ohun èlò (àwo, ife, ṣíbí) àti aṣọ ìbùsùn sọ́tọ̀ fún aláìsàn, fọ ọwọ́ lẹ́yìn ìfọwọ́kàn kọ̀ọ̀kan, kí ó sì ya ohun tí ó ti jáde lára aláìsàn sọ́tọ̀ kí ó sì pa á mọ́.

Ṣùgbọ́n, tí èyíkéyìí nínú àwọn wọ̀nyí bá jẹ́ òótọ́, ẹ gbé aláìsàn lọ sí ilé ìwòsàn lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀:

Aláìsàn ti ṣàfihàn àmì gbígbẹ ara tó burú. Aláìsàn jẹ́ ọmọdé tí kò tíì pé ọdún márùn-ún. Aláìsàn jẹ́ obìnrin tí ó lóyún. Aláìsàn ní àìsàn mìíràn tẹ́lẹ̀.

Kọ́lẹ́rà lè pa ju ìdajì àwọn tí kò gba ìtọ́jú lọ, ṣùgbọ́n pẹ̀lú ìtọ́jú ìfomi-padà-sí-ara tó dára, ìwọ̀n ikú lè dín kù sí ìdá kan nínú ọgọ́rùn-ún (1%). Nítorí náà, ríra ilé ìwòsàn jẹ́ ìyàtọ̀ láàárín ìyè àti ikú.

Tí Ènìyàn Bá Kú

Tí ènìyàn bá kú sí ohun tí wọ́n fura sí pé kọ́lẹ́rà ni, ara oku náà ṣì lè tàn àrùn kálẹ̀. Àwọn tí wọ́n ti gba ìdánilẹ́kọ̀ọ́ ni wọ́n yẹ kí wọ́n múra oku náà sílẹ̀ fún ìsìnkú. Tí àwọn tí wọ́n ti gba ìdánilẹ́kọ̀ọ́ kò bá sí, àwọn tí wọ́n bá ń kó oku gbọ́dọ̀ wọ gílọ́ọ̀fù, dín ìfọwọ́kàn omi ara kù, fi omi chlorine 0.5% wẹ̀ ara oku náà, wọ́n sì gbọ́dọ̀ fọ ọwọ́ wọn dáadáa lẹ́yìn náà. Àpéjọ ìsìnkú ńlá tí gbogbo ènìyàn bá jọ jẹun ti jẹ́ ohun tí ó ti tàn kọ́lẹ́rà kálẹ̀ nínú ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àjàkálẹ̀ àrùn ṣáájú. Ẹ dín iye ènìyàn kù, kí ẹ sì yẹra fún oúnjẹ àpapọ̀ ní ibi ìsìnkú.

Ohun Tí Ẹbí Kò Gbọ́dọ̀ Ṣe

Ẹ má lo oògùn tí ó ń da ìgbẹ́ dúró (bíi loperamide). Irú oògùn bẹ́ẹ̀ máa ń fa ìfun lọ́ra ṣùgbọ́n kò pa kòkòrò àrùn. Yóò bò iye omi tí ara ń pàdánù mọ́, ohun sì yóò burú sí i.

Ẹ má lọ ra oògùn apakòkòrò (antibiotic) ní ọjà fúnra yín. Oògùn apakòkòrò ní ipò rẹ̀ nínú ìtọ́jú kọ́lẹ́rà tó burú, ṣùgbọ́n àwọn oṣiṣẹ́ ìlera nìkan ló yẹ kí wọ́n pinnu èwo àti ìgbà wo. Oògùn apakòkòrò kò rọ́pò ìfomi-padà-sí-ara, bí ènìyàn sì bá ń lo oògùn apakòkòrò lọ́nà tí kò tọ́, kòkòrò àrùn yóò kẹ́kọ̀ọ́ bí a ṣe lè kọjú rẹ̀.

Ẹ má lé àwọn ẹbí tí wọ́n ní aláìsàn kúrò tàbí dójútì wọ́n. Tí ènìyàn bá bẹ̀rẹ̀ sí yẹra tàbí fi àbùkù kàn àwọn ẹbí tí kọ́lẹ́rà bá, àwọn ẹbí yẹn yóò bẹ̀rù láti sọ tàbí lọ sí ilé ìwòsàn, ènìyàn sì yóò tún kú sí i. Ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ yìí ti ṣẹlẹ̀ ní ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àjàkálẹ̀ àrùn kọ́lẹ́rà ṣáájú.

Ibi Tí Ìmọ̀ràn Yìí Ti Wá

Ìmọ̀ràn yìí dá lórí àwọn ìwé WHO (World Health Organization) lórí kọ́lẹ́rà àti ìlànà ìdáhùn sí àjàkálẹ̀ àrùn, ìmọ̀ràn WHO/UNICEF lórí ìtọ́jú ìfomi-padà-sí-ara (oral rehydration therapy), àwọn ìgbaniníyànjú WHO fún ìṣe omi mímọ́ nínú ilé àti ìpamọ́ rẹ̀ lọ́nà ààbò, àti ìlànà CDC (U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention) fún ìdènà àti ìṣàkóso kọ́lẹ́rà. Ìwọ̀n chlorine fún àwọn ohun oríṣiríṣi (0.2% fún ìgbẹ́ àti ilẹ̀, 0.5% fún oku) tẹ̀lé ìlànà WHO fún ìlera àyíká ní àsìkò pàjáwìrì. Ìfiwéra ìwọ̀n ikú (ju ìdajì lọ láìsí ìtọ́jú, ṣùgbọ́n kéré ju 1% pẹ̀lú ìtọ́jú) wá láti inú àkójọ àwọn ìṣirò àbójútó kọ́lẹ́rà àgbáyé WHO.

Ẹ tẹ̀lé ohun tí àwọn aṣojú ìlera àdúgbò tàbí ti orílẹ̀-èdè yín bá sọ, nítorí ọ̀nà tí wọ́n ń gbà kọjú àjàkálẹ̀ àrùn lè yàtọ̀ láti orílẹ̀-èdè dé orílẹ̀-èdè, ó sì lè yí padà bí ipò bá ń yí padà.

Kínni Àwọn Ẹbí Le Ṣe Tí Ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ Ènìyàn Bá Ń Ṣe Àìsàn Ìgbẹ́ Gbuuru Olómi Àti Èèbì, Tí Wọ́n Sì Ń Fura Sí Kọ́lẹ́rà
Bí A Ṣe Lè Mọ̀ Pé Ọ̀ràn Yìí Ṣe Pàtàkì

Nígbà tí ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ènìyàn ní àgbègbè kan bá bẹ̀rẹ̀ sí ṣe ìgbẹ́ gbuuru olómi tó le gan-an àti èèbì ní àkókò kúkúrú kan náà, ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ yìí jẹ́ àmì ewu ńlá tó ń fi hàn pé àjàkálẹ̀ àrùn ń ṣẹlẹ̀, ó sì ṣeéṣe kí ó jẹ́ láti orísun kan tí gbogbo wọn ń lò, bíi omi tàbí oúnjẹ. Kọ́lẹ́rà (tí kòkòrò àrùn Vibrio cholerae ń fà á) máa ń mú kí ènìyàn máa gbe omi jáde lára púpọ̀ nípasẹ̀ ìgbẹ́ gbuuru tí kò ní ìrora inú. Ìgbẹ́ náà máa ń rí bíi omi ìrẹsì. Ẹni tí àìsàn náà bá lé lórí lè pàdánù ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ lítà omi láti ara rẹ̀ láàárín wákàtí díẹ̀. Gbígbẹ ara (dehydration) ni ohun tó máa ń pa ènìyàn, ó sì lè pa ènìyàn láàárín wákàtí díẹ̀ tí ènìyàn kò bá gba ìtọ́jú. Àmọ́ àwọn àìsàn mìíràn lè rí bí kọ́lẹ́rà, pẹ̀lú rotavirus, norovirus, E. coli tó ń mú májèlé jáde, Shigella, àti Cryptosporidium. Ìdánwò yàrá (lab test) nìkan ló lè fi ẹ̀rí hàn ohun tó ń fà á gan-an. Ṣùgbọ́n ìdáhùn lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀ tí àdúgbò yẹ kí ó gbé jẹ́ ohun kan náà láìka irú kòkòrò àrùn sí: dènà ikú nípasẹ̀ gbígbẹ ara, ṣe ìjábọ̀ sí àwọn aṣojú ìlera, dáàbò bo orísun omi, kí a sì gé ọ̀nà tí àrùn ń gbà tàn kálẹ̀.

Ohun Àkọ́kọ́: Má Jẹ́ Kí Ènìyàn Kú Nítorí Gbígbẹ Ara

Gbígbẹ ara ni ohun tó ń pa ènìyàn nínú kọ́lẹ́rà àti àwọn àrùn ìgbẹ́ gbuuru olómi mìíràn, kì í ṣe kòkòrò àrùn fúnra rẹ̀. Ikú lè ṣẹlẹ̀ láàárín wákàtí díẹ̀ lẹ́yìn tí àwọn àmì àìsàn bá bẹ̀rẹ̀, ní pàtàkì fún àwọn ọmọdé, àwọn àgbàlagbà, àwọn aboyún, àti àwọn tí wọ́n ti ní àìsàn mìíràn tẹ́lẹ̀. Fífún aláìsàn ní omi àti iyọ̀ padà sínú ara gbọ́dọ̀ bẹ̀rẹ̀ ní ilé lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀, ṣáájú kí aláìsàn tó dé ilé ìwòsàn.

Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) ni ohun tó ṣe pàtàkì jù lọ. Tí àpò ORS bá wà, ẹ pọ̀ mọ́ omi mímọ́ tí ẹ ti sè tàbí tí ẹ ti lo chlorine ṣe, gẹ́gẹ́ bí wọ́n ṣe kọ sórí àpò náà. Tí ORS kò bá sí, ẹ lè ṣe ọ̀kan fún ìgbà díẹ̀ ní ilé: ẹ fi ṣúgà ìwọ̀n ṣíbí kékeré mẹ́fà tí ó kún àti ìdajì ṣíbí kékeré iyọ̀ sínú lítà omi mímọ́ kan. Èyí jẹ́ fún ìgbà pàjáwìrì nìkan, kì í ṣe ohun tó lè rọ́pò ORS tó dára. Ẹ máa fún aláìsàn ní kéré-kéré, ṣùgbọ́n ẹ máa fún un ní ìgbà gbogbo, ẹ má dáwọ́ dúró. Ẹ má dúró títí aláìsàn yóò fi sọ pé òùngbẹ ń gbẹ́ ọn, nítorí nígbà tí gbígbẹ ara bá ti pọ̀ jù, ènìyàn kì yóò tilẹ̀ mọ̀ pé òùngbẹ ń gbẹ́ ọn mọ́. Àgbàlagbà tí ara rẹ̀ ti gbẹ gidigidi lè nílò ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ lítà láàárín àwọn wákàtí àkọ́kọ́.

Fún ọmọdé tí ó ṣì ń mu ọmú, ẹ máa tẹ̀síwájú fífún un ní ọmú pẹ̀lú ORS. Fún ìkókó tí kò mu ọmú, ẹ tẹ̀síwájú fífún un ní wàrà tàbí fọ́múlà tí ó ń lò láàárín àwọn ìwọ̀n ORS.

Ẹ máa wò fún àwọn àmì ewu wọ̀nyí tí ó fi hàn pé gbígbẹ ara ti pọ̀ jù: ojú ti rì sínú, tí ẹ bá fa awọ ẹ̀yìn ọwọ́ kò padà sí ipò rẹ̀ kíákíá, ọkàn ń lu kánkán ṣùgbọ́n aláìlágbára, ènìyàn ń sùn kiri tàbí kò lè dáhùn, kò lè mu omi tàbí ó ń bì ohun gbogbo padà, kò sì tọ̀ tàbí ìtọ̀ rẹ̀ ṣókùnkùn púpọ̀. Tí ẹ bá rí èyíkéyìí nínú àwọn wọ̀nyí, ìyẹn jẹ́ pàjáwìrì. Ẹ gbé aláìsàn lọ sí ilé ìwòsàn lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀ nítorí wọ́n nílò omi inú iṣọ́n (drip/IV fluid).

Àwọn àmì ewu àfikún fún ọmọdé: ọmọ ń bì ohun gbogbo padà láìdáwọ́dúró, ẹ̀jẹ̀ wà nínú ìgbẹ́, ìkókó tí kò tíì pé oṣù mẹ́fà ní ibà gíga pẹ̀lú ìgbẹ́ gbuuru, àti ọmọ tí ó kọ̀ láti jẹun tàbí mu ohunkóhun. Gbogbo àwọn wọ̀nyí nílò ìtọ́jú ìṣègùn tó ní ìyára, bí ó tilẹ̀ jẹ́ pé ọmọ kò dà bí ẹni tí ara rẹ̀ ti gbẹ.

Kọ́lẹ́rà lè pa ju ìdajì àwọn tí kò gba ìtọ́jú lọ, ṣùgbọ́n pẹ̀lú ìtọ́jú ìfomi-padà-sí-ara tó dára, ìwọ̀n ikú lè dín kù sí ìdá kan nínú ọgọ́rùn-ún (1%). Nítorí náà, ríra ilé ìwòsàn jẹ́ ìyàtọ̀ láàárín ìyè àti ikú.

Ẹ Sọ Fún Àwọn Aṣojú Ìlera Lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀

Ẹ má dúró de èsì ìdánwò yàrá kí ẹ tó jábọ̀. Tí ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ènìyàn bá ń ṣe ìgbẹ́ gbuuru olómi àti èèbì ní àgbègbè kan ní àkókò kan náà, ìyẹn ti tó fún ìfitóníléti lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀ lábẹ́ àwọn Òfin Ìlera Àgbáyé ti WHO àti lábẹ́ ètò ìṣọ́ àrùn orílẹ̀-èdè fẹ́rẹ̀ẹ́ jẹ́ gbogbo wọn.

Ẹ kàn sí ilé ìwòsàn tó sún mọ́ yín, ẹ̀ka ìlera ìjọba ìbílẹ̀, olùṣọ́ àrùn àjàkálẹ̀ (disease surveillance officer), tàbí ọ̀nà ìfitóníléti orílẹ̀-èdè. Ẹ sọ fún wọn: iye ènìyàn tí wọ́n ti ṣàìsàn, bí ọjọ́ orí wọn ṣe tó, ìgbà tí àìsàn náà bẹ̀rẹ̀ (ẹ sọ bóyá gbogbo wọn bẹ̀rẹ̀ ní àkókò kan náà tàbí ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan, nítorí ìyẹn yóò ran àwọn aṣojú ìlera lọ́wọ́ láti mọ̀ bóyá ó jẹ́ ìfara-hàn ẹ̀ẹ̀kan ṣoṣo tàbí ìfara-hàn tó ń tẹ̀síwájú), orúkọ àti ibùdó orísun omi tí a fura sí, àti ohunkóhun mìíràn tí wọ́n ṣàkíyèsí (bóyá àwọ̀ omi yí padà, bóyá ó ń rùn, bóyá ìkún omi ti ṣẹlẹ̀ láìpẹ́, bóyá ilé ìgbọ̀nsẹ̀ wà nítòsí orísun omi, bóyá ẹranko ń wọlé sí ibẹ̀).

Ìfitóníléti ní kíákíá máa ń bẹ̀rẹ̀ àwọn ìdáhùn tí àdúgbò fúnra rẹ̀ kò lè ṣe: ìdánwò yàrá ti orísun omi, ìfọwọ́sí àìsàn ní ìṣègùn, ìpèsè ORS àti omi drip, ìwádìí àjàkálẹ̀ àrùn láti fi ẹ̀rí orísun múlẹ̀ àti láti wá gbogbo àwọn tí wọ́n ti farahan, àti àtúnṣe ti ẹ̀rọ fún orísun omi náà.

Ẹ Dáàbò Bo Orísun Omi

Kọ́lẹ́rà àti ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn ohun mìíràn tó ń fa ìgbẹ́ gbuuru olómi máa ń tàn kálẹ̀ ní pàtàkì nípasẹ̀ omi àti oúnjẹ tí ìgbẹ́ ẹni tí ó ní àrùn ti bà jẹ́. Orísun omi tí gbogbo ènìyàn ń lò papọ̀ tí ó ti di àìmọ́ ni ohun tó ń fà á jù lọ nínú àjàkálẹ̀ àrùn.

Ẹ dáwọ́ lílo orísun omi tí ẹ fura sí dúró lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀. Èyí ni ìgbésẹ̀ àyíká tí àkókò ṣe pàtàkì jù lọ fún un. Wákàtí kọ̀ọ̀kan tí orísun omi tí ó ti di àìmọ́ bá ṣì ń ṣiṣẹ́, àwọn ènìyàn tuntun ń farahan sí ewu. Àwọn ìdílé gbọ́dọ̀ dáwọ́ lílo orísun omi náà dúró fún ohunkóhun: mímu, sísè oúnjẹ, ṣíṣe oúnjẹ sílẹ̀, fífọ oúnjẹ, fífọ ohun èlò oúnjẹ, fífọ eyín, àti ohunkóhun mìíràn tí yóò mú kí omi náà wọ ẹnu ènìyàn. Tí orísun náà bá jẹ́ kànga àdúgbò, ìhó omi (borehole), paipu omi, tàbí odò, àwọn olórí àdúgbò gbọ́dọ̀ sọ fún gbogbo ilé tí ó ń lò ó. Ìkìlọ̀ lẹ́nu nìkan kò tó. Ìdènà ti ara munadoko jù: ẹ fí okùn yí ká, fi ènìyàn sí ibẹ̀ láti ṣọ́, fi àmì ìkìlọ̀ sí ibi tí gbogbo ènìyàn yóò rí.

Ṣùgbọ́n ẹ gbọ́dọ̀ pèsè omi mìíràn lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀. A kò lè sọ fún ènìyàn pé kí wọ́n dáwọ́ lílo omi dúró láì fún wọn ní àṣàyàn mìíràn.

Ẹ ṣe gbogbo omi mímu. Ẹ sè omi tí yóò fi gbóná hùhù (rolling boil) fún ìṣẹ́jú kan ṣáájú kí ẹ tó lò ó. Ẹ jẹ́ kí ó tutù nínú ikòkò kan náà tí ẹ ti sè é, ẹ sì fi ìdérí bo ò. Ẹ má dà á sínú ohun èlò tí kò mọ́.

Tí sísè kò bá ṣeéṣe nítorí iye omi tí a nílò tàbí nítorí epo tàbí igi iná kò tó, ẹ lo chlorine. Ẹ lo àwọn ohun èlò chlorine ilé (omi bleach tàbí tábúlẹ́ẹ̀tì ìmọ́tótó omi tó wà lọ́jà) kí ẹ sì tẹ̀lé ìlànà tó wà lórí àpò rẹ̀. WHO ṣe ìgbaniníyànjú pé omi gbọ́dọ̀ ní nǹkan bíi 2 mg/L free chlorine residual fún omi tó mọ́. Tí omi bá ṣúṣú (cloudy), ẹ kọ́kọ́ ṣẹ̀ ẹ́ nípasẹ̀ aṣọ tó mọ́ tàbí ẹ jẹ́ kí ó jókòó, lẹ́yìn náà ẹ fi iye chlorine tó pọ̀ sí i sínú, nítorí àwọn nǹkan tí ó wà nínú omi ṣúṣú máa ń jẹ chlorine, yóò sì dín bí ó ṣe ń ṣiṣẹ́ kù. Lẹ́yìn tí ẹ bá ti fi chlorine sí, ẹ dúró fún ìṣẹ́jú ọgbọ̀n ṣáájú kí ẹnikẹ́ni tó mu.

Tí sísè àti chlorine kò bá sí, ẹ lè lo ọ̀nà SODIS: ẹ fi omi kún igo ìkékeré oníhà méjì tó mọ́ (PET, kì í ṣe irú tí a kò lè rí inú), ẹ fi sí ibi tí oòrùn ń tàn tààrà fún wákàtí mẹ́fà. Tí àwọsánmà bá bo oòrùn, ẹ fi sílẹ̀ fún ọjọ́ méjì. Ọ̀nà yìí yóò dín kòkòrò àrùn kù dáadáa, ṣùgbọ́n kò pé pátápátá. Kò munadoko sí Cryptosporidium, kò sì ṣe é gbára lé bí sísè tàbí chlorination.

Ẹ fi omi tí ẹ ti ṣe pamọ́ dáadáa. Ẹ fi sínú ohun èlò tó mọ́, tó ní ìdérí, tí ẹnu rẹ̀ kéré. Ẹ má fi ọwọ́, ife, tàbí ohunkóhun bọ̀ sínú omi náà. Ẹ dà á jáde, tàbí ẹ lo ohun èlò tí ó ní tapu.

Ilé Ìgbọ̀nsẹ̀ Àti Ìmọ́tótó

Fífọ ọwọ́ ṣe pàtàkì fún gbogbo ilé, kì í ṣe àwọn tí wọ́n ní aláìsàn nìkan. Gbogbo ènìyàn gbọ́dọ̀ fọ ọwọ́ pẹ̀lú ọṣẹ àti omi lẹ́yìn tí wọ́n bá lo ilé ìgbọ̀nsẹ̀, lẹ́yìn ìfọwọ́kàn pẹ̀lú aláìsàn tàbí ohunkóhun tí ìgbẹ́ tàbí èèbì rẹ̀ ti kàn, ṣáájú sísè oúnjẹ, ṣáájú jíjẹun, àti ṣáájú fífún ọmọ ní oúnjẹ. Tí ọṣẹ kò bá sí, eérú lè ṣe àǹfààní díẹ̀, ṣùgbọ́n ọṣẹ dára jù.

Ṣe ìsọnù ìgbẹ́ àti èèbì aláìsàn ní ọ̀nà tó tọ́. Gbogbo ìgbẹ́ àti èèbì aláìsàn gbọ́dọ̀ wọ inú ilé ìgbọ̀nsẹ̀. Tí aláìsàn kò bá lè dé ilé ìgbọ̀nsẹ̀, ẹ fi garawa tàbí ohun èlò mú u, ẹ fi omi chlorine (0.2% chlorine) sí, ẹ dúró ìṣẹ́jú ọgbọ̀n, lẹ́yìn náà ẹ dà á sínú ilé ìgbọ̀nsẹ̀. Ẹ má dà ìgbẹ́ tí ẹ kò tíì ṣe mọ́tótó sínú gọ́tà, odò, tàbí lórí ilẹ̀ pẹ̀tẹ́lẹ̀. Tí ẹ bá ṣe bẹ́ẹ̀, ẹ ń ṣẹ̀dá ọ̀nà àìmọ́ mìíràn tí ó lè ba àwọn orísun omi mìíràn jẹ́ tàbí tàn àrùn láàárín ènìyàn.

Fọ ibi tí ìgbẹ́ tàbí èèbì ti kàn mọ́. Ẹ fi omi chlorine 0.2% fọ aṣọ ìbùsùn, aṣọ, àti ilẹ̀ tí ìgbẹ́ tàbí èèbì ti kàn. Àwo, ife, àti ṣíbí tí aláìsàn lò, ẹ fọ wọ́n lọ́tọ̀ pẹ̀lú omi mímọ́ àti ọṣẹ tàbí omi chlorine.

Yíyàgbẹ́ sí ìta gbọ́dọ̀ dáwọ́ dúró pátápátá. Tí àwọn ènìyàn kan nínú àdúgbò ṣì ń yàgbẹ́ sí ìta, ìyẹn ti di ewu ńlá fún gbogbo ènìyàn báyìí. Ìgbẹ́ ènìyàn kọ̀ọ̀kan tí ó bá wọ inú àyíká láì ṣe mọ́tótó jẹ́ orísun àìmọ́ tó ṣeéṣe kí ó máa tẹ̀síwájú tàbí kí ó bẹ̀rẹ̀ àìmọ́ tuntun. Ẹ nílò ètò ilé ìgbọ̀nsẹ̀ pàjáwìrì lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀. Tí ilé ìgbọ̀nsẹ̀ tó wà kò bá tó, ẹ lè wa ihò ilé ìgbọ̀nsẹ̀ fún ìgbà díẹ̀, ṣùgbọ́n ẹ yà á sọ́tọ̀ ní ó kéré jù mítà 30 sí orísun omi èyíkéyìí, ẹ sì ri dájú pé ìsàlẹ̀ ihò náà wà ní ó kéré jù mítà 1.5 lókè ìpele omi ilẹ̀ (water table).

Ààbò Oúnjẹ

Ẹ sè oúnjẹ dáadáa kí ẹ sì jẹ ẹ́ nígbà tí ó ṣì gbóná. Ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn kòkòrò àrùn tí ó ń fa ìgbẹ́ gbuuru nípasẹ̀ omi máa ń kú nígbà tí oúnjẹ bá gbóná. Ẹ má jẹ ẹfọ́ tàbí èso tí ẹ kò bá lè bó (peel). Ẹ má jẹ oúnjẹ tí ó ti pẹ́ ní ìwọ̀n oòrùn yàrá, ní pàtàkì nígbà tí ojú ọjọ́ bá gbóná. Ẹ yẹra fún oúnjẹ tí wọ́n ta lójú pópó tàbí oúnjẹ àpéjọ nígbà àjàkálẹ̀ àrùn àyàfi tí ẹ bá mọ̀ pé wọ́n ṣe é dáadáa. Ẹ fọ ibi tí ẹ ń gbé sè oúnjẹ pẹ̀lú omi mímọ́ ṣáájú kí ẹ tó bẹ̀rẹ̀.

Ẹ sọ oúnjẹ tí wọ́n ṣe pẹ̀lú omi tí a fura sí nù. Oúnjẹ èyíkéyìí tí wọ́n fọ, sè, tàbí ṣe pẹ̀lú omi láti orísun tí a fura sí ṣáájú kí a tó mọ̀ pé ó ti di àìmọ́, ẹ sọ ọ́ nù. Èyí pẹ̀lú oúnjẹ tí wọ́n ṣe fún títà tàbí oúnjẹ fún àpéjọ.

Bí A Ṣe Lè Tọ́jú Aláìsàn Ní Ilé

Tí aláìsàn bá ṣì lè mu omi, tí gbígbẹ ara rẹ̀ kò sì lé jù, ẹ lè máa tọ́jú rẹ̀ ní ilé pẹ̀lú ORS nígbà tí ẹ ń retí tàbí láàárín àwọn ìbẹ̀wò ilé ìwòsàn. Ẹni tí ó ń tọ́jú aláìsàn gbọ́dọ̀ yà àwọn ohun èlò (àwo, ife, ṣíbí) àti aṣọ ìbùsùn sọ́tọ̀ fún aláìsàn, fọ ọwọ́ lẹ́yìn ìfọwọ́kàn kọ̀ọ̀kan, kí ó sì ya ohun tí ó ti jáde lára aláìsàn sọ́tọ̀ kí ó sì pa á mọ́.

Ṣùgbọ́n, tí èyíkéyìí nínú àwọn wọ̀nyí bá jẹ́ òótọ́, ẹ gbé aláìsàn lọ sí ilé ìwòsàn lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀:

Aláìsàn ti ṣàfihàn àmì gbígbẹ ara tó burú. Aláìsàn jẹ́ ọmọdé tí kò tíì pé ọdún márùn-ún. Aláìsàn jẹ́ obìnrin tí ó lóyún. Aláìsàn ní àìsàn mìíràn tẹ́lẹ̀.

Tí Ènìyàn Bá Kú

Tí ènìyàn bá kú sí ohun tí wọ́n fura sí pé kọ́lẹ́rà ni, ara oku náà ṣì lè tàn àrùn kálẹ̀. Àwọn tí wọ́n ti gba ìdánilẹ́kọ̀ọ́ ni wọ́n yẹ kí wọ́n múra oku náà sílẹ̀ fún ìsìnkú. Tí àwọn tí wọ́n ti gba ìdánilẹ́kọ̀ọ́ kò bá sí, àwọn tí wọ́n bá ń kó oku gbọ́dọ̀ wọ gílọ́ọ̀fù, dín ìfọwọ́kàn omi ara kù, fi omi chlorine 0.5% wẹ̀ ara oku náà, wọ́n sì gbọ́dọ̀ fọ ọwọ́ wọn dáadáa lẹ́yìn náà. Àpéjọ ìsìnkú ńlá tí gbogbo ènìyàn bá jọ jẹun ti jẹ́ ohun tí ó ti tàn kọ́lẹ́rà kálẹ̀ nínú ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àjàkálẹ̀ àrùn ṣáájú. Ẹ dín iye ènìyàn kù, kí ẹ sì yẹra fún oúnjẹ àpapọ̀ ní ibi ìsìnkú nígbà àjàkálẹ̀ àrùn.

Ohun Tí Àwọn Ẹbí Kò Gbọ́dọ̀ Ṣe

Ẹ má lo oògùn tí ó ń da ìgbẹ́ dúró (bíi loperamide). Irú oògùn bẹ́ẹ̀ máa ń fa ìfun lọ́ra láì kojú àkóràn tó wà nísàlẹ̀. Ó máa ń bò iye omi tí ara ń pàdánù mọ́, ohun sì lè burú sí i, ní pàtàkì fún ọmọdé àti fún àwọn àkóràn tí àwọn ohun alààyè tí ó ń wọ inú (bíi Shigella) ń fà, níbi tí fífa ìfun lọ́ra lè mú kí ara gba májèlé síwájú sí i.

Ẹ má ra oògùn apakòkòrò (antibiotic) láìsí ìtọ́sọ́nà oníṣègùn. Oògùn apakòkòrò ní ipò pàtó nínú àwọn àrùn ìgbẹ́ gbuuru kan (ní pàtàkì kọ́lẹ́rà àti shigellosis), ṣùgbọ́n irú oògùn apakòkòrò wo, ìwọ̀n mélo, àti bóyá a yẹ kí a lò ó rárá dá lórí irú kòkòrò àrùn, àwọn àṣà àtakò (resistance patterns) tó wà ní àgbègbè, àti bí àìsàn ṣe le tó. Lílo oògùn apakòkòrò lọ́nà tí kò tọ́ máa ń yára mú àtakò antimicrobial, ó sì lè ṣe ìpalára tí kòkòrò àrùn bá jẹ́ vaírọ́sì, parasaiti, tàbí irú tí ó ń mú májèlé jáde tí oògùn apakòkòrò kò bá yẹ fún.

Ẹ má fi àbùkù kàn tàbí lé àwọn ìdílé tí wọ́n ní aláìsàn kúrò. Yíyọ àwọn ìdílé tí wọ́n ní àwọn ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ aláìsàn kúrò ní àwùjọ máa ń ti ènìyàn láti fi àìsàn pamọ́, fa fífi ìgbà padà sí wíwá ìtọ́jú, àti dín ìfọwọ́sowọ́pọ̀ pẹ̀lú àwọn aṣojú ìlera kù. Orísun omi tí ó ti di àìmọ́ ni ó fa àrùn náà, kì í ṣe àwọn ìdílé. Ẹ̀bi tí a bá dá fún àwọn ìdílé dípò ewu àyíká kò tọ́ ní ti òótọ́ àti kò sì wúlò ní ti iṣẹ́.

Ẹ má rò pé àjàkálẹ̀ àrùn ti parí nítorí àwọn ẹ̀ṣọ̀ tuntun ti dín kù. Àkókò tí àwọn kòkòrò àrùn oríṣiríṣi ń gbé lára ṣáájú kí àmì àìsàn tó hàn yàtọ̀: kọ́lẹ́rà àti E. coli tí ó ń mú májèlé jáde lè hàn láàárín wákàtí díẹ̀, ṣùgbọ́n Cryptosporidium àti hepatitis A lè gbé ọjọ́ tàbí ọ̀sẹ̀. Àwọn ẹ̀ṣọ̀ àìsàn lè ṣì ń fara hàn kódà lẹ́yìn tí a ti kojú orísun náà, láti ọ̀dọ̀ àwọn ènìyàn tí wọ́n mu omi náà ṣáájú ìgbésẹ̀. Ẹ máa tẹ̀síwájú ṣíṣe omi, ìṣọ́, àti mímú ìmọ́tótó pọ̀ sí i títí tí àwọn aṣojú ìlera yóò fi fi ẹ̀rí hàn pé àjàkálẹ̀ àrùn ti wà lábẹ́ ìṣàkóso.

Ibi Tí Ìmọ̀ràn Yìí Ti Wá

Ìmọ̀ràn yìí dá lórí àwọn ìtọ́sọ́nà WHO lórí dídára omi mímu (àtẹ̀jáde kẹrin àti àwọn ìmúdójúìwọ̀n tó tẹ̀lé e), àwọn ìwé àlàyé WHO lórí kọ́lẹ́rà àti àrùn ìgbẹ́ gbuuru ní kíákíá àti àwọn ìtọ́sọ́nà ìdáhùn àjàkálẹ̀ àrùn, àwọn ìgbaniníyànjú WHO/UNICEF lórí ìṣe omi mímọ́ nínú ilé àti ìpamọ́ àìléwu, ìtọ́sọ́nà WHO/UNICEF lórí ìtọ́jú ìfomi-padà-sí-ara, àwọn ìlànà ìdáhùn àjàkálẹ̀ àrùn omi CDC, àti àwọn ìtọ́sọ́nà WHO lórí ìmọ́tótó àti ìlera. Ìlànà ORS (omi ṣúgà-iyọ̀) tẹ̀lé àwọn pàtó ìfomi-padà-sí-ara pàjáwìrì ti WHO. Ìwọ̀n chlorine (0.2% fún ìgbẹ́ àti ṣíṣe ilẹ̀ mọ́tótó, nǹkan bíi 2 mg/L free chlorine residual fún omi mímu, 0.5% fún oku) tẹ̀lé ìtọ́sọ́nà ìlera àyíká ní àsìkò pàjáwìrì ti WHO. Ìfiwéra ìwọ̀n ikú (ju ìdajì lọ láìsí ìtọ́jú, ṣùgbọ́n kéré ju 1% pẹ̀lú ìtọ́jú) wá láti inú àkójọ àwọn ìṣirò àbójútó kọ́lẹ́rà àgbáyé WHO. Ìjìnnà tó kéré jù fún ilé ìgbọ̀nsẹ̀ sí orísun omi (mítà 30) àti ìjìnnà tó kéré jù lókè ìpele omi ilẹ̀ (mítà 1.5) tẹ̀lé àwọn ìlànà ìmọ́tótó pàjáwìrì ti WHO/UNICEF.

Àwọn ìdílé yẹ kí wọ́n tẹ̀lé àwọn ìlànà láti ọ̀dọ̀ àjọ ìlera orílẹ̀-èdè tàbí àdúgbò wọn, nítorí àwọn ìlànà ìdáhùn àjàkálẹ̀ àrùn pàtó lè yàtọ̀ gẹ́gẹ́ bí orílẹ̀-èdè, irú kòkòrò àrùn, àti ohun àmúṣe àdúgbò, wọ́n sì lè jẹ́ ìmúdójúìwọ̀n bí ipò bá ń yí padà.

Ti ọpọlọpọ eniyan ba bẹrẹ si ni igbe gbuuru pupọ ati eebi, o ṣe pataki ki ẹbi gbe igbese lati dinku ewu itankale arun ati lati dabobo ilera wọn.

Ohun ti ẹbi le ṣe
Fọ ọwọ nigbagbogbo pẹlu ọṣẹ ati omi, paapaa lẹyin lilo ile igbọnsẹ ati ki wọn to jẹun tabi se ounjẹ.
Mu omi mimọ. Ti ailewu omi ba n ṣeyemeji, se omi naa tabi lo ọna miiran lati sọ ọ di mimọ.
Jẹ ounjẹ ti a se daradara ki o si bo ounjẹ lati dena idoti.
Lo ile igbọnsẹ to mọ, ki o si sọ egbin di mimọ ni ọna to yẹ.
Yago fun pinpin awọn ohun elo ti ara ẹni, bii ago ati sibi, pẹlu ẹni ti o n ṣaisan.
Fun ẹni ti o n ṣaisan ni omi pupọ tabi omi amu-ara-pada (oral rehydration solution, ORS) lati dena gbigbẹ ara.
Wa iranlọwọ ilera ni kiakia fun ẹnikẹni ti o ni igbe gbuuru pupọ, eebi pupọ, tabi awọn ami gbigbẹ ara bii ẹnu gbigbẹ, ailera pupọ, tabi ito ti o dinku.

Gbigbẹ ara pupọ
Ẹjẹ ninu igbe
Ko le mu omi duro nitori eebi
Ailera pupọ tabi aiji
Awọn ọmọde kekere, awọn agbalagba, tabi awọn ẹni ti ilera wọn tẹlẹ ko pe

Awọn iṣe wọnyi le ṣe iranlọwọ lati dinku itankale arun igbe gbuuru ati lati daabobo awọn ọmọ ẹgbẹ ẹbi ati agbegbe.

Ti ẹnì kan bá ń fi àwọn àmì àìsàn Ebola hàn, àwọn ará adúgbò yẹ kí wọ́n ṣe àwọn nǹkan wọ̀nyí lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀:

Pe àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ ìlera tàbí iṣẹ́ pajawiri tó yẹ kí wọ́n lè ṣe àyẹ̀wò ẹni náà kíákíá.
Yàgò fún fífi ọwọ́ kan ẹ̀jẹ̀, ẹ̀gbin ara, eebi, ito, tàbí àwọn omi ara míì láti ọdọ ẹni náà.
Ran ẹni náà lọ́wọ́ láti gba ìtọju ìlera ní kíákíá ní ọ̀nà tó dáàbò bo gbogbo ènìyàn.
Fọ ọwọ́ dáadáa pẹ̀lú ọṣẹ àti omi lẹ́yìn ìfarakanra kankan pẹ̀lú ẹni náà tàbí àyíká rẹ̀.
Má ṣe pín àwọn ohun èlò ara ẹni, bíi ago, ṣíbí, aṣọ, tàbí ibùsùn, pẹ̀lú ẹni tí ó ń ṣàìsàn.
Tẹ̀lé gbogbo ìtọ́nisọ́nà àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ ìlera àti àwọn aláṣẹ ìlera.

Àwọn àmì àìsàn Ebola lè ní:

Ibà
Àìlókun púpọ̀
Orífífó
Ìrora iṣan ara
Eebi
Ìgbẹ́ gbuuru
Ní àwọn ọ̀ràn kan, ẹ̀jẹ̀ jíjádè

Ó ṣe pàtàkì kí adúgbò náà má ṣe tan àròsọ tàbí fi ẹni náà sílẹ̀ nítorí ìbẹ̀rù, ṣùgbọ́n kí wọ́n wá ìrànlọ́wọ́ ìlera kíákíá, kí wọ́n sì tẹ̀lé ìmòràn àwọn amòye ìlera.

Bí ọ̀pọ̀ ènìyàn bá ń ní ìgbẹ́ gbuuru àti eebi, ó ṣe pàtàkì kí ìdílé gba àwọn ìgbésẹ̀ láti dènà ìtànkálẹ̀ àrùn àti láti dáàbò bo ara wọn.

Ohun tí ìdílé lè ṣe
Fọ ọwọ́ déédéé pẹ̀lú ọṣẹ àti omi mímọ́, pàápàá lẹ́yìn lílo ilé ìgbọ̀nsẹ, kí wọ́n tó jẹun, àti kí wọ́n tó pèsè oúnjẹ.
Máa mu omi tó mọ́, bí omi tí a ti sè dáadáa, omi tí a ti tọ́jú, tàbí omi tó dájú pé ó mọ́.
Jẹ oúnjẹ tí a sè dáadáa kí o sì bo oúnjẹ mọ́ kúrò lọ́wọ́ ẹyẹ àti fó.
Lo ilé ìgbọ̀nsẹ dáadáa, kí o sì yẹra fún fífi ìdọ̀tí sí ibi gbogbo.
Má ṣe pín ohun èlò jíjẹ, ife, tàbí aṣọ ìnura pẹ̀lú ẹni tó ń ṣàìsàn, bí ó bá ṣeé ṣe.
Nu àwọn ibi tí eebi tàbí ìgbẹ́ ti kan dáadáa pẹ̀lú ọṣẹ àti omi tàbí ohun èlò ìmótótó tó yẹ.
Tí ẹnikẹ́ni bá ń ṣàìsàn
Máa fún un ní omi púpọ̀ láti dènà gbígbẹ ara (dehydration).
Tí ORS (Oral Rehydration Solution) bá wà, ó lè ràn án lọ́wọ́ láti rọ́pò omi àti àsíà tó ń pàdánù.
Wá ìtọ́jú ìlera kíákíá bí ẹni náà bá ní ààmì gbígbẹ ara, ìrẹ̀wẹ̀sì púpọ̀, tàbí bí ìgbẹ́ gbuuru àti eebi ṣe ń le sí i.

Tí ọ̀pọ̀ ènìyàn bá ń ní àwọn àmì àìsàn wọ̀nyí ní agbègbè kan, ó yẹ kí a jẹ́ kí àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ ìlera mọ̀ ní kíákíá kí wọ́n lè ṣe àyẹ̀wò ohun tó ń ṣẹlẹ̀ àti láti dènà ìtànkálẹ̀ àrùn sí i.

Nke a nwere ike ịbụ ntiwapụ ọrịa kọlera. Ndị ezinụlọ kwesịrị ịgwa ụlọọgwụ, ndị ọrụ ahụike ọha ma ọ bụ ndị otu na-ahụ maka ọrịa mberede ozugbo. Echela nsonaazụ nyocha ụlọọgwụ tupu ịmalite inye mmiri ọgwụ na ime ihe ga-egbochi mgbasa ọrịa.

Maka onye ọ bụla nwere afọ ọsịsa mmiri mmiri ma ọ bụ na-agbọ agbọ:

Malite inye ya oral rehydration solution, ORS, ozugbo. Gaa n’ihu inye ya ka a na-ebuga ya ebe ahụike.
Gwakọta ORS dị n’akpa dịka ntụziaka dị n’akpa ahụ si dị.
Ọ bụrụ na ORS adịghị, gwakọta otu lita mmiri dị ọcha, ngaji tii shuga isii juru larịị na ọkara ngaji tii nnu juru larịị. Tụọ ha nke ọma, n’ihi na oke nnu nwere ike ịdị ize ndụ.
Na-enye ya obere mmiri ahụ ugboro ugboro, ọkachasị mgbe ọ bụla ọ gara afọ. Nne kwesịrị ịga n’ihu inye nwa ara.
Kpọga onye ahụ ebe ahụike ngwa ngwa. Mmiri ịkọ n’ahụ nwere ike ịkpata ọnwụ n’ime awa ole na ole, onye ahụ nwekwara ike ịchọ mmiri a na-etinye n’akwara.
Enyela ya antibiotics ma ọ bụ ọgwụ na-akwụsị afọ ọsịsa, belụsọ ma onye ọrụ ahụike ruru eru nyere iwu.

Chọọ enyemaka mberede ozugbo ma ọ bụrụ na onye ahụ:

Akpịrị na-akpọ ya nkụ nke ukwuu
Adịghị ike, na-arahụ ụra nke ukwuu ma ọ bụ na-agbagwoju anya
Enweghị ike ịṅụ mmiri
Na-agbọ mmiri ọ bụla ọ ṅụrụ
Anya ya bara n’ime
Na-amịrị obere mamịrị ma ọ bụ na ọ naghị amịrị mamịrị
Daa ma ọ bụ tụfuo onwe ya

Iji gbochie mgbasa ọrịa:

Jiri naanị mmiri karama mechiri emechi, mmiri e siri nke ọma, ma ọ bụ mmiri e mere ka ọ dị ọcha maka ịṅụ, isi nri na ịsa ezé.

Sie nri nke ọma ma rie ya mgbe ọ ka na-ekpo ọkụ. Jiri mmiri dị ọcha saa mkpụrụ osisi na akwụkwọ nri.

Jiri ncha na mmiri dị ọcha saa aka mgbe ị gachara ụlọ mposi, mgbe ihichachara onye ọrịa ma ọ bụ ihe ruru unyi, nakwa tupu isi nri, iri nri ma ọ bụ inye nwa nri.
Jiri ụlọ mposi ma ọ bụ latrine. Kpofu nsị ụmụaka n’ụzọ kwesịrị ekwesị. Ekwela ka nsị na agbọ rute olulu mmiri, iyi ma ọ bụ ebe a na-esi nri.
Jiri disinfectant ndị ọrụ ahụike kwadoro hichaa ụlọ mposi, ala, uwe na akwa ụra nsị ma ọ bụ agbọ metụrụ.
Sie nri nke ọma ma rie ya mgbe ọ ka na-ekpo ọkụ. Jiri mmiri dị ọcha saa mkpụrụ osisi na akwụkwọ nri.
Onye nwere afọ ọsịsa ekwesịghị isi nri nye ndị ọzọ ruo mgbe onye ọrụ ahụike kwuru na ọ dị mma.
Soro ndị ọrụ ahụike rụkọọ ọrụ n’ịkọ ndị ọrịa, inyocha mmiri, ime ka gburugburu dị ọcha na mmemme ọgwụ mgbochi kọlera ọ bụla.
Ekwula okwu ọjọọ ma ọ bụ kewapụ ezinụlọ ndị ọrịa. Kọlera na-agbasakarị site na nri ma ọ bụ mmiri nsị onye bu ọrịa metọrọ.

Ihe Ndị Ezinụlọ Kwesịrị Ime Mgbe Ọrịa Kọlera na-Ebubata
Ihe Mbụ: Mezie Onwe Gị Nʻụzọ Zuru Okè

Mmiri Ọcha

Ṅụ mmiri a kụziiri ọkụ (boiled water) tupu ị ṅụ ya
Ị nwekwara ike iji mmiri chlorinated ma ọ bụ mmiri a tinye chlorine (bleach) obere oge
Kọ mmiri ọcha na efere ma mee ka ọ dị ọcha

Aka na Elu Ahụ

Saa aka gị na mmiri ọcha at sepu kwa ụbọchị, naanụ́ mgbe ị gụrụ, mgbe ị jiri aka azụ́ okwu, na mgbe ị siri nri
Emejị ọnụ gị na sepu kwa ụbọchị

Nri

Rie nri a kụziiri ọkụ nke mma
Kii se ire nri a tụkọchiteghị nʻọkụ ma ọ bụ nri tupu ọ jụsiri oge
Jiri ngaji ọcha iji ṅara nri
Mgbochie: Ihe Ndị Ụzọ Mma

Ebe Ịgba Ụdị (Toilet/Latrine)

Mee ka onye ọ bụla nʻụlọ yị lọ́ na toilet ma ọ bụ latrine - kii se eyi ebe ọ bụla
Ụdị mmadụ kwesịrị ịbanye naanụ́ na ebe a
Emejị ụdị, saa aka gị na mmiri ọcha at sepu

Ebe Mmiri Ọcha

Dụọ mmiri ọcha site naanụ́ ebe zuru okè
Kii se ebe mmiri e na-azụ́ ihe, ebe ụdị mmadụ na-aba, ma ọ bụ ebe a na-atapu ụdị
Kii se ebe mmiri e na-acha mma ma ọ bụ ihe mma
Mgbe Otu Mmadụ Rịara Afọ ma Ọ Bụ Agbọ

Tu Onye Ahụ Isii

Tunye onye a na otu ụlọ kacha anya site na ndị ọzọ
Kii se ụlọ yị dabere nʻọdụ mmiri ma ọ bụ ịdị nʻakụkụ ndị ezinụlọ ọzọ

Ọgwụ Mmiri (Oral Rehydration Solution - ORS)

Mee ORS: ṅụ ụnụ salt (½ tsp) + suga (6 teaspoon) + mmiri ọcha (1 lita)
Nyere onye ahụ ọgwụ mmiri a ụbọchị, nʻusoro dị ntakịrị-ntakịrị
Ọ bụ ihe kacha mkpa - onye a aghaghị ịnwụ site naʻọrịa a ma ọ bụ naanụ́ na-enwe mmiri

Ziri ụkọ Oniṣẹgun

Zi ụkọ oniṣẹgun ma ọ bụ ụkọ ụlọ-ọgwụ oge a - kii se ihewa
Ọrịa kọlera pụrụ ịkpa ọnwụ ma ejiri ụkọ mma na oge

Ihe Ndị Iji Ụdị

Mee ka onye a lọ́ gị naanụ́ na éje ya na ụlọ
Jiri efere pụtara ụdị mmadụ ma tinye ụgbọ ma ọ bụ chlorine
Saa aka ihe ndị a na mmiri ọcha at sepu
Ihe Ndị Mgbaàmụ (Prevention for Others)
Saa aka naanụ́ mgbe a kwụrụ, tupu ire nri, na mgbe ị siri nri
Kii se ire nri ma ọ bụ mmiri ndị ọzọ nyere
Mee ka ụlọ gị zụlite na mmiri ọcha
Ghazie ụdị ma ọ bụ ihe e ji azụ́ ya naanụ́ nʻahalị dị anya

Ọ bụ ihe kacha mkpa: ọrịa kọlera bụ ihe dị ngọngọ mma, mana ka a na-agwọ ya nke mma ma ọ bụ a na-emedo ọgwụ mmiri na oge ziri ụkọ.

Gịnị Ka Ezinụlọ Kwesịrị Ime Ma Ọ Bụrụ Na Ọtụtụ Ndị Mmadụ N'Otu Ama Amalite Ịrịa Afọ Ọsịsa Mmiri Mmiri Na Ịgbọ Agbọ, A Na-Enwe Enyo Na Ọ Bụ Kọlera
Otu Esi Amata Na Okwu A Dị Njọ

Mgbe ọtụtụ ndị mmadụ nọ n'otu ama amalitere ịrịa afọ ọsịsa mmiri mmiri na ịgbọ agbọ n'otu oge, nke a bụ ihe ịrịbama dị oke egwu. Kọlera (nke nje bacteria a na-akpọ Vibrio cholerae na-akpata) na-eme ka mmadụ na-agbapụ mmiri n'ahụ site n'afọ ọsịsa. Afọ ọsịsa ahụ na-adị ka mmiri ọsọ osikapa, ọ naghị eme ka afọ na-arụ ụkwụ, mana mmiri na-apụ n'ahụ dị oke egwu. Onye ọrịa lere n'anya nwere ike ịtụfu otutu lita mmiri n'ime elekere ole na ole. Ịkpọnwụ ahụ (dehydration) bụ ihe na-egbu ndị mmadụ, ọ nwekwara ike igbu mmadụ n'ime elekere ole na ole ma onye ahụ ahụghị nọọsụ. Mana ọrịa ndị ọzọ nwere ike ịdị ka kọlera, ya mere ọ bụ naanị nyocha ụlọ nyocha (lab test) ga-egosi n'ezie ihe na-eme.

Ihe Mbụ: Ekwela Ka Ahụ Mmadụ Kpọọ Nkụ

Ịkpọnwụ ahụ bụ ihe na-egbu ndị mmadụ karịsịa na kọlera. Mmadụ anaghị anwụ n'ihi nje bacteria n'onwe ya, kama n'ihi na ahụ atụfuola mmiri na nnu karịrị akarị. Ya mere, ihe mbụ ndị ezinụlọ kwesịrị ime bụ ịmalite inye onye ọrịa mmiri na nnu ọzọ n'ahụ ozugbo, tupu ha eruo ụlọ ọgwụ.

Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) bụ ihe kacha dị mkpa. Ọ bụrụ na ORS sachet dị, jikọtara ya na mmiri dị ọcha dịka e si dee n'elu akpa ahụ. Ọ bụrụ na ORS adịghị, ị nwere ike ịkwado nke oge nwa oge n'ụlọ: tinye spoon nta isii (6) nke shuga e juru eju na ọkara spoon nta nnu (ịdajị spoon nta) n'ime otu lita mmiri dị ọcha (mmiri ị sịịrị maọbụ jiri chlorine mee). Nke a bụ maka oge mberede, ọ bụghị ihe ga-anọchi anya ORS nke ọma. Na-enye onye ọrịa obere obere, mana na-enye ya mgbe niile, akwụsịla. Nwoke maọbụ nwanyị nke ahụ ya kpọnwụsịrị ike nwere ike ịchọ ọtụtụ lita n'ime elekere mbụ ole na ole. Maka nwa nta ka na-aṅụ ara, ga n'ihu na-enye ya ara tinyekwara ORS.

Na-ahụ maka ihe ịrịbama ndị a nke gosiri na ịkpọnwụ ahụ akarịala: anya abanyelarị n'ime, ọ bụrụ na ị kpụọ akpụkpọ ahụ n'azụ aka ọ naghị alọta azụ ngwa ngwa, obi na-akụ ọsọ mana ike adịghị, mmadụ na-arahụ ụra ebe ọbụla maọbụ enweghị ike ịza, enweghịkwa ike ịṅụ mmiri ọzọ, ọ naghị anyụ mamịrị maọbụ mamịrị ya na-agba ọchịchịrị nke ukwu. Ọ bụrụ na ị hụ nke ọbụla n'ime ihe ndị a, buru onye ọrịa gaa ụlọ ọgwụ ozugbo, n'ihi na ha ga-achọ mmiri drip (IV fluid). Nke a bụ mberede.

Kpọọ Ndị Ọrụ Ahụike Ozugbo

Echere eche nsonaazụ nyocha ụlọ nyocha tupu ị kọọ. Ọ bụrụ na ọtụtụ ndị mmadụ n'otu ebe amalitere ịrịa afọ ọsịsa na ịgbọ agbọ n'otu oge, nke ahụ eruola ebe ị kwesịrị ikwu okwu. Kpọọ ụlọ ọgwụ kacha nso, ngalaba ahụike gọọmenti obodo, maọbụ onye nlekọta ọrịa na-efe efe (disease surveillance officer). Gwa ha ọnụ ọgụgụ ndị nrịa nrịa, ebe ha nọ, oge ọrịa ahụ bidoro, na ma enwere ihe ha niile yiri ka ha kerịtara oke, dịka otu olulu mmiri, otu isi mmiri, otu nri, maọbụ otu nnọkọ.

Ọ bụrụ na ị kọọ ngwa ngwa, ndị ọrụ ahụike ga-enwe ike ịbịa nyochaa mmiri, gosi ọrịa ahụ n'ụzọ ziri ezi, weta ORS na mmiri drip, wee malite nzaghachi kwesịrị ekwesị.

Chekwaa Mmiri Unu

Kọlera na-agbasa karịsịa site na mmiri na nri nke nsị mmadụ nwere ọrịa banyere n'ime. Isi mmiri nke onye ọbụla na-eji nke rụrụ arụ bụ ihe na-akpata ọrịa kọlera karịsịa n'oge ọrịa na-ebili.

Hazie mmiri niile unu chọrọ ịṅụ. Sienụ mmiri ka ọ gbọọ ụfụfụ nke ọma opekata mpe nkeji otu tupu unu eji ya eme ihe. Ọ bụrụ na unu enweghị ike isi, jiri chlorine, dịka mmiri bleach maọbụ tabuleti nke ịme mmiri ka ọ dị ọcha nke dị n'ahịa, sorokwa ntụzịaka dị n'elu akpa ya. Ọ bụrụ na unu enweghị chlorine ma unu enweghịkwa ike isi mmiri, unu nwere ike ịnwale ụzọ SODIS: kujuo karama plastik nke doro anya mmiri, debe ya ebe anwụ na-amụkwasị kpọm kpọm opekata mpe elekere isii (6). Nke a ezughịghị okè, mana ọ ga-ebelata ihe egwu.

Chekwaa mmiri unu hazicharịrị nke ọma. Tinye ya n'ime ihe dị ọcha, nke nwere mkpuchi, nke ọnụ ya dị nta. Etinyela aka maọbụ iko n'ime mmiri ahụ. Wụpụta ya, maọbụ jiri ihe nwere tapu.

Kwụsị iji isi mmiri ahụ unu na-enyo enyo maka ịṅụ, isi nri, ịsa nri, maọbụ ịsa eze ruo mgbe ndị ọrụ ahụike ga-abịa nyochaa ya ma kwuo na ọ dị mma, maọbụ ruo mgbe unu nwetara mmiri ọzọ dị ọcha.

Ụlọ Mposi Na Ịdị Ọcha

Ịsa aka abụghị nhọrọ, ọ bụ ihe a ga-eme. Onye ọbụla nọ n'ụlọ ga-asa aka ya na ncha na mmiri mgbe ha si n'ụlọ mposi, mgbe ha metụrụ onye ọrịa maọbụ ihe ọbụla nsị maọbụ agbọ ọsịsa ya metụrụ aka, tupu ha esie nri, tupu ha erie nri, na tupu ha enye nwa nri. Ọ bụrụ na ncha adịghị, ntụ nwere ike inyere aka nwa ntakịrị, mana ncha ka mma.

Wepụ nsị na agbọ ọsịsa n'ụzọ ziri ezi. Nsị na agbọ ọsịsa niile sitere n'onye ọrịa ga-abanye n'ụlọ mposi. Ọ bụrụ na onye ọrịa enweghị ike iru ụlọ mposi, jiri ịkwọ maọbụ ihe ọzọ nara ya, tinye mmiri chlorine (0.2% chlorine), chere nkeji iri atọ (30), wee wụpụ ya n'ụlọ mposi. Ewụpụla nsị a na-emechabeghị n'ime ọhịa, iyi, mmiri, maọbụ n'elu ala.

Sachapụ ebe ọbụla nsị maọbụ agbọ ọsịsa metụrụ. Jiri mmiri chlorine 0.2% saa akwa ndina, uwe, na ala nke nsị maọbụ agbọ ọsịsa metụrụ. Efere, iko, na ngaji nke onye ọrịa jiri, sapụ ha iche site n'iji mmiri e mere ka ọ dị ọcha na ncha maọbụ chlorine.

Ịnya nsị n'èzí ga-akwụsị kpamkpam. Ọ bụrụ na ụfọdụ ndị nọ n'ama ka na-anya nsị n'èzí, nke ahụ aghọọla ihe ize ndụ dị oke njọ maka onye ọbụla ugbu a. A chọrọ ụlọ mposi nke mberede ozugbo.

Nchekwa Nri

Sienụ nri nke ọma, riekwanụ ya mgbe ọ ka na-ekpo ọkụ. Nje bacteria kọlera na-anwụ mgbe nri na-ekpo ọkụ. Erila akwụkwọ nri maọbụ mkpụrụ osisi na-adịghị ehi ehi ma ọ bụghị nke ị nwere ike ịkpụchapụ akpụkpọ ya. Erila nri nke nọọla oge n'ọnọdụ okpomọkụ ụlọ, karịsịa mgbe ihu igwe na-ekpo ọkụ. Zere nri ndị a na-ere n'okporo ụzọ maọbụ nri nnọkọ n'oge ọrịa a na-ebili, ma ọ bụghị na ị mara na e siri ya nke ọma.

Sachapụ ebe ị na-akwadebe nri na mmiri dị ọcha tupu ị malite.

Otu Esi Elekọta Onye Ọrịa N'ụlọ

Ọ bụrụ na onye ọrịa ka nwere ike ịṅụ mmiri ma ịkpọnwụ ahụ ya adịghịkwa njọ, ị nwere ike ịnọ n'ụlọ na-elekọta ya na ORS mgbe ị na-eche maọbụ n'etiti oge ị na-aga ụlọ ọgwụ. Onye na-elekọta onye ọrịa kwesịrị ịhapụ efere, iko, ngaji, na akwa ndina iche maka onye ọrịa, saa aka nke ọma mgbe ọbụla ha metụrụ onye ọrịa aka, wee debe ihe si n'ahụ onye ọrịa pụta iche ma sachapụ ya.

Mana, ọ bụrụ na nke ọbụla n'ime ihe ndị a metụtara onye ọrịa, buru ya gaa ụlọ ọgwụ ozugbo:

Onye ọrịa agosịla ihe ịrịbama nke ịkpọnwụ ahụ dị njọ. Onye ọrịa bụ nwa nta nke na-erughị afọ ise. Onye ọrịa bụ nwanyị dị ime. Onye ọrịa nwere ọrịa ọzọ n'ahụ ya mbụ.

Kọlera nwere ike igbu karịa ọkara ndị na-enwetaraghị ọgwụgwọ, mana site na ọgwụgwọ ịtinye mmiri ọzọ n'ahụ nke ọma, ọnwụ nwere ike ịda ruo ihe dịka otu n'ime narị (1%). Ya mere, iru ụlọ ọgwụ bụ ihe dị iche n'etiti ndụ na ọnwụ.

Ọ Bụrụ Na Mmadụ Anwụọ

Ọ bụrụ na mmadụ anwụọ n'ihe a na-enyo enyo na ọ bụ kọlera, ozu ahụ ka nwere ike ịkesa ọrịa. Ndị e zụrụ azụ kwesịrị ịkwado ozu ahụ maka olili ozu. Ọ bụrụ na ndị e zụrụ azụ adịghị, ndị ga-ejide ozu ahụ kwesịrị iyi gloovu, belata otu ha si emetụ mmiri ahụ onye nwụrụ anwụ aka, jiri mmiri chlorine 0.5% sachaa ahụ ozu ahụ, wee saa aka ha nke ọma mgbe ha mechara. Nnọkọ olili ozu nke dị ukwu ebe ndị mmadụ niile nọ na-eri nri ọnụ abụrụla ihe na-eme ka kọlera gbasaa n'ọtụtụ oge ọrịa ebiliri n'oge gara aga. Belatanụ ọnụ ọgụgụ ndị mmadụ, zerekwanụ nri ọha n'ebe olili ozu.

Ihe Ezinụlọ Ekwesịghị Ime

Ejila ọgwụ na-akwụsị afọ ọsịsa (dịka loperamide). Ụdị ọgwụ a na-eme ka afọ daa jụụ mana ọ naghị egbu nje bacteria. Ọ ga-ezo otu mmiri si efu n'ahụ, ihe ga-adịkwa njọ karịa.

Ejela gaa zụta ọgwụ antibiotic n'ahịa n'onwe unu. Ọgwụ antibiotic nwere ọrụ ya na kọlera dị njọ, mana ọ bụ naanị ndị ọrụ ahụike kwesịrị ikpebi nke ha na oge ole. Antibiotic adịghị anọchi anya ịtinye mmiri ọzọ n'ahụ, ọ bụrụkwa na ndị mmadụ na-eji antibiotic eme ihe n'ụzọ na-ezighị ezi, nje bacteria ahụ ga-amụta otu esi eguzogide ya.

Achụpụla maọbụ enye ndị ezinụlọ nwere ndị nrịa nrịa ihere. Ọ bụrụ na ndị mmadụ amalite ịzere maọbụ isi mee ka ndị ezinụlọ nwere kọlera nwee ihere, ndị ezinụlọ ndị ahụ ga-atụ egwu ikwu okwu maọbụ ịga ụlọ ọgwụ, ọtụtụ ndị mmadụ ga-anwụkwa karịa. Ihe a emehụrụla n'ọtụtụ oge ọrịa kọlera ebiliri n'oge gara aga.

Ebe Ndụmọdụ A Si Pụta

Ndụmọdụ a dabere na akwụkwọ ozi WHO (World Health Organization) banyere kọlera na usoro nzaghachi maka ọrịa na-efe efe, ntụzịaka WHO/UNICEF maka ọgwụgwọ ịtinye mmiri ọzọ n'ahụ site n'ọnụ (oral rehydration therapy), ntụzịaka WHO maka ịme mmiri ka ọ dị ọcha n'ụlọ na ịchekwa ya n'ụzọ dị mma, yana usoro CDC (U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention) maka ịgbochi na ịchịkwa kọlera. Oke chlorine maka ihe dị iche iche (0.2% maka nsị na ala, 0.5% maka ozu) na-eso iwu WHO maka ahụike gburugburu ebe obibi n'oge mberede. Ntụnyere ọnwụ (karịa ọkara ma enweghị ọgwụgwọ, mana erughị 1% ma enwere ọgwụgwọ) si na data nlekọta kọlera nke ụwa niile nke WHO.

Soronụ ihe ndị ọrụ ahụike obodo unu maọbụ nke mba kwuru, n'ihi na ụzọ e si eji akwụsị ọrịa na-efe efe nwere ike ịdị iche site na mba ruo mba, nwekwara ike ịgbanwe ka ọnọdụ ahụ si agbanwe.

Gịnị Ka Ndị Ezinụlọ Kwesịrị Ime Mgbe Ọtụtụ Ndị Mmadụ N'Otu Ama Amalitere Ịrịa Afọ Ọsịsa Mmiri Mmiri Nke Ukwu Na Ịgbọ Agbọ, A Na-Enwe Enyo Na Ọ Bụ Kọlera
Otu Esi Amata Na Okwu A Dị Njọ

Mgbe ọtụtụ ndị mmadụ nọ n'otu ama amalitere ịrịa afọ ọsịsa mmiri mmiri dị njọ na ịgbọ agbọ n'otu oge, nke a bụ ihe ịrịbama dị oke egwu nke na-egosi na ọrịa na-efe efe na-amalite, ọ nwekwara ike ịbụ na o si n'otu isi ihe, dịka mmiri ndị mmadụ niile na-eji maọbụ nri. Kọlera (nke nje bacteria a na-akpọ Vibrio cholerae na-akpata) na-eme ka mmadụ na-agbapụ mmiri n'ahụ site n'afọ ọsịsa. Afọ ọsịsa ahụ na-adị ka mmiri ọsọ osikapa, ọ naghị eme ka afọ na-arụ ụkwụ, mana mmiri na-apụ n'ahụ dị oke egwu. Onye ọrịa lere n'anya nwere ike ịtụfu ọtụtụ lita mmiri n'ime elekere ole na ole. Ịkpọnwụ ahụ (dehydration) bụ ihe na-egbu ndị mmadụ, ọ nwekwara ike igbu mmadụ n'ime elekere ole na ole ma onye ahụ ahụghị nọọsụ. Mana ọrịa ndị ọzọ nwere ike ịdị ka kọlera, dịka rotavirus, norovirus, E. coli na-emepụta nsị, Shigella, na Cryptosporidium. Ọ bụ naanị nyocha ụlọ nyocha (lab test) ga-egosi n'ezie ihe na-akpata ya. Mana nzaghachi ozugbo nke obodo kwesịrị ime bụ otu ihe ahụ n'agbanyeghị ụdị nje: gbochie ọnwụ site n'ịkpọnwụ ahụ, kpọọ ndị ọrụ ahụike, chekwaa isi mmiri, wee gbochie ọrịa ahụ ịga n'ihu na-agbasa.

Ihe Mbụ: Ekwela Ka Mmadụ Nwụọ N'ihi Ịkpọnwụ Ahụ

Ịkpọnwụ ahụ bụ ihe na-egbu ndị mmadụ na kọlera na ọrịa afọ ọsịsa mmiri mmiri ndị ọzọ, ọ bụghị nje bacteria n'onwe ya. Ọnwụ nwere ike ịme n'ime elekere ole na ole mgbe mgbaàmà bidoro, karịsịa n'ụmụaka, ndị okenye, ndị inyom dị ime, na ndị nwere ọrịa ọzọ n'ahụ ha na mbụ. Ịtinye mmiri ọzọ n'ahụ kwesịrị ịmalite n'ụlọ ozugbo, tupu onye ọrịa eruo ụlọ ọgwụ.

Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) bụ ihe kacha dị mkpa. Ọ bụrụ na ORS sachet dị, jikọtara ya na mmiri dị ọcha nke a sịịrị maọbụ jiri chlorine mee dịka e si dee n'elu akpa ahụ. Ọ bụrụ na ORS sachet adịghị, ị nwere ike ịkwado nke oge nwa oge n'ụlọ: tinye spoon nta isii (6) nke shuga e juru eju na ọkara spoon nta nnu n'ime otu lita mmiri dị ọcha (mmiri ị sịịrị maọbụ jiri chlorine mee). Nke a bụ maka oge mberede naanị, ọ bụghị ihe ga-anọchi anya ORS nke kwesịrị ekwesị. Na-enye onye ọrịa obere obere, mana na-enye ya mgbe niile, akwụsịla. Echerekwala ka onye ọrịa sị na akpịrị na-akpọ ya nkụ, n'ihi na mgbe ịkpọnwụ ahụ adịla njọ, mmadụ anaghịzi enwe mmetụta nke akpịrị ịkpọ nkụ. Nwoke maọbụ nwanyị nke ahụ ya kpọnwụsịrị ike nwere ike ịchọ ọtụtụ lita n'ime elekere mbụ ole na ole.

Maka nwa nta ka na-aṅụ ara, ga n'ihu na-enye ya ara tinyekwara ORS. Maka nwa nta na-anaghị aṅụ ara, ga n'ihu na-enye ya mmiri ara ehi maọbụ fọmula ha na-eji n'etiti oge ORS.

Na-ahụ maka ihe ịrịbama ndị a nke gosiri na ịkpọnwụ ahụ akarịala: anya abanyelarị n'ime, ọ bụrụ na ị kpụọ akpụkpọ ahụ n'azụ aka ọ naghị alọta azụ ngwa ngwa, obi na-akụ ọsọ mana ike adịghị, mmadụ na-arahụ ụra ebe ọbụla maọbụ enweghị ike ịza, enweghị ike ịṅụ mmiri maọbụ na-agbọ ihe ọbụla ọ ṅụrụ, ọ naghị anyụ mamịrị maọbụ mamịrị ya na-agba ọchịchịrị nke ukwu. Ọ bụrụ na ị hụ nke ọbụla n'ime ihe ndị a, nke ahụ bụ mberede. Buru onye ọrịa gaa ụlọ ọgwụ ozugbo n'ihi na ha ga-achọ mmiri drip (IV fluid).

Ihe ịrịbama ndị ọzọ dị ize ndụ maka ụmụaka: nwa na-agbọ agbọ ihe niile a na-enye ya n'enweghị nkwụsị, ọbara dị n'ime nsị, nwa nta nke na-erughị ọnwa isii nwere ahụ ọkụ dị elu na afọ ọsịsa, nwa jụrụ iri nri maọbụ ịṅụ ihe niile. Ihe ndị a niile chọrọ nlekọta ahụike nke ngwa ngwa, n'agbanyeghị ma ọ dị ka nwa ahụ kpọnwụrụ ahụ maọbụ na ọ dịghị.

Kọlera nwere ike igbu karịa ọkara ndị na-enwetaraghị ọgwụgwọ, mana site na ọgwụgwọ ịtinye mmiri ọzọ n'ahụ nke ọma, ọnwụ nwere ike ịda ruo ihe dịka otu n'ime narị (1%). Ya mere, iru ụlọ ọgwụ bụ ihe dị iche n'etiti ndụ na ọnwụ.

Kpọọ Ndị Ọrụ Ahụike Oku Ozugbo

Echere eche nsonaazụ nyocha ụlọ nyocha tupu ị kọọ. Mgbe ọtụtụ ndị mmadụ nwere afọ ọsịsa mmiri mmiri na ịgbọ agbọ n'otu ama n'otu oge, nke ahụ eruola ebe a ga-akọ ozugbo n'okpuru Iwu Ahụike Mba Ụwa nke WHO (International Health Regulations) na n'okpuru usoro nlekọta ọrịa nke fere bụrụ mba niile.

Kpọtụrụ ụlọ ọgwụ kacha nso, ngalaba ahụike gọọmenti obodo, onye nlekọta ọrịa na-efe efe (disease surveillance officer), maọbụ ụzọ ikwu okwu ọrịa nke mba. Gwa ha: ọnụ ọgụgụ ndị nrịa nrịa, ihe afọ ha na-adị, oge ọrịa ahụ bidoro (kwuo ma ha niile bidoro n'otu oge maọbụ otu otu, n'ihi na ozi a ga-enyere ndị ọrụ ahụike aka ịghọta ma ọ bụ otu imetụ maọbụ imetụ na-aga n'ihu), aha na ebe isi mmiri a na-enyo enyo dị, na ihe ọbụla ọzọ ha hụrụ banyere isi mmiri ahụ (ma agba ya agbanweela, ma ọ na-esi ísì, ma mmiri ozuzo emejuola ebe ahụ n'oge na-adịbeghị anya, ma ụlọ mposi dị ya nso, ma anụmanụ na-abanye n'ime ya).

Ịkpọ oku ngwa ngwa na-amalite nzaghachi ndị obodo n'onwe ya enweghị ike ime: nyocha ụlọ nyocha nke isi mmiri iji chọpụta nje, nkwenye ọrịa nke ahụike, iweta ORS na mmiri drip, nyocha ọrịa na-efe efe iji gosi isi mmiri ma chọta ndị niile metụtara, na ndozi nka nke isi mmiri ahụ.

Chekwaa Isi Mmiri

Kọlera na ọtụtụ ihe ndị ọzọ na-akpata afọ ọsịsa mmiri mmiri na-agbasa karịsịa site na mmiri na nri nke nsị mmadụ nwere ọrịa banyere n'ime. Isi mmiri nke onye ọbụla na-eji nke rụrụ arụ bụ ihe na-akpata ọrịa karịsịa n'oge ọrịa na-ebili.

Kwụsị iji isi mmiri ahụ a na-enyo enyo ozugbo. Nke a bụ ihe oge kacha dị mkpa maka ya. Elekere ọbụla isi mmiri rụrụ arụ ahụ ka nọ na-arụ ọrụ, ndị mmadụ ọhụrụ na-enweta ọrịa. Ezinụlọ ndị niile ga-akwụsị iji mmiri ahụ eme ihe ọbụla: ịṅụ, isi nri, ikwadebe nri, ịsa nri, ịsa efere na ngaji, ịsa eze, na ihe ọbụla nke ga-eme ka mmiri ahụ banye n'ọnụ mmadụ. Ọ bụrụ na isi mmiri ahụ bụ olulu ama, bọọhol, paipu mmiri, maọbụ iyi, ndị ndu obodo ga-agwa ezinụlọ niile na-eji ya. Okwu ọnụ naanị ezughị okè. Ihe mgbochi nke a ga-ahụ anya na-arụ ọrụ ka mma: kenye eriri gburugburu ya, debe onye ga-anọ na-elekọta ya, tinye ihe ngosi ịdọ aka na ntị nke onye ọbụla ga-ahụ. Ndị mmadụ jiri isi mmiri ahụ mee ihe ruo ọtụtụ afọ nwere ike ịnọgide na-aga ebe ahụ n'ihi àgwà, ọ bụladị mgbe ha nụchara ịdọ aka na ntị.

Mana ị ga-enyecharịrị ha mmiri ọzọ ozugbo. Ị gaghị agwa ndị mmadụ ka ha kwụsị iji mmiri ma ị nyeghị ha nhọrọ ọzọ. Ọ bụrụ na isi mmiri ọzọ dị ọcha adịghị, a ga-emechara mmiri ọbụla a kụtere n'ebe ahụ tupu onye ọbụla eji ya mee ihe ọbụla nke ga-abanye n'ọnụ.

Meenụ mmiri niile unu ga-aṅụ ka ọ dị ọcha. Sienụ mmiri ka ọ gbọọ ụfụfụ nke ọma (rolling boil) opekata mpe nkeji otu tupu e wepụ ya n'ọkụ. Hapụnụ ya ka o jụọ n'ime otu ite ahụ unu sịịrị ya, kpuchiekwanụ ite ahụ. Ewụpụla ya n'ime ihe na-adịghị ọcha.

Ọ bụrụ na ịsị anaghị adị mfe n'ihi oke mmiri a chọrọ maọbụ n'ihi na nkụ maọbụ mmanụ ọkụ ezughị, jiri chlorine mee. Jiri ngwongwo chlorine ụlọ (mmiri bleach maọbụ tabuleti e ji eme mmiri ka ọ dị ọcha nke dị n'ahịa) wee soro ntụzịaka dị n'elu akpa ya. WHO na-atụ aro na mmiri kwesịrị ịnweta ihe dịka 2 mg/L free chlorine residual maka mmiri doro anya. Ọ bụrụ na mmiri ahụ gbara ụzọ maọbụ na-acha (cloudy), buru ụzọ sị ya site n'akwa dị ọcha maọbụ hapụ ya ka ihe ndị dị n'ime ya daa ala, wee tinye chlorine karịa, n'ihi na ihe rụrụ arụ nọ n'ime mmiri gbara ụzọ na-eri chlorine, na-ebelata otu o si arụ ọrụ. Mgbe ị tinyechara chlorine, chere opekata mpe nkeji iri atọ (30) tupu onye ọbụla aṅụ.

Ọ bụrụ na ịsị na chlorine adịghị, ị nwere ike ịnwale ụzọ SODIS: kujuo karama plastik nke doro anya (PET, ọ bụghị nke na-adịghị ahụ n'ime) mmiri, debe ya ebe anwụ na-amụkwasị kpọm kpọm opekata mpe elekere isii. Ọ bụrụ na igwe ojii kpuchiri anyanwụ, hapụ ya ruo ụbọchị abụọ. Ụzọ a na-ebelata nje nke ọma, mana o zubeghị okè. Ọ naghị arụ ọrụ megide Cryptosporidium, ọ dịghịkwa ka e nwere ike ịdabere na ya dịka ịsị maọbụ chlorination.

Chekwaa mmiri unu mechara nke ọma. Tinye ya n'ime ihe dị ọcha, nke nwere mkpuchi, nke ọnụ ya dị nta. Etinyela aka, iko, maọbụ ihe ọbụla n'ime mmiri ahụ. Wụpụta ya, maọbụ jiri ihe nwere tapu.

Ụlọ Mposi Na Ịdị Ọcha

Ịsa aka bụ ihe dị oke mkpa maka ezinụlọ ọbụla, ọ bụghị naanị ndị nwere ndị nrịa nrịa. Onye ọbụla ga-asa aka na ncha na mmiri mgbe ha si n'ụlọ mposi, mgbe ha metụrụ onye ọrịa maọbụ ihe ọbụla nsị maọbụ agbọ ọsịsa ya metụrụ aka, tupu ha esie nri, tupu ha erie nri, na tupu ha enye nwa nri. Ọ bụrụ na ncha adịghị, ntụ nwere ike inyere aka nwa ntakịrị, mana ncha ka mma.

Wepụ nsị na agbọ ọsịsa onye ọrịa n'ụzọ ziri ezi. Nsị na agbọ ọsịsa niile sitere n'onye ọrịa ga-abanye n'ụlọ mposi. Ọ bụrụ na onye ọrịa enweghị ike iru ụlọ mposi, jiri ịkwọ maọbụ ihe ọzọ nara ya, tinye mmiri chlorine (0.2% chlorine), chere nkeji iri atọ (30), wee wụpụ ya n'ụlọ mposi. Ewụpụla nsị a na-emechabeghị n'ime gọta, iyi, osimiri, maọbụ n'elu ala. Ọ bụrụ na ị mee otú ahụ, ị na-emepụta ụzọ ọzọ nke ịmeta rụ nke nwere ike imetụta isi mmiri ndị ọzọ maọbụ mee ka ọrịa gbasaa site n'onye gaa n'onye.

Sachapụ ebe ọbụla nsị maọbụ agbọ ọsịsa metụrụ. Jiri mmiri chlorine 0.2% saa akwa ndina, uwe, na ala nke nsị maọbụ agbọ ọsịsa metụrụ. Efere, iko, na ngaji nke onye ọrịa jiri, sapụ ha iche site n'iji mmiri e mere ka ọ dị ọcha na ncha maọbụ chlorine.

Ịnya nsị n'èzí ga-akwụsị kpamkpam. Ọ bụrụ na ụfọdụ ndị nọ n'obodo ka na-anya nsị n'èzí, n'ọhịa, maọbụ ebe ọbụla na-abụghị ụlọ mposi, nke ahụ aghọọla ihe ize ndụ dị oke njọ maka onye ọbụla ugbu a. Nsị mmadụ ọbụla nke banyere n'ebe obibi a na-emechaghị nwere ike ịghọ isi ihe ịmeta rụ ọzọ na-aga n'ihu maọbụ ịmeta rụ ọhụrụ. A chọrọ ụlọ mposi nke mberede ugbu a. Ọ bụrụ na ụlọ mposi dị adị ezughị, ị nwere ike ịgwu ụlọ mposi olulu nke oge nwa oge, mana ya dị opekata mpe mita 30 n'ebe isi mmiri ọbụla dị, ala ala olulu ahụ kwesịkwa ịnọ opekata mpe mita 1.5 n'elu oke mmiri dị n'okpuru ala (water table).

Nchekwa Nri

Sienụ nri nke ọma, riekwanụ ya mgbe ọ ka na-ekpo ọkụ. Ọtụtụ n'ime nje na-akpata ọrịa afọ ọsịsa site na mmiri na-anwụ mgbe nri na-ekpo ọkụ. Erila akwụkwọ nri maọbụ mkpụrụ osisi na-adịghị ehi ehi ma ọ bụghị nke ị nwere ike ịkpụchapụ akpụkpọ ya. Erila nri nke nọọla oge n'ọnọdụ okpomọkụ ụlọ, karịsịa mgbe ihu igwe na-ekpo ọkụ. Zere nri ndị a na-ere n'okporo ụzọ maọbụ nri nnọkọ n'oge ọrịa a na-ebili, ma ọ bụghị na ị mara na e siri ya nke ọma. Sachapụ ebe ị na-akwadebe nri na mmiri dị ọcha tupu ị malite.

Tụfuo nri e ji mmiri ahụ a na-enyo enyo kwadebe. Nri ọbụla e sere, ji mmiri ahụ sie, maọbụ ji mmiri sitere n'isi mmiri ahụ a na-enyo enyo kwadebe tupu a mara na ọ rụrụ arụ, tụfuo ya. Nke a gụnyere nri e siri ire maọbụ nri maka nnọkọ ọha.

Otu Esi Elekọta Onye Ọrịa N'ụlọ

Ọ bụrụ na onye ọrịa ka nwere ike ịṅụ mmiri ma ịkpọnwụ ahụ ya adịghịkwa njọ, ị nwere ike ịnọ n'ụlọ na-elekọta ya na ORS mgbe ị na-eche maọbụ n'etiti oge ị na-aga ụlọ ọgwụ. Onye na-elekọta onye ọrịa kwesịrị ịhapụ efere, iko, ngaji, na akwa ndina iche maka onye ọrịa, saa aka nke ọma mgbe ọbụla ha metụrụ onye ọrịa aka, wee debe ihe si n'ahụ onye ọrịa pụta iche ma sachapụ ya.

Mana, ọ bụrụ na nke ọbụla n'ime ihe ndị a metụtara onye ọrịa, buru ya gaa ụlọ ọgwụ ozugbo:

Onye ọrịa agosịla ihe ịrịbama nke ịkpọnwụ ahụ dị njọ. Onye ọrịa bụ nwa nta nke na-erughị afọ ise. Onye ọrịa bụ nwanyị dị ime. Onye ọrịa nwere ọrịa ọzọ n'ahụ ya na mbụ.

Ọ Bụrụ Na Mmadụ Anwụọ

Ọ bụrụ na mmadụ anwụọ n'ihe a na-enyo enyo na ọ bụ kọlera, ozu ahụ ka nwere ike ịkesa ọrịa. Ndị e zụrụ azụ kwesịrị ịkwado ozu ahụ maka olili ozu. Ọ bụrụ na ndị e zụrụ azụ adịghị, ndị ga-ejide ozu ahụ kwesịrị iyi gloovu, belata otu ha si emetụ mmiri ahụ onye nwụrụ anwụ aka, jiri mmiri chlorine 0.5% sachaa ahụ ozu ahụ, wee saa aka ha nke ọma mgbe ha mechara. Nnọkọ olili ozu nke dị ukwu ebe ndị mmadụ niile nọ na-eri nri ọnụ abụrụla ụzọ ịkesa ọrịa e dere n'akwụkwọ n'oge ọrịa kọlera na-efe efe. Belatanụ ọnụ ọgụgụ ndị mmadụ, zerekwanụ nri ọha n'ebe olili ozu n'oge ọrịa na-efe efe.

Ihe Ezinụlọ Ekwesịghị Ime

Ejila ọgwụ na-akwụsị afọ ọsịsa (dịka loperamide). Ụdị ọgwụ a na-eme ka afọ daa jụụ mana ọ naghị egbu nje. Ọ na-ezo otu mmiri si efu n'ahụ, ihe nwekwara ike ịdị njọ karịa, karịsịa maka ụmụaka na maka ọrịa nke nje ndị na-abanye n'ime ahụ (dịka Shigella) na-akpata, ebe ịme ka afọ daa nwayọọ nwere ike ime ka ahụ nara nsị (toxin) karịa.

Ejela gaa zụta ọgwụ antibiotic n'ahịa n'enweghị ntụzịaka dọkịta. Ọgwụ antibiotic nwere ọrụ ya pụrụ iche na ụfọdụ ọrịa afọ ọsịsa (karịsịa kọlera na shigellosis), mana ụdị antibiotic ole, ọtụtụ ole, na ma a ga-eji ya bụ ihe dabere na nje ole na-akpata ya, usoro mgbochi (resistance patterns) dị n'ógbè, na etu ọrịa ahụ si dị njọ. Ọ bụrụ na ndị mmadụ na-eji antibiotic eme ihe n'ụzọ na-ezighị ezi, nje ga-amụta otu esi eguzogide ya, maka ụfọdụ ọrịa nke vaịrọsị maọbụ parasaịtị na-akpata, antibiotic agaghị enyere aka ma nwekwara ike ime ihe ọjọọ.

Enyela ndị ezinụlọ nwere ndị nrịa nrịa ihere maọbụ achụpụla ha. Ịkewapụ ezinụlọ ndị nwere ndị na-arịa arịa na-akụziri ndị mmadụ ka ha zoo ọrịa, na-eme ka ha nọọ nwa oge tupu ha achọọ ọgwụgwọ, na-ebelatakwa otu ha si enyere ndị ọrụ ahụike aka. Isi mmiri rụrụ arụ kpatara ọrịa ahụ, ọ bụghị ezinụlọ ndị ahụ. Ịtụ ụta n'isi ezinụlọ kama n'isi mmiri nke metụtara gburugburu ebe obibi ezighị ezi n'eziokwu ma bụrụkwa ihe na-emerụ ahụ n'ọrụ.

Echekwala na ọrịa na-efe efe agwụla n'ihi na ọrịa ọhụrụ ebelatala. Effective outbreak communication should:

Listen first: Identify the exact rumour, where it is circulating, why it appears credible and what fear or information gap is driving it.
Respond promptly: Correct harmful claims before they spread widely, while avoiding repeated or sensational presentation of the false claim.
Lead with the verified fact: State what is known, explain the evidence briefly, then give the action people should take.
Acknowledge uncertainty: Clearly distinguish confirmed information from what is still being investigated. State when and where updates will appear.

Give practical instructions: Explain symptoms, transmission routes, prevention measures, where to seek care and which services are free or available.
Provide evidence: Name the responsible health authority and link or direct people to an official source, hotline or treatment centre that can verify the information.
Coordinate messages: Health agencies and partner organisations should use consistent facts and explain any change in guidance.
Create two-way communication: Provide ways for people to ask questions, report rumours and receive answers. Track whether corrections are understood.
Avoid stigma and blame: Do not associate infection with an ethnic, religious, occupational or migrant group. Protect patients’ privacy.
Correct mistakes openly: If authorities previously gave incorrect or incomplete information, acknowledge it, explain what changed and issue the corrected guidance.

Addressing Rumours During Infectious Disease Outbreaks

Rumours spread fastest when information gaps exist and when people don't trust official sources. Here's what actually works:

1. Speed Matters More Than Perfection

Don't wait for complete data before communicating. Early, honest uncertainty beats late certainty. If you're silent for three weeks while rumors proliferate, you've already lost credibility.

Say: "We don't have all the answers yet, but here's what we know and what we're investigating."

Don't say nothing, then appear later with the "real" answer.

2. Address the Rumour Directly—By Name

Ignoring a rumour doesn't kill it; it lets it grow unchallenged. Name it explicitly and explain why it's wrong.

Indirect: "People should trust science."

Effective: "Some people are saying bleach can cure this disease. It cannot. Bleach is toxic and will cause severe harm."

The specificity matters. Vague reassurance reads as evasion.

3. Lead With What IS True, Then Correct

The "illusory truth effect" means people remember repetition, not refutation. If you repeat the rumour too much while denying it, you reinforce it.

Structure: State the correct information first and most prominently. Then address the false claim briefly. Don't dwell.

4. Explain the "Why" Behind Your Message

People who understand reasoning are harder to mislead later. Explain the mechanism, the evidence base, the source of the information.

Weak: "Wash your hands."

Stronger: "The virus survives on skin and surfaces for hours. Soap breaks down the lipid layer that protects it, rendering it inactive. This is why hand-washing works."

5. Use Trusted Local Intermediaries

Your official health ministry's written statement has less reach and credibility in many communities than a respected elder, religious leader, market trader, or community health worker saying the same thing.

Build relationships before outbreak. Train community figures on accurate information so they can correct rumours in real-time at the local level, not through distant campaigns.

6. Acknowledge Legitimate Concerns Underneath the Rumour

Rumours often root in real anxieties: "Will I lose my job if I report symptoms?" or "Has the government hidden outbreak data before?"

Address the legitimate fear, not just the false claim.

Rumour: "The disease doesn't actually exist; the government invented it."

Underlying concern: "The government lies to us sometimes."

Response: "We understand past health messages weren't always accurate. Here's what's different now [explain oversight, transparency mechanisms, community involvement]. Here's how to verify information independently..."

7. Provide Simple, Repeatable Action Items

Rumours often thrive because people feel powerless. Give them concrete, low-barrier things to do.

Not: "Trust the system."

Yes: "Bring symptoms to [specific location], tell [named person], ask these [three specific] questions about treatment, and contact [number] if you have concerns."

8. Use Multiple Channels Suited to How Your Population Communicates

If people get information via radio, church announcements, and messaging apps—use all three. One channel isn't enough.

And meet people where they already are. Text messages might reach 30% of your audience. Community gatherings reach a different 30%. You need both.

9. Accept You Cannot Control All Narratives

Some people will believe the rumour regardless. Your goal isn't universal belief; it's shifting the median. Focus on people who are genuinely uncertain, not those deeply committed to a false belief.

10. Consistency Across Messengers Matters Enormously

If your health ministry says one thing, a regional official says another, and a local clinic says a third, you've failed. Rumours fill inconsistency gaps.

Align messaging across all official channels before you communicate publicly. This takes coordination time, but it pays back immediately.

The Hard Truth

Rumour control isn't primarily about messaging skill—it's about trust earned over years, not weeks. Communities that trusted their health system before the outbreak will believe it during. Communities that didn't won't.

If this is your first outbreak communication, you're starting from a deficit. You can narrow it with transparency, speed, and consistency, but you won't erase it. Plan accordingly.

Also: some rumours will seem absurd to you and feel unworthy of a response. Respond anyway. The absurdity is precisely why it spreads—it's memorable.

How Public-Health Messages Should Address Rumours During an Infectious-Disease Outbreak
Why Rumours Demand a Deliberate Response

Rumours during outbreaks are not incidental noise. They function as competing explanations that fill information vacuums, and they spread through the same social networks that public-health messages must use. Unaddressed rumours have directly contributed to treatment refusal, attacks on health workers, flight from quarantine, and continued unsafe practices in documented outbreaks including Ebola in West Africa (2014–2016), Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo (2018–2020), and COVID-19 globally. The WHO's formal framework for managing infodemics, developed from 2020 onward, treats misinformation as a threat vector parallel to the pathogen itself.

Ignoring rumours does not cause them to dissipate. It cedes the information space to unverified claims and erodes institutional credibility over time.

Principles That Govern Effective Rumour Response

Acknowledge the rumour directly before correcting it. Research in health communication, including findings synthesised in the WHO's guidance on risk communication and community engagement (RCCE), indicates that people need to hear that their concern has been registered before they will consider an alternative explanation. A message that opens with the correction without naming the belief it is correcting often fails to connect with the audience that holds the belief. The recommended structure is: state the claim that is circulating, acknowledge why it might seem plausible or why people are concerned, then provide the factual correction with evidence.

However, this must be done carefully. Repeating a false claim too prominently or too many times can inadvertently reinforce it. The correction should receive more space, emphasis, and repetition than the rumour itself. This principle draws on research in cognitive psychology regarding the "continued influence effect" and the "familiarity backfire effect," though more recent evidence suggests the backfire effect is less robust than initially believed. The practical guidance remains: lead with the truth, use the rumour as a reference point rather than as the headline.

Provide a causal explanation, not just a denial. Flat denials ("That is not true") are among the least effective forms of correction. People hold beliefs because those beliefs provide an explanatory framework. Displacing a rumour requires offering an alternative explanation that accounts for the same observations. If the rumour is "the government created the disease to control us," a flat denial addresses the claim but not the underlying distrust. A more effective message explains what is actually known about the pathogen's origin, what evidence supports that explanation, and what the government's actual response actions are, while acknowledging that distrust has legitimate historical roots.

Match the channel and messenger to the audience. A technically accurate correction issued through a ministry press release will not reach communities that distrust government institutions and receive their information through religious leaders, market networks, or social media groups. WHO and CDC rumour-response guidance consistently emphasises identifying trusted voices within the affected community, equipping those voices with accurate information, and supporting them to deliver corrections in their own words through the channels their community actually uses. Community health workers, religious leaders, traditional leaders, teachers, and local radio presenters have all served this function effectively in documented outbreak responses.

Respond rapidly. Rumours consolidate quickly. A rumour that circulates uncorrected for days or weeks becomes part of the community's shared understanding and is far harder to dislodge. The WHO's RCCE framework and the CDC's Crisis and Emergency Risk Communication (CERC) model both emphasise that speed of initial response is critical, even when complete information is not yet available. Saying "we are aware of this concern, here is what we know so far, and we will share more as we confirm it" is more effective than waiting for perfect information while the rumour spreads unopposed.

Use the language and framing of the affected community. Messages composed in formal, technical, or bureaucratic language are filtered out by audiences under stress. Effective rumour correction uses the vernacular of the community, references local experience, and frames explanations in terms that connect to existing knowledge. This is not simplification for its own sake. It is a recognition that information must be cognitively accessible under conditions of fear, uncertainty, and competing claims. Multilingual contexts require messages produced in each relevant language, not translated from a single source text, but adapted to reflect the communicative norms and conceptual frameworks of each language community.

Structural Approaches to Rumour Management

Establish systematic rumour surveillance. Effective outbreak communication operations do not wait for rumours to cause visible harm before responding. They actively monitor what communities are saying through social media listening, feedback from community health workers, reports from contact tracers, call-centre logs, and direct community engagement. The WHO, UNICEF, and IFRC jointly developed a community feedback mechanism for this purpose during the DRC Ebola response, and similar systems operated during COVID-19. The objective is to detect rumours early, categorise them by risk level, and prioritise response.

Categorise rumours by potential harm. Not all rumours require the same intensity of response. A rumour that a specific food prevents infection is low-risk and may warrant a brief clarification. A rumour that health workers are deliberately spreading the disease, or that treatment centres are killing patients, poses an immediate threat to the response and to health worker safety, requiring urgent, high-intensity, multi-channel correction with direct community engagement. Triage allows resource allocation proportional to risk.

Create feedback loops. Correction is not a single event. After a rumour-response message is disseminated, the communication team must monitor whether the correction is reaching its intended audience, whether it is being believed, and whether the rumour is persisting, mutating, or being replaced by new rumours. This iterative cycle of listen, analyse, respond, and monitor is central to the WHO infodemic management framework.

What Public-Health Communicators Should Avoid

Do not dismiss or ridicule the people who believe the rumour. Condescension triggers defensive entrenchment. People who feel mocked or dismissed become more resistant to correction, not less. The goal is to change the information environment, not to win an argument.

Do not over-promise or make claims that later prove false. If a health authority corrects a rumour with a confident factual claim that subsequently turns out to be wrong or incomplete, the credibility damage is severe and durable. It is better to be transparent about uncertainty than to project false confidence. Statements like "based on current evidence" and "we will update this if new information emerges" preserve credibility even when the situation evolves.

Do not rely on a single correction. Cognitive research consistently shows that a single exposure to a correction is insufficient to displace a well-established false belief. Corrections must be repeated across multiple channels, by multiple messengers, over time. This does not mean repeating the rumour. It means repeating the true explanation through varied formats, voices, and contexts.

Do not centralise all messaging in a single institutional voice. Institutional messaging has a role, but it is insufficient alone, particularly in contexts where institutional trust is low. Effective rumour response is distributed: it equips many messengers with consistent core facts while allowing each to communicate in their own voice and through their own relationships.

Evidence Base

The principles above are drawn from the WHO Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE) framework, the WHO infodemic management framework (developed from 2020), the CDC Crisis and Emergency Risk Communication (CERC) manual, published evaluations of community engagement during the 2014–2016 West Africa Ebola outbreak and the 2018–2020 DRC Ebola outbreaks, and the broader health-communication and cognitive-psychology literature on misinformation correction. Key contributing research areas include the continued influence effect (Johnson & Seifert, 1994, and subsequent work), the debunking literature reviewed in Lewandowsky et al. (2012, "Misinformation and Its Correction"), and field evaluations of community feedback mechanisms by WHO, UNICEF, and IFRC.

Specific operational protocols vary by country and outbreak. National health authorities and WHO country offices maintain context-specific guidance that should be consulted for implementation.

Addressing Rumours in Public-Health Messaging During Outbreaks

Rumours during infectious-disease outbreaks aren't just noise — they're signals. They tell you where trust has broken down, where official communication has left gaps, and what communities actually fear. Treating them as problems to suppress rather than information to respond to is one of the most common and costly mistakes in outbreak communication.

Here's what the evidence and field experience actually support:

Acknowledge, Don't Dismiss

The instinct of most health authorities is to ignore rumours or issue blanket denials. This backfires almost every time. When people hear "that's not true" without any engagement with why they believed it, they conclude officials are either hiding something or don't understand their reality.

The more effective approach is to name the rumour directly. Say what people are hearing, say you understand why it's circulating, and then provide the specific, verifiable counter-information. Vague reassurance — "the situation is under control" — actively fuels distrust.

Speed Matters More Than Perfection

Rumours fill information vacuums. If official channels go silent for 48 hours during an active outbreak, that vacuum will be filled by speculation, fear, and fabrication. Particularly on platforms like WhatsApp, voice notes and forwarded messages spread faster than any press release.

Health authorities need to communicate frequently, even when the update is "we don't have new numbers yet, here's what we're doing to get them." Admitting uncertainty is far more credible than delayed certainty.

Match the Language and Channel

This is where many outbreak responses fail structurally. Rumours spread in the languages people actually speak, through the channels they actually use — community WhatsApp groups, market conversations, religious gatherings, radio call-in shows. Official responses issued only in English, only through formal press conferences, or only through government websites simply don't reach the populations most affected.

Effective counter-messaging must operate in the same linguistic register and on the same platforms where the rumours circulate. This means local languages, vernacular forms, voice notes, community radio, and messaging through figures people already trust.

Use Trusted Intermediaries, Not Just Authority Figures

During outbreaks, trust in government health officials is often already damaged — sometimes for legitimate historical reasons. Deploying messages exclusively through official channels can actually reduce credibility.

Community health workers, religious leaders, traditional leaders, market women's associations, and especially people who have recovered from the disease in question are significantly more persuasive messengers. A recovered patient saying "I went to the treatment centre and this is what happened" addresses fear and rumour simultaneously in a way no press statement can.

Be Transparent About What You Don't Know

One of the most persistent generators of rumours is the gap between what communities observe and what officials report. If people see neighbours dying but official case counts seem low, they will conclude — often reasonably — that numbers are being suppressed. If treatment centres are perceived as places people enter but don't leave, conspiracy theories about what happens inside will spread.

The response isn't to insist the numbers are correct. It's to explain how cases are counted, why there might be discrepancies, and what is actually happening in treatment facilities. Radical transparency about methodology, limitations, and uncertainty is more credible than confident pronouncements that contradict people's lived experience.

Address the Emotional Root, Not Just the Factual Claim

Most outbreak rumours aren't really about facts — they're about fear, loss of control, and distrust. "The government created this disease" is rarely a sincere epidemiological hypothesis. It's an expression of powerlessness and suspicion rooted in historical experience.

Effective messaging acknowledges the fear and the historical basis for distrust before presenting corrective information. This isn't about being soft — it's about being strategically honest about the conditions that make rumours plausible to the people spreading them.

Provide Actionable Guidance, Not Just Corrections

Telling people a rumour is false without giving them something concrete to do instead leaves them with anxiety and no outlet. Every piece of counter-messaging should include specific, locally feasible protective actions. Not "wash your hands" in the abstract, but "here is where you can get soap or chlorine solution in your area, here is what to do if someone in your household develops symptoms, here is who to call."

The goal isn't to win an argument with a rumour. It's to give people a credible alternative narrative that includes a clear path of action.

The central principle underlying all of this: rumours are a symptom of communication failure, not a cause of it. If your outbreak response is generating persistent rumours, the problem isn't misinformation — the problem is that your communication strategy has not earned enough trust, moved fast enough, or met communities where they actually are.

How Public-Health Messages Suppose Take Address Rumours During Disease Outbreak

When sickness dey spread from person to person, rumours they spread even faster. Here na how to fight am proper:

1. Talk Fast Before Rumour Take Over

No be wait make you get all answer before you open your mouth. If you stay quiet for three weeks while false information dey fly everywhere, you don already lose the battle.

Better approach: "We know some things now, but we still dey investigate other things. Here na wetin we know for sure..."

No be wait till everything perfect. Start talk immediately, even if say the full picture no complete yet.

2. Call the Rumour By Name—Say Am Clear Clear

Pretend like the rumour no exist no go kill am. You must name am directly and explain why am wrong.

Weak way: "People suppose trust medical knowledge."

Strong way: "Some people dey say say drinking salt water go cure this sickness. That one lie. Salt water no cure am—am go make you sick instead."

When you name am clear, people understand say you hear the talk and you get answer for am.

3. Put the True Thing First, Then Correct the False One

If you repeat the lie too many times even when you dey deny am, people go remember the lie better than the truth.

Do am this way: Say the correct thing first and strongest. Then address the false claim quick quick, no be make you dwell on am.

Correct way: "Hand washing save lives because soap kill the virus. That na why we say wash hand. No be the story say bleach go cure am—that one no work."

4. Explain Why—Not Just What

When people understand the reason behind the message, dem go understand better and rumours go find hard time catch dem.

Weak: "Wash your hand."

Better: "The virus stay on skin and hands for many hours. Soap destroy the thing wey protect the virus. That na why washing hand work strong strong."

5. Use People Wey Community Trust

Your government health office paper or announcement no go reach everybody strong strong. But when the village elder talk, or the imam, or the market woman wey everybody respect—that message go enter people mind different.

No wait for outbreak before you do this. Build relationship with community leaders now now. Teach them proper information so when rumour start fly, them go correct am right there in the community.

6. Address the Real Fear Wey Hide Inside the Rumour

Rumours them usually grow from real worry: "If I report say I sick, government go lock me up?" or "Government hide truth from us before, why we suppose trust now?"

You suppose answer the real fear, not just the false claim itself.

Example:

Rumour say: "The sickness no real—government invent am."

Real worry underneath: "Government lie to us many times before."

Your answer: "We hear say government no always tell truth before. But this time, here na the difference [explain]. You can check this information yourself by [how to verify]. Call [number] if you get questions."

7. Give People Something To Do

When people feel like dem powerless, rumours spread more. Give them clear, simple action they can take.

No be: "Trust the system."

Better: "Go to [this place], talk to [this person], ask these questions [list three], and call [this number] if something no clear."

8. Use All the Ways People Get Information

If your community dey listen radio, if dem dey go church, if dem dey use WhatsApp—use all of am. One way no be enough.

Radio, community gathering, text message, mosque announcement, market talk, clinic poster—use everything wey reach your people.

9. Make Sure All Authorities Talk the Same Thing

If federal government say one thing, state official say another thing, and clinic say different thing again—you don already fail. Rumour go use that confusion to spread.

Before you talk to public, make sure all your people agree on the message. This take time to coordinate, but am worth am.

10. Understand Say You No Go Win Everybody

Some people go believe the rumour no matter wetin you do. Your work no be to convince everybody—your work be to convince the people wey still uncertain.

The people wey already deep inside false belief, leave them for now. Focus on the people still thinking, still asking questions.

The Real Talk

The biggest secret: rumour control no be about message skill alone—am about trust.

Communities wey trust their health system before sickness come go believe am during sickness. Communities wey no trust am before, you go struggle to convince am now.

If this na your first time you dey communicate about outbreak, you start from behind. You can improve am with honest talk, speed, and consistency—but you no go erase the doubt quick quick. Plan for am.

One more thing: if rumour seem foolish to you, respond to am anyway. The foolishness na exactly why am spread fast—people remember am because am surprising.

Why Rumour Na Serious Problem Wey You No Fit Ignore
