Dem dey work like another explanation wey dey compete with the correct information, and dem dey spread through the same community network wey health message suppose use. When rumour dey spread and nobody address am, e dey make people refuse treatment, attack health workers, run comot from quarantine, and continue to do the same dangerous things wey dey spread sickness.

This one no be theory. During Ebola for West Africa (2014–2016), rumour say treatment centres dey kill people make community people attack health workers and hide sick family members. During Ebola for DRC (2018–2020), distrust and misinformation slow down the whole response. During COVID-19, misinformation spread across the whole world cause people to refuse vaccine and use dangerous fake remedies. Na because of all these experiences, WHO develop infodemic management framework from 2020, wey treat misinformation as threat wey dey dangerous like the disease itself.

If you leave rumour, e no go just die by itself. E go fill the space wey correct information suppose dey, and the more time e stay, the more people go believe am and the harder e go be to remove am.

The Main Principles Wey Suppose Guide How You Take Respond to Rumour

Acknowledge the rumour first before you correct am. Research for health communication, including wetin WHO put inside their Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE) guidance, show say people need to hear say you understand their concern before dem go open mind to hear another explanation. If you just jump straight to correction without first calling the belief wey dey circulate by name, the people wey believe the rumour no go feel say you dey talk to them. The correct way be say: first talk the claim wey dey go round, acknowledge why e fit look like say e make sense or why people dey worried, then give the correct fact with evidence to back am.

But you must do this one with care. If you repeat the false claim too many times or put am for headline, you fit accidentally make people remember the lie more than the truth. The correction suppose get more space, more emphasis, and more repetition pass the rumour itself. Research for cognitive psychology on wetin dem call "continued influence effect" support this approach. The practical rule be say: lead with the truth, use the rumour as reference point, but no make the rumour be the main thing people remember.

Give explanation, no just deny. To just say "that one no be true" na one of the weakest way to correct rumour. People believe rumour because the rumour explain something wey dem dey observe or fear. To remove rumour from somebody mind, you need to give them another explanation wey make sense of the same thing wey dem dey see.

For example, if the rumour be say "government create this disease to control us," to just say "no, government no do am" address the claim but e no address the distrust wey make person believe am for the first place. Better message go explain wetin science actually know about where the disease come from, wetin evidence support that explanation, wetin government dey actually do for the response, and e go acknowledge say distrust of government get legitimate historical reasons. You dey replace one story with a better, true story, you no just dey delete the old one.

Make sure the correct messenger carry the message through the correct channel. Accurate correction wey ministry of health release through press conference no go reach community wey no trust government and wey dey get their information from religious leader, market women, WhatsApp group, or local radio. WHO and CDC rumour-response guidance dey always emphasise say you must find the people wey community trust, give those people correct information, and support them to deliver the correction for their own words through the channels wey their people actually dey use.

People wey don work well as trusted messengers for documented outbreak responses include community health workers, pastors and imams, traditional rulers, teachers, and local radio presenters. The key be say the community already trust this person. Trust no be something you fit create overnight during emergency. E dey built on existing relationships.

Respond quick-quick. Rumour dey harden fast. Rumour wey circulate for days or weeks without anybody correct am go enter the community shared understanding, and e go become very hard to shift. Both the WHO RCCE framework and the CDC Crisis and Emergency Risk Communication (CERC) model dey emphasise say speed of first response dey critical, even when you never get complete information yet.

To say "we don hear this concern, this na wetin we know so far, we go share more as we confirm am" dey more effective pass to keep quiet until you get perfect information while rumour dey spread without opposition.

Use the language and the way wey the community dey talk. Message wey dem write for formal, technical, or government language go pass through the ears of people wey dey under stress without entering their mind. Effective rumour correction use the way community dey talk, reference local experience, and explain things for terms wey connect to wetin people already know.

This one no be about making things simple for simple sake. Na about understanding say information must fit enter person head under conditions of fear, confusion, and plenty competing claims. For communities wey speak different languages, messages need to dey produced for each language, and no be say you just translate from one source. You need to adapt the message to fit the way each language community dey communicate and think.

WHO, UNICEF, and IFRC together develop community feedback mechanism for this purpose during DRC Ebola response, and similar systems run during COVID-19. The goal be say, catch rumour early, rank am by how dangerous e be, and respond according to priority.

Rank rumour by how much harm e fit cause. No be every rumour need the same level of response. Rumour say one particular food dey prevent infection dey low-risk, you fit just do quick clarification. But rumour say health workers dey deliberately spread disease, or say treatment centre dey kill patients, that one dey threaten the whole response and the safety of health workers. That kind rumour need urgent, strong, multi-channel correction with direct community engagement. If you rank rumour by risk, you fit use your resources for where dem matter most.

Create feedback loop. To correct rumour no be one-time event. After you don send correction message, the communication team must monitor whether the correction dey reach the people wey need to hear am, whether dem dey believe am, and whether the rumour still dey, don change form, or new rumour don replace am. People wey feel say you dey insult them go resist correction more, no be less. The goal na to change the information environment, no be to win argument or prove say you smart pass them.

Àwọn ìpolongo ìlera àwùjọ yẹ kí wọ́n kojú àhesọ nígbà ìbúrẹ́kẹ́ àrùn tó ń ranni ní kíákíá, pẹ̀lú òtítọ́, àti láì fi ẹ̀gàn tàbí ẹ̀bi kan àwọn ènìyàn.

Fetí sí àwọn àhesọ tó ń tàn káàkiri. Mọ ohun tí àwọn ènìyàn ń sọ àti ohun tí wọ́n ń bẹ̀rù kí ìdáhùn lè dá lórí ìṣòro gidi.
Dáhùn pẹ̀lú ìsọfúnni tó ṣe kedere. Ṣàlàyé ohun tí a mọ̀, ohun tí a kò tíì mọ̀ dájú, àti ohun tí àwọn amòye ń ṣe láti rí ìdáhùn.
Má ṣe tún àhesọ ṣe lọ́nà tó lè mú kí ó túbọ̀ tàn. Ṣe àfihàn òtítọ́ tó yẹ dípò fífi àhesọ náà sí iwájú.
Lo àwọn orísun tí àwùjọ gbẹ́kẹ̀ lé, bí àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ ìlera, olórí àwùjọ, olórí ẹ̀sìn, àti àwọn ilé-iṣẹ́ ìlera tó yẹ.
Ṣe ìsọfúnni náà ní èdè àti ọ̀nà tí àwọn ènìyàn lè lóye, pẹlu redio, WhatsApp, ìpàdé àwùjọ, àti àwọn ikanni míì tó wọ́pọ̀ ní agbègbè náà.
Fún àwọn ènìyàn ní ìtọ́sọ́nà tó wúlò. Kí wọ́n mọ ohun tí wọ́n lè ṣe láti dín ewu kù, àwọn àmì tí wọ́n yẹ kí wọ́n ṣọ́ra fún, àti ibi tí wọ́n ti lè gba ìtọ́jú.
Ṣe àtúnṣe ìsọfúnni nígbà tí ẹ̀rí tuntun bá dé. Bí ìmọ̀ bá yí padà, sọ ìdí tí ìtọ́sọ́nà tuntun fi yàtọ̀ sí ti tẹ́lẹ̀.
Yẹra fún ìdẹruba, ẹ̀gàn, tàbí ìfi ẹ̀sùn kan ẹgbẹ́ kan. Èyí lè ba ìgbẹ́kẹ̀lé jẹ́, kí ó sì mú kí àwọn ènìyàn fi àìsàn pamọ́ tàbí kọ ìtọ́jú.

Ìdí pàtàkì ni pé ìpolongo náà yẹ kí ó kọ́ ìgbẹ́kẹ̀lé, dá àhesọ dúró pẹ̀lú òtítọ́, kí ó sì fún àwọn ènìyàn ní ìgbésẹ̀ tó ṣeé ṣe láti dáàbò bo ara wọn àti àwọn míì.

Àwọn ìpolongo ìlera àwùjọ yẹ kí wọ́n kojú àhesọ nígbà ìbúrẹ́kẹ́ àrùn tó ń ranni ní kíákíá, pẹ̀lú ìsọfúnni tó ṣe kedere, àti láì fi ẹ̀gàn tàbí ẹ̀sùn kan àwọn ènìyàn.

Mọ ohun tí àhesọ náà ń sọ àti ìdí tí àwọn ènìyàn fi ń gbà á. Èyí máa ń ràn ẹgbẹ́ ìlera lọ́wọ́ láti dáhùn sí ìbẹ̀rù tàbí àìní ìsọfúnni tó wà ní abẹ́ rẹ̀.
Fi ohun tí a mọ̀ hàn ní kedere. Sọ ohun tí a ti fìdí rẹ̀ múlẹ̀, ohun tí a kò tíì mọ̀ dájú, àti ohun tí àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ ìlera ń ṣe láti rí ìdáhùn.
Dáhùn sí àhesọ pẹ̀lú ẹ̀rí, dípò kí wọ́n kan sọ pé “irọ́ ni.” Bí ìsọfúnni tuntun bá yí ohun tí a mọ̀ padà, ṣàlàyé ìdí tí ìmọ̀ràn tuntun fi yàtọ̀.
Lo àwọn ènìyàn àti ikanni tí àwùjọ gbẹ́kẹ̀ lé, bí àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ ìlera, olórí àwùjọ, olórí ẹ̀sìn, redio, WhatsApp, àti àwọn ìpàdé àdúgbò.
Lo èdè tó rọrùn àti ìmọ̀ràn tó ṣeé ṣe. Fún àwọn ènìyàn ní ohun tí wọ́n lè ṣe láti dáàbò bo ara wọn, àwọn àmì tí wọ́n yẹ kí wọ́n ṣọ́ra fún, àti ibi tí wọ́n ti lè gba ìtọ́jú.
Ṣí ọ̀nà fún ìbéèrè àti ìdáhùn. Ìbánisọ̀rọ̀ yẹ kí ó jẹ́ ọ̀nà méjì, kí àwọn aráàlú lè béèrè ìbéèrè, jabo àhesọ, tàbí sọ ohun tí wọ́n ń bẹ̀rù.
Yẹra fún ẹ̀gàn, ìdẹruba, àti fífi ẹ̀sùn kan ẹgbẹ́ kan. Irú èyí lè ba ìgbẹ́kẹ̀lé jẹ́, kí ó sì mú kí àwọn ènìyàn fi àìsàn pamọ́ tàbí kọ ìtọ́jú.

Ìlànà yìí bá àwọn ìmọ̀ràn WHO Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE) mu, èyí tó tẹnumọ́ ìsọfúnni tó yarayara, tó jẹ́ òtítọ́, gbigbọ́ ohun tí àwùjọ ń sọ, àti fífi àwọn olùgbé kópa nínú ìdáhùn sí ìbúrẹ́kẹ́ àrùn.

Nígbà ìbúrẹ́kẹ́ àrùn onígbà méjì tí a ti fìdí rẹ̀ múlẹ̀, ẹgbẹ́ ìlera àwùjọ yẹ kí ó dáhùn sí àwọn àhesọ ní kíákíá, ní gbangba, àti pẹ̀lú ìsọfúnni tó ṣe kedere. Kí wọ́n má ṣe kọ àwọn ìbéèrè àwọn aráàlú sílẹ̀ tàbí dá àwọn tó ń ṣàníyàn lẹ́bi.

Jẹ́wọ́ àníyàn àwọn ènìyàn. Sọ pé ó bófin mu kí àwọn aráàlú fẹ́ mọ iye àwọn ọ̀ràn àti àwọn ikú tó ṣẹlẹ̀.
Tẹ̀jáde ìṣirò tó jẹ́ tuntun ní gbogbo ìgbà. Yà àwọn ọ̀ràn tí a ti fìdí múlẹ̀ sọ́tọ̀ kúrò lọ́dọ̀ àwọn tí a ṣì ń ṣàyẹ̀wò, kí wọ́n sì fi ọjọ́ àti àsìkò ìmúdójúìwọ̀n hàn.
Ṣàlàyé bí a ṣe ń gba data náà. Bí ìṣirò bá yí padà nítorí àbájáde àyẹ̀wò tuntun, ìforúkọsílẹ̀ tuntun, tàbí àtúnṣe data, sọ ìdí náà ní kedere.
Sọ ohun tí a mọ̀ àti ohun tí a kò tíì mọ̀ dájú. Má ṣe fi àfojúsùn tàbí ìròyìn tí a kò tíì jẹ́rìí sí hàn bí òtítọ́.
Dáhùn sí àhesọ pẹ̀lú ẹ̀rí, kì í ṣe pẹ̀lú ìbínú. Bí ìròyìn WhatsApp kan bá jẹ́ àìtọ́, ṣàlàyé ohun tó tọ́ àti bí a ṣe mọ̀ ọ́.
Lo àwọn ikanni tí àwùjọ ń lò, bí WhatsApp, redio, ìpàdé àdúgbò, àwọn olórí ẹ̀sìn, olórí àwùjọ, àti àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ ìlera tí àwọn ènìyàn gbẹ́kẹ̀ lé.
Ṣí ọ̀nà fún ìbéèrè àti ìdáhùn. Kí àwọn ènìyàn mọ ibi tí wọ́n ti lè béèrè ìbéèrè, jabo àhesọ, tàbí jabo ẹni tó ń fi àmì àìsàn hàn.
Má ṣe fi ẹ̀gàn kàn àwọn aláìsàn tàbí ìdílé wọn. Ẹ̀gàn lè mú kí àwọn ènìyàn fi àìsàn pamọ́ tàbí pẹ́ kí wọ́n tó wá ìtọ́jú.

Ní gbogbo ìmúdójúìwọ̀n, ẹgbẹ́ ìlera yẹ kí ó tún fún àwọn olùgbé ní ìtọ́sọ́nà tó rọrùn láti tẹ̀lé:

Mu omi tó dájú pé ó mọ́. Bí ààbò omi kò bá dájú, ṣe é síse tàbí tọ́jú rẹ̀ gẹ́gẹ́ bí ìtọ́sọ́nà àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ ìlera.
Fọ ọwọ́ dáadáa pẹ̀lú ọṣẹ àti omi, pàápàá lẹ́yìn lílo ilé ìgbọ̀nsẹ̀ àti kí a tó se oúnjẹ tàbí jẹun.
Jẹ oúnjẹ tó jinna dáadáa, kí o sì dáàbò bo oúnjẹ àti omi kúrò lọ́wọ́ ìdọ̀tí.
Lo ilé ìgbọ̀nsẹ̀ tó yẹ, kí ìgbẹ́ má bà a wọ orísun omi.
Ẹnikẹ́ni tó ní ìgbẹ́ olómi púpọ̀ yẹ kí ó bẹ̀rẹ̀ ORS kíákíá, kí ó sì lọ gba ìtọ́jú ìlera.
Bí ẹni náà kò bá lè mu omi, ó ń dákú, ito rẹ̀ dín kù gan-an, tàbí ó ń fi àmì pé ara rẹ̀ ti gbẹ gidigidi hàn, ó nílò ìtọ́jú pajawiri.

Ohun tó ṣe pàtàkì jù ni pé ẹgbẹ́ ìlera má ṣe kan béèrè fún ìgbẹ́kẹ̀lé. Kí wọ́n kọ́ ọ́ nípasẹ̀ ìṣípayá, ìmúdójúìwọ̀n tó ṣe deede, ìdáhùn sí àhesọ pẹ̀lú ẹ̀rí, àti ìtọ́sọ́nà tó wúlò fún àwọn ènìyàn.

Àwọn Ọ̀nà Tí Àwọn Ìpolongo Nípa Ìlera Àwùjọ Ṣe Lè Kojú Àwọn Àhesọ Nígbà Ìbúrẹ́kẹ́ Àrùn

Báwo ni ó ṣe yẹ kí àwọn ìpolongo oòduá ṣe lè ní agbára láti ṣẹ́gun àwọn ìlànà tó wù àwọn aláìgbàmọ́ ní àkókò ìbúrẹ́kẹ́ àrùn tó ń yí ènìyàn lóko?

1. Íṣẹ̀dá Àǹfààní pẹ̀lú Ìmọ̀ Àìsí

Àwọn ìpolongo tó dáa gbọdọ̀ pèsè àlàyé tó tẹ́ríbà àti tó gbẹ̀ẹ̀ láti ara àwọn ifẹ́ nílórí:

Àṣìsẹ àrùn (àwọn ìyẹ nígbà àyípadà, bíi ifẹ́ tó wà nínú ètè tàbí òrísun gbogbo àra)
Ìkẹ́kọ̀ọ́ nípa ọ̀nà isẹ̀dá (báwo ní àrùn ṣe ń yíradà, àwọn ohun tó ṣe é búburú, àwọn ìkẹ́kọ̀ọ́ ijù)
Ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ lílo ìgbóhùn àrùn (irísí, ìgbà tó yẹ, àwọn iṣiṣẹ́ ìdí àti àdánimọ̀)

Ó ṣe pàtàkì láti fihàn pé àwọn ìpolongo tó wà nínú àwùjọ jẹ́ ẹ̀rí ìmọ̀ẹ́ẹ̀ tó bẹ̀ẹ̀rẹ̀ lórí àwọn ìjìnlẹ̀ ìwádìí.

2. Òǹkà Ìbílogun Tó Ní Àwọn Àdánimọ̀

Nígbà tó bá di pé ìpolongo ṣe kíìkìlì àrùn tàbí ìwọ̀ sànná àrùn, gbọdọ̀ jẹ́ pé:

Àwọn àkìyèsí àìrọ̀ ní tètè — ẹnìkan náà gbọdọ̀ rò sí ọ̀kan tó jẹ́ olù àwọ̀ (olù ìrànwọ́ ilé ẹ̀kọ́), ní ìbadandun àìlábojú
Pàtàkì àìtóí orísun àwọn ìlànà àrùn — ṣíṣe ìwádìí sátà àwọn àrùn wà nínú ilẹ̀ kọ̀ọ̀kan, kàkà jẹ́ pé ìjíntí aláìfọwọ́sọ yóò péwọ́ ní tẹ̀ẹ́ lórí àwọn ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ tó àìrọ̀
Àkópa nípa àwọn ohun ẹ̀kọ́ — láti ijẹ́, ọ̀bẹ̀, rírú iṣẹ̀, àti àwọn ìwọ̀ ìgòjúmọ̀
3. Àkọsọ̀ Tó Ṣẹ́gun Àìfẹ́ Ìgbélọ̀

Ìpolongo nípa ìlera àwùjọ tó jẹ́ ẹ̀rí ìmọ̀ẹ́ẹ̀ gbọdọ̀:

Rí ẹ̀rí àìsí — kí ó lè gba àwọn aláìgbàmọ́ lénu nípá àwọn àkìyèsí tó yẹ
Rí ẹ̀rí àlàyé — kí ó lè tẹ̀jú pé àwọn ìlànà àrùn ní àǹfààní, ní dè àǹfààní orísun
Rí ẹ̀rí ìṣẹ̀dá — kí ó lè dáa fún gbogbo àwọn ohun ẹ̀kọ́

Àìníìfọwọ́sọ, àǹfààní aláìjẹ́, àti àìmọ̀ ẹ̀rí jẹ́ àwọn ohun tó máa fà ilé àwọn ìwọ̀.

Àlàyé tó díẹ̀: Nígbà tó bá wàyé ìbúrẹ́kẹ́ àrùn, àwọn aláìgbàmọ́ ń fẹ́ oríṣìríṣì ìkẹ́kọ̀ọ́ àti ìpalà tó ní àìsí. Àwọn ìpolongo oòduá jẹ́ àkópa pàtàkì nítorí pé wọ́n ní ìmọ̀ ẹ̀kọ́ tó ìbádúrà àti wọ́n pé ní òtítọ́ àwọn aláìgbàmọ́ sábà.

Báwo Ni Àwọn Ìpolongo Ìlera Àwùjọ Ṣe Lè Kojú Àwọn Àhesọ Nígbà Ìbúrẹ́kẹ́ Àrùn Tó Ń Ràn Ní Àkókò Kan
Kí Nìdí Tí Àhesọ Fi Jẹ́ Ọ̀ràn Tó Ṣe Pàtàkì Tí A Kò Gbọ́dọ̀ Fojú Fo

Àhesọ nígbà ìbúrẹ́kẹ́ àrùn kì í ṣe ọ̀rọ̀ ẹnu lásán. Wọ́n ń ṣiṣẹ́ gẹ́gẹ́ bí àlàyé mìíràn tó ń bá àlàyé tó tọ́ jà, wọ́n sì máa ń tàn kálẹ̀ nípasẹ̀ àwọn ìbáṣepọ̀ àdúgbò kan náà tí àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ ìlera gbọ́dọ̀ lò. Nígbà tí àhesọ bá ń kálẹ̀ tí ẹnikẹ́ni kò sì dáhùn sí wọn, wọ́n máa ń mú kí ènìyàn kọ ìtọ́jú, kọlu àwọn oṣiṣẹ́ ìlera, sá kúrò nínú ààyè ìpamọ́, wọ́n sì máa ń tẹ̀síwájú àwọn ìwà ewu tí ó ń tàn àrùn kálẹ̀.

Ẹ̀rí tí a ti ní lórí èyí wà kedere. Nígbà Ebola ní Ìwọ̀ Oòrùn Áfríkà (2014–2016), àhesọ pé àwọn ilé ìtọ́jú ń pa ènìyàn mú kí àwọn ará àdúgbò kọlu àwọn oṣiṣẹ́ ìlera, wọ́n sì fi àwọn ẹbí wọn tí wọ́n ń ṣàìsàn pamọ́. Nígbà Ebola ní Orílẹ̀-èdè Olómìnira Kọ́ńgò (DRC, 2018–2020), àìgbàgbọ́ àti ìmọ̀ àṣìṣe fa fífi ẹ̀yìn tì gbogbo ìgbésẹ̀ ìlera. Nígbà COVID-19, ìmọ̀ àṣìṣe tàn kálẹ̀ jákèjádò ayé, ó mú kí ènìyàn kọ àjẹsára, wọ́n sì ń lo àwọn ọ̀nà ìtọ́jú olóró tí kò fi ẹsẹ̀ múlẹ̀. Nítorí gbogbo àwọn ìrírí wọ̀nyí, WHO gbé ètò ìṣàkóso ìmọ̀ àṣìṣe (infodemic management framework) kalẹ̀ láti ọdún 2020, tó ń ṣe ìtọ́jú ìmọ̀ àṣìṣe gẹ́gẹ́ bí ewu tó lè fi wé àrùn fúnra rẹ̀.

Tí a bá fi àhesọ sílẹ̀, kì yóò parẹ́ fúnra rẹ̀. Yóò kún ibi tí ìmọ̀ tó tọ́ bá yẹ kí ó wà, bí ó sì bá pẹ́ tó, yóò di apá kan ohun tí àwùjọ gbà gbọ́, yóò sì di ohun tó ṣòro láti yọ kúrò.

Àwọn Ìpìlẹ̀ Pàtàkì Tí Ó Yẹ Kí Ó Darí Ìdáhùn Sí Àhesọ

Gbà pé àhesọ náà wà kí o tó ṣàtúnṣe rẹ̀. Ìwádìí nínú ìbánisọ̀rọ̀ ìlera, pẹ̀lú ohun tí WHO fi sínú ìtọ́sọ́nà wọn lórí Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE), fi hàn pé ènìyàn nílò láti gbọ́ pé a ti mọ àníyàn wọn ṣáájú kí wọ́n tó ṣí ọkàn láti gbọ́ àlàyé mìíràn. Tí ìpolongo bá fò tààrà lọ sí àtúnṣe láì kọ́kọ́ pe ìgbàgbọ́ tí ó ń kálẹ̀ ní orúkọ, àwọn ènìyàn tí wọ́n gbà àhesọ náà gbọ́ kì yóò nímọ̀lára pé a ń bá wọn sọ̀rọ̀. Ọ̀nà tó tọ́ ni pé: kọ́kọ́ sọ ohun tí wọ́n ń sọ kálẹ̀, gbà pé ó ní ìdí tí ó fi lè dà bí ohun tó jẹ́ òótọ́ tàbí ìdí tí ó fi ń yọ ènìyàn lẹ́nu, lẹ́yìn náà pèsè àtúnṣe pẹ̀lú ẹ̀rí tí ó fi ẹsẹ̀ múlẹ̀.

Ṣùgbọ́n a gbọ́dọ̀ ṣe èyí pẹ̀lú ìṣọ́ra. Tí a bá tún ọ̀rọ̀ èké náà sọ ní ìgbà púpọ̀ jù tàbí fi sí ipò àkọ́kọ́, a lè mú kí ènìyàn rántí irọ́ náà ju òótọ́ lọ láìmọ̀. Àtúnṣe náà gbọ́dọ̀ gba àyè tó pọ̀ jù, tẹnu mọ́ ọn jù, a sì gbọ́dọ̀ tún un sọ ní ìgbà tó pọ̀ jù àhesọ náà lọ. Ìwádìí nínú ẹ̀kọ́ ọpọlọ lórí ohun tí wọ́n ń pè ní "continued influence effect" ṣe àtìlẹ́yìn fún ọ̀nà yìí. Òfin ìṣe ni pé: fi òótọ́ ṣáájú, lo àhesọ gẹ́gẹ́ bí àmì ìtọ́kasí, ṣùgbọ́n má ṣe jẹ́ kí àhesọ jẹ́ ohun tó tóbi jù nínú ìrántí ènìyàn.

Pèsè àlàyé tó dára, má ṣe kan sé. Láti kan sọ pé "ìyẹn kì í ṣe òótọ́" jẹ́ ọ̀kan lára àwọn ọ̀nà àtúnṣe tí kò mu iṣẹ́ ṣe jù lọ. Ènìyàn gbà àhesọ gbọ́ nítorí pé àhesọ náà pèsè àlàyé fún ohun tí wọ́n ń rí tàbí ohun tí wọ́n bẹ̀rù. Láti yọ àhesọ kúrò nínú ọkàn ènìyàn, o nílò láti fún wọn ní àlàyé mìíràn tí ó ṣàlàyé ohun kan náà tí wọ́n ń rí.

Fún àpẹẹrẹ, tí àhesọ bá jẹ́ pé "ìjọba dá àrùn yìí láti fi ṣàkóso wa," láti kan sọ pé "rárá, ìjọba kò ṣe bẹ́ẹ̀" dáhùn sí ọ̀rọ̀ náà ṣùgbọ́n kò dáhùn sí àìgbàgbọ́ tí ó mú kí ènìyàn gbà á gbọ́ ní àkọ́kọ́. Ọ̀rọ̀ tó dára jù yóò ṣàlàyé ohun tí sáyẹ́nsì mọ̀ gan-an nípa ibi tí àrùn náà ti wá, ẹ̀rí wo ni ó ṣe àtìlẹ́yìn fún àlàyé yẹn, ohun tí ìjọba ń ṣe gan-an nínú ìdáhùn, yóò sì gbà pé àìgbàgbọ́ nínú ìjọba ní àwọn ìdí tí ó fi ẹsẹ̀ múlẹ̀ nínú ìtàn. O ń fi ìtàn tuntun tó jẹ́ òótọ́ rọ́pò ìtàn àtijọ́, o kì í kan pa ìtàn àtijọ́ rẹ́.

Ri dájú pé oníṣẹ́ tó tọ́ ń gbé ọ̀rọ̀ náà lọ nípasẹ̀ ọ̀nà tó tọ́. Àtúnṣe tó tọ́ tí ẹ̀ka ìlera bá fi jáde nípasẹ̀ àpéjọ àwọn oníròyìn kì yóò dé àwọn àdúgbò tí kò gbẹ́kẹ̀lé àwọn àjọ ìjọba, tí wọ́n sì ń gba ìmọ̀ wọn nípasẹ̀ àwọn aṣáájú ìjọsìn, ojà, ẹgbẹ́ WhatsApp, tàbí rédíò àdúgbò. Ìtọ́sọ́nà àdáhùn-sí-àhesọ WHO àti CDC máa ń tẹnu mọ́ pé a gbọ́dọ̀ wá àwọn ènìyàn tí àwùjọ gbẹ́kẹ̀lé, fún àwọn ènìyàn wọ̀nyẹn ní ìmọ̀ tó tọ́, a sì gbọ́dọ̀ ṣe àtìlẹ́yìn fún wọn láti fi ọ̀rọ̀ tiwọn jẹ́ ṣe àtúnṣe nípasẹ̀ àwọn ọ̀nà tí àwọn ènìyàn wọn ń lò gan-an.

Àwọn ènìyàn tí wọ́n ti ṣiṣẹ́ dáadáa gẹ́gẹ́ bí oníṣẹ́ tí àdúgbò gbẹ́kẹ̀lé nínú àwọn ìdáhùn àjàkálẹ̀ àrùn tí a ti ṣàkọsílẹ̀ pẹ̀lú àwọn oṣiṣẹ́ ìlera àdúgbò, àwọn pásítọ̀ àti àwọn imámù, àwọn baálẹ̀ àti ọba, àwọn olùkọ́, àti àwọn olùgbéròyìn rédíò àdúgbò. Ohun tó ṣe pàtàkì ni pé àdúgbò ti gbẹ́kẹ̀lé ènìyàn yìí tẹ́lẹ̀. Ìgbẹ́kẹ̀lé kì í ṣe ohun tí a lè dá sílẹ̀ lójijì nígbà pàjáwìrì. Ó dá lórí àwọn ìbáṣepọ̀ tí ó ti wà tẹ́lẹ̀.

Dáhùn ní kíákíá. Àhesọ máa ń le gan-an ní kíákíá. Àhesọ tí ó bá ń kálẹ̀ fún ọjọ́ tàbí ọ̀sẹ̀ láì sí àtúnṣe yóò di apá kan ìmọ̀ tí àdúgbò pín jọ, yóò sì di ohun tó ṣòro púpọ̀ láti yí padà. Ètò RCCE ti WHO àti àwòṣe CERC ti CDC méjèèjì tẹnu mọ́ ọn pé ìyára ìdáhùn àkọ́kọ́ ṣe pàtàkì, kódà nígbà tí ìmọ̀ kò tíì pé.

Láti sọ pé "a ti gbọ́ àníyàn yìí, èyí ni ohun tí a mọ̀ títí di ìsinsin yìí, a ó sì ṣàlàyé si i bí a bá fi ẹ̀rí rẹ̀ múlẹ̀" dára jù láti dákẹ́ títí tí o fi ní ìmọ̀ tó pé, nígbà tí àhesọ ń tàn kálẹ̀ láìsí ìdáhùn.

Lo èdè àti ọ̀nà tí àdúgbò ń bá ara wọn sọ̀rọ̀. Ọ̀rọ̀ tí wọ́n kọ ní èdè ìjọba, ọ̀rọ̀ ìmọ̀ ìjìnlẹ̀, tàbí èdè ọ́fíìsì máa ń gba ẹ̀gbẹ́ etí àwọn ènìyàn tí ìdààmú bá ń ṣe kọjá láì wọ inú wọn. Àtúnṣe àhesọ tó munadoko máa ń lo ọ̀nà tí àdúgbò ń bá ara wọn sọ̀rọ̀, ó máa ń tọ́ka sí ìrírí àdúgbò, ó sì máa ń ṣàlàyé nǹkan ní ọ̀nà tí ó so pọ̀ mọ́ ohun tí ènìyàn ti mọ̀ tẹ́lẹ̀.

Èyí kì í ṣe nítorí fífún ni ní rọrùn fún ara rẹ̀. Ó jẹ́ ìmọ̀ pé ìmọ̀ gbọ́dọ̀ lè wọ inú ènìyàn lábẹ́ ìpò ìbẹ̀rù, ìdàrúdàpọ̀, àti ọ̀rọ̀ oríṣiríṣi tó ń bá ara wọn jà. Nínú àwọn àdúgbò tí wọ́n ń sọ èdè oríṣiríṣi, àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ nílò láti jẹ́ ṣíṣe ní èdè kọ̀ọ̀kan, kì í ṣe ìtumọ̀ lásán láti inú ọ̀rọ̀ ìpilẹ̀ kan. A nílò láti ṣe àtúnṣe ọ̀rọ̀ náà kí ó bá ọ̀nà tí àwùjọ èdè kọ̀ọ̀kan ṣe ń bá ara wọn sọ̀rọ̀ àti bí wọ́n ṣe ń ronú mu.

Ètò Ìṣàkóso Àhesọ Gẹ́gẹ́ Bí Iṣẹ́ Tí Ó Ń Tẹ̀síwájú, Kì Í Ṣe Ohun Ẹ̀ẹ̀kan

Fi ètò ìṣọ́ àhesọ kalẹ̀. Iṣẹ́ ìbánisọ̀rọ̀ àjàkálẹ̀ àrùn tó dára kò gbọ́dọ̀ dúró títí àhesọ yóò fi fa ìpalára tó hàn ṣáájú kí wọ́n tó dáhùn. Wọ́n gbọ́dọ̀ máa ṣọ́ ohun tí àdúgbò ń sọ lọ́wọ́ nípasẹ̀ ìtẹ̀tí sí ojú ìtàkùn àwùjọ (social media), ìròyìn láti ọ̀dọ̀ àwọn oṣiṣẹ́ ìlera àdúgbò, ìjábọ̀ láti ọ̀dọ̀ àwọn olùtọpasẹ̀ (contact tracers), àkọsílẹ̀ ilé ìgbìmọ̀ ìpè (call-centre), àti ìbáṣepọ̀ tààrà pẹ̀lú àdúgbò. WHO, UNICEF, àti IFRC papọ̀ gbé ètò ìrísí ìdáhùn àdúgbò (community feedback mechanism) kalẹ̀ fún ìdí èyí nígbà ìdáhùn Ebola ní DRC, àwọn ètò tó jọra sì ṣiṣẹ́ nígbà COVID-19. Ohun tí wọ́n ń lépa ni láti rí àhesọ ní kíákíá, ṣe ìpín wọn gẹ́gẹ́ bí bí ewu wọn ṣe pọ̀ tó, kí wọ́n sì ṣètò ìdáhùn tí ó bá ewu mu.

Ṣe ìpín àhesọ gẹ́gẹ́ bí bí ìpalára wọn ṣe lè pọ̀ tó. Kì í ṣe gbogbo àhesọ ni ó nílò ìdáhùn kan náà. Àhesọ pé oúnjẹ kan lè dènà àrùn jẹ́ ewu kékeré, ó sì lè tó àlàyé kúkúrú. Ṣùgbọ́n àhesọ pé àwọn oṣiṣẹ́ ìlera ń tàn àrùn mọ̀ọ̀mọ̀ kálẹ̀, tàbí pé ilé ìtọ́jú ń pa àwọn aláìsàn, ìyẹn ń halẹ̀ mọ́ gbogbo ìdáhùn àti ààbò àwọn oṣiṣẹ́ ìlera. Irú àhesọ bẹ́ẹ̀ nílò àtúnṣe tó ní ìyára, tó lágbára, tó ń lọ nípasẹ̀ ọ̀nà oríṣiríṣi, pẹ̀lú ìbáṣepọ̀ tààrà pẹ̀lú àdúgbò. Tí a bá ṣe ìpín àhesọ gẹ́gẹ́ bí ewu, a lè lo ohun èlò wa níbi tí wọ́n ṣe pàtàkì jù.

Dá ọ̀nà ìdáhùn padà-wá kalẹ̀. Àtúnṣe àhesọ kì í ṣe ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ ẹ̀ẹ̀kan. Lẹ́yìn tí a ti fi ọ̀rọ̀ àtúnṣe ránṣẹ́, ẹgbẹ́ ìbánisọ̀rọ̀ gbọ́dọ̀ máa ṣọ́ bóyá àtúnṣe náà ń dé àwọn ènìyàn tí ó yẹ kí wọ́n gbọ́ ọ, bóyá wọ́n gbà á gbọ́, àti bóyá àhesọ náà ṣì wà, ti yí padà sí irú mìíràn, tàbí àhesọ tuntun ti rọ́pò rẹ̀. Ìyípo yìí ti gbígbọ́, ṣíṣe àyẹ̀wò, dídáhùn, àti ṣíṣọ́ ni ọkàn ètò ìṣàkóso ìmọ̀ àṣìṣe WHO.

Ohun Tí Àwọn Olùṣàkóso Ìbánisọ̀rọ̀ Ìlera Kò Gbọ́dọ̀ Ṣe

Má ṣe fi ẹ̀rín tàbí ẹ̀gàn bá àwọn tí wọ́n gbà àhesọ gbọ́. Ẹ̀gàn máa ń mú kí ènìyàn di àhesọ wọn mú lé koko. Àwọn ènìyàn tí wọ́n bá nímọ̀lára pé a ń fi wọ́n ṣe yẹ̀yẹ́ yóò fi agídí kọjú àtúnṣe, kì yóò dín kù. Ohun tí a ń lépa ni láti yí àyíká ìmọ̀ padà, kì í ṣe láti borí ìjiyàn tàbí fi hàn pé a gbọ́n ju wọn lọ.

Má ṣe ṣèlérí ohun tí o kò lè mú ṣẹ, má sì ṣe sọ ọ̀rọ̀ tí ó lè di irọ́ lẹ́yìn. Tí àjọ ìlera bá ṣàtúnṣe àhesọ pẹ̀lú ọ̀rọ̀ tí ó fi ìgboyà sọ tí ó sì di ohun tí kò tọ́ tàbí tí kò pé lẹ́yìn náà, ìbàjẹ́ sí ìgbẹ́kẹ̀lé wọn yóò burú, yóò sì pẹ́ tó. Ó dára láti fi hàn ní gbangba ohun tí o kò dájú jù láti fi ìgboyà irọ́ hàn. Àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ bíi "gẹ́gẹ́ bí ẹ̀rí tí a ní lọ́wọ́lọ́wọ́ báyìí" àti "a ó ṣe àtúnṣe èyí tí ìmọ̀ tuntun bá wá" máa ń dáàbò bo ìgbẹ́kẹ̀lé kódà nígbà tí ipò bá ń yí padà.

Má gbára lé àtúnṣe ẹ̀ẹ̀kan ṣoṣo. Ìwádìí nínú ẹ̀kọ́ ọpọlọ fi hàn ní ìgbà gbogbo pé àtúnṣe ẹ̀ẹ̀kan kò tó láti yọ ìgbàgbọ́ irọ́ tí ó ti fi ìdí múlẹ̀ dáadáa kúrò nínú ọkàn ènìyàn. A gbọ́dọ̀ tún àlàyé tó tọ́ sọ nípasẹ̀ ọ̀nà oríṣiríṣi, nípasẹ̀ oníṣẹ́ oríṣiríṣi, ní àkókò oríṣiríṣi. Èyí kò túmọ̀ sí pé a ń tún àhesọ sọ. Ó túmọ̀ sí pé a ń tún àlàyé tó jẹ́ òótọ́ sọ nípasẹ̀ ọ̀nà oníṣiríṣi, ohùn oníṣiríṣi, àti ipò oníṣiríṣi.

Má fi gbogbo ọ̀rọ̀ sí ẹnu àjọ kan ṣoṣo. Ọ̀rọ̀ àjọ ìjọba tàbí ẹ̀ka ìlera ní ipò rẹ̀, ṣùgbọ́n kò tó fúnra rẹ̀, ní pàtàkì ní àwọn ibi tí ènìyàn kò gbẹ́kẹ̀lé àwọn àjọ. Ìdáhùn àhesọ tó munadoko jẹ́ ohun tí a pín kálẹ̀: ó fún oníṣẹ́ oríṣiríṣi ní àwọn òótọ́ pàtàkì kan náà, ṣùgbọ́n ó jẹ́ kí ẹnìkọ̀ọ̀kan sọ̀rọ̀ ní ohùn tirẹ̀ àti nípasẹ̀ ìbáṣepọ̀ tirẹ̀ pẹ̀lú àdúgbò.

Ibi Tí Ìmọ̀ràn Yìí Ti Wá

Àwọn ìpìlẹ̀ tí ó wà lókè yìí wá láti inú ètò WHO Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE), ètò ìṣàkóso ìmọ̀ àṣìṣe WHO (tí wọ́n gbé kalẹ̀ láti ọdún 2020), ìwé àfọwọ́kọ CDC Crisis and Emergency Risk Communication (CERC), àwọn àyẹ̀wò tí a ti tẹ̀ jáde lórí ìbáṣepọ̀ àdúgbò nígbà àjàkálẹ̀ Ebola ní Ìwọ̀ Oòrùn Áfríkà 2014–2016 àti àjàkálẹ̀ Ebola DRC 2018–2020, àti àwọn ìwé ìmọ̀ ìjìnlẹ̀ lórí ìbánisọ̀rọ̀ ìlera àti ẹ̀kọ́ ọpọlọ lórí àtúnṣe ìmọ̀ àṣìṣe. Àwọn ẹ̀ka ìwádìí pàtàkì tí ó ṣe àfikún pẹ̀lú continued influence effect (Johnson àti Seifert, 1994, àti iṣẹ́ tí ó tẹ̀lé e), ìwé àyẹ̀wò ìtújáde (debunking literature) tí Lewandowsky àti àwọn ẹlẹgbẹ́ rẹ̀ ṣe (2012, "Misinformation and Its Correction"), àti àwọn ìṣirò pápá lórí àwọn ètò ìrísí ìdáhùn àdúgbò nípasẹ̀ WHO, UNICEF, àti IFRC.

Àwọn ìlànà iṣẹ́ pàtó yàtọ̀ láti orílẹ̀-èdè dé orílẹ̀-èdè àti láti àjàkálẹ̀ àrùn dé àjàkálẹ̀ àrùn. Àwọn àjọ ìlera orílẹ̀-èdè àti àwọn ọ́fíìsì WHO ní orílẹ̀-èdè kọ̀ọ̀kan máa ń tọ́jú ìtọ́sọ́nà tí ó bá ipò wọn mu tí a gbọ́dọ̀ yẹ̀ wò ṣáájú ìmúṣẹ.

Bí Àwọn Ìpolongo Ìlera Àwùjọ Ṣe Lè Kojú Àwọn Àhesọ Nígbà Ìbúrẹ́kẹ́ Àrùn

Àwọn àhesọ jẹ́ ọ̀kan lára àwọn ìdojúkọ tó pọ̀ jù lọ nígbà tí àrùn bá ń ránni káàkiri. Tí a kò bá kojú wọn dáadáa, wọ́n lè ba iṣẹ́ ìdènà àrùn jẹ́ gidigidi. Èyí ni àwọn ọ̀nà pàtàkì tí àwọn ìpolongo ìlera lè gbà:

1. Ṣe àkíyèsí àwọn àhesọ kí o sì mọ̀ wọ́n

Kí o tó lè kojú àhesọ, o gbọ́dọ̀ mọ̀ pé wọ́n wà. Àwọn olùṣètọ́jú ìlera gbọ́dọ̀:

Máa tẹ́tí sí ohun tí àwọn ènìyàn ń sọ ní ọjà, ní ilé ìjọsìn, àti lórí WhatsApp àti àwọn ojú-ìtàkùn àjọlò mìíràn.
Kó àwọn àhesọ jọ, ṣàkójọ wọn, kí o sì mọ èyí tó ń tàn káàkiri jù lọ.
Ṣe ìdámọ̀ ohun tí ń mú àwọn àhesọ wọ̀nyí dàgbà — ṣé ìbẹ̀rù ni, ṣé àìgbàgbọ́ nínú ìjọba ni, tàbí àìlóye ni?
2. Máa sọ òtítọ́ ní gbangba, kí o sì ṣe é ní kíákíá

Ìdákẹ́rọ́rọ́ ń fún àhesọ ní agbára. Dípò kí o pa àhesọ tì tàbí kí o ṣe bí ẹni pé kò sí, àwọn ọ̀gá ìlera gbọ́dọ̀:

Dáhùn sí àwọn àhesọ ní tààràtà. Fún àpẹẹrẹ: "A ti gbọ́ pé àwọn ènìyàn ń sọ pé oogun yìí ń pa ènìyàn — jẹ́ kí a sọ ohun tí a mọ̀ gan-an fún yín..."
Ṣàlàyé ìdí tí àwọn nọ́mbà tàbí ìròyìn ṣe lè yàtọ̀ sí ohun tí àwọn ènìyàn rí ní àdúgbò wọn. Fún àpẹẹrẹ, tí àwọn ènìyàn bá rí ọ̀pọ̀ aláìsàn ṣùgbọ́n ìjọba sọ pé díẹ̀ ni, ṣàlàyé bí ìkà-ènìyàn ṣe ń ṣiṣẹ́, dípò kí o kàn sọ pé "ẹ má dààmú."
Máa sọ ohun tí o mọ̀ àti ohun tí o kò tíì mọ̀. Ìgboyà láti sọ pé "a kò tíì mọ̀ ẹ̀yà àrùn yìí pátápátá, ṣùgbọ́n ohun tí a mọ̀ ni pé..." ń mú ìgbẹ́kẹ̀lé pọ̀ sí i ju ìfihàn bí ẹni pé o mọ gbogbo nǹkan lọ.
3. Lo àwọn ènìyàn tí àwùjọ gbẹ́kẹ̀lé

Nínú ọ̀pọ̀ àwùjọ, àwọn ènìyàn kì í gbàgbọ́ ìjọba tàbí àwọn dókítà tí wọ́n kò mọ̀. Àwọn ènìyàn tí wọ́n gbẹ́kẹ̀lé jù lọ ni:

Àwọn aṣáájú ìbílẹ̀ àti àwọn olórí ẹ̀sìn — Baálẹ̀, Imam, Pásítọ̀ — tí wọ́n bá sọ pé àrùn yìí jẹ́ gidi, àwọn ènìyàn á gbọ́.
Àwọn aláìsàn tí wọ́n ti rí ìwòsàn — Ẹ̀rí ẹni tí ó ti ṣàìsàn tí ó sì gbádùn ni ẹ̀rí tó lágbára jù lọ. "Èmi náà rò pé iró ni, ṣùgbọ́n mo lọ ilé ìwòsàn, wọ́n tọ́jú mi, mo sì rí ìwòsàn" — ọ̀rọ̀ bẹ́ẹ̀ lágbára ju ìpolongo ìjọba lọ.
Àwọn oṣiṣẹ́ ìlera àdúgbò (Community Health Extension Workers) — wọ́n jẹ́ ará ìlú, wọ́n sì mọ èdè àti àṣà ibẹ̀.
4. Sọ̀rọ̀ ní èdè tí àwọn ènìyàn lóye

Èyí kì í ṣe ìtumọ̀ Gẹ̀ẹ́sì nìkan. Ó túmọ̀ sí pé:

Lo èdè tí àwọn ènìyàn ń sọ lójoojúmọ́ — Yorùbá, Igbo, Pidgin, tàbí èdè ìbílẹ̀ mìíràn — kì í ṣe èdè tí wọ́n kà nínú ìwé nìkan.
Lo àpèjúwe àti ọ̀rọ̀ àkànlò tí ó yẹ fún àṣà ibẹ̀.
Àhesọ máa ń tàn ní èdè ìbílẹ̀; tí ìdáhùn rẹ bá wà ní Gẹ̀ẹ́sì nìkan, kò ní dé ọ̀dọ̀ àwọn ènìyàn tí àhesọ náà ti dé.
5. Sọ ohun tí àwọn ènìyàn lè ṣe ní pàtó

Àhesọ máa ń gbilẹ̀ nígbà tí àwọn ènìyàn bá ní ìrùkèrúdò tí wọ́n kò sì mọ ohun tí wọ́n lè ṣe. Dípò kí o kàn sọ pé "ẹ lọ ilé ìwòsàn," sọ fún wọn ní pàtó pàtó:

Ilé ìwòsàn wo ni? Ó wà ní bo?
Owó mélòó ni? Tàbí ọ̀fẹ́ ni?
Kí ni àmì àrùn tí wọ́n gbọ́dọ̀ wá ní kíákíá?
Kí ni wọ́n lè ṣe ní ilé kí wọ́n tó dé ilé ìwòsàn?
6. Má ṣe bú àwọn ènìyàn tàbí fi wọ́n ṣe yẹ̀yẹ́

Ọ̀nà tó burú jù lọ láti kojú àhesọ ni láti sọ pé àwọn tó gbà á gbọ́ jẹ́ aṣiwèrè tàbí aláìmọ̀kan. Èyí á mú kí wọ́n dì mú àhesọ náà gan-an, nítorí pé:

Ẹni tí wọ́n bú kì í yí èrò rẹ̀ padà; ó máa ń dìmú ohun tó ti gbàgbọ́ tẹ́lẹ̀.
Ọ̀pọ̀ àhesọ ní ìdí — bóyá ìrírí búburú tí àwọn ènìyàn ti rí pẹ̀lú àwọn ilé ìwòsàn, tàbí ìtàn tí ó ti pẹ́ nínú àwùjọ.
Dípò kí o bú, gbìyànjú láti lóye ìdí tí wọ́n fi gbà àhesọ náà gbọ́, kí o sì bá wọn sọ̀rọ̀ láti ibẹ̀.
7. Lo àwọn ọ̀nà ìbánisọ̀rọ̀ oríṣiríṣi

Kì í ṣe gbogbo ènìyàn ló ń lo WhatsApp. Kì í ṣe gbogbo ènìyàn ló ń gbọ́ rédíò. Nítorí náà:

Lo rédíò fún àwọn àgbàlagbà àti àwọn tó wà ní ìgbèríko.
Lo WhatsApp àti àwọn ojú-ìtàkùn àjọlò fún àwọn ọ̀dọ́.
Lo ìpolongo ní ọjà àti ní ibi ìpàdé àwùjọ fún àwọn tí kò sí lórí ayélujára.
Lo àwọn megaphone àti àwọn akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ ìlera tí wọ́n máa ń lọ ilé-dé-ilé.

Ní àkótán, ohun tó ṣe pàtàkì jù lọ ni pé: àhesọ kì í ṣe ìṣòro ìmọ̀ nìkan — ó jẹ́ ìṣòro ìgbẹ́kẹ̀lé. Tí àwọn ènìyàn kò bá gbẹ́kẹ̀lé ẹni tó ń sọ̀rọ̀, wọn kò ní gbà ohun tó sọ, bó tilẹ̀ jẹ́ pé òtítọ́ ni. Nítorí náà, ìkọ́lé ìgbẹ́kẹ̀lé — nípasẹ̀ gbangba, ìtẹ́tí sí àwùjọ, àti ọ̀wọ̀ fún àwọn ènìyàn — ni ìpìlẹ̀ gbogbo iṣẹ́ ìdènà àhesọ.

Nígbà ìbúrẹ́kẹ́ àrùn tó ń ranni, ó ṣe pàtàkì kí àwọn ìpolongo ìlera àwùjọ kojú àwọn àhesọ ní kíákíá àti pẹ̀lú ìmọ̀ tó péye, nítorí àhesọ lè mú kí àwọn ènìyàn ṣe àwọn ìpinnu tí kò dára fún ìlera wọn.

Àwọn ìpolongo bẹ́ẹ̀ lè ṣe èyí nípa:

Pípèsè ìmọ̀ tó tọ́ àti tó ṣe kedere nípa àrùn náà, bí ó ṣe ń tàn, àti bí a ṣe lè dáàbò bo ara ẹni.
Ṣíṣe àtúnṣe àwọn àhesọ tààràtà, nípa ṣàlàyé ohun tí kò tọ́ àti ohun tí ẹ̀rí ìmọ̀ sáyẹ́ǹsì fìdí múlẹ̀.
Lílo èdè tí ènìyàn lóye, pẹ̀lú àwọn èdè agbègbè bí ó bá yẹ.
Mímú àwọn olórí àwùjọ, olórí ẹ̀sìn, àti àwọn ènìyàn tí àwùjọ gbẹ́kẹ̀ lé kópa, kí wọ́n lè ran lọ́wọ́ láti tan ìsọfúnni tó péye.
Fífún àwọn ènìyàn ní ànfàní láti béèrè ìbéèrè, kí wọ́n sì gba ìdáhùn láti ọwọ́ àwọn amòye ìlera.
Yíyẹra fún èdè tó ń dẹ́rù bá ènìyàn, kí a sì dojú kọ́ òtítọ́ àti ojútùú.

Ọ̀nà tó dára ni láti fi ọ̀wọ̀ hàn sí àwọn ènìyàn tí wọ́n gbà àhesọ náà gbọ́, kí a sì pèsè ìmọ̀ tuntun ní ọ̀nà tó rọrùn, tó dá lórí ẹ̀rí, tí kò sì ní ẹ̀gàn. Èyí máa ń jẹ́ kí àwọn ènìyàn ní ìgbọ́kànlé sí àwọn ìsọfúnni ìlera àwùjọ.

Àwọn ìgbésẹ̀ tó ṣe pàtàkì ni:

Pèsè ìsọfúnni tó péye àti tó ń ṣe àfihàn òtítọ́ ní kíákíá, kí àwọn àhesọ má bàa gba ààyè.
Ṣàlàyé ohun tí a mọ̀ àti ohun tí a kò tíì mọ̀ nípa àrùn náà ní gbangba.
Dáhùn sí àwọn àhesọ ní taara, ṣùgbọ́n pẹ̀lú ọ̀wọ̀, láì fi ẹ̀sùn kan àwọn ènìyàn tó gbà wọ́n gbọ́.

Fún àwọn ènìyàn láàyè láti béèrè ìbéèrè kí wọ́n sì gba ìdáhùn láti ọ̀dọ̀ àwọn amòye ìlera.
Yẹra fún fífi ìbẹ̀rù kún ìbẹ̀rù, kí wọ́n sì dojú kọ́ àwọn ìgbésẹ̀ tó le dáàbò bo ìlera.

Ní àfikún, àwọn ìpolongo náà yẹ kí wọ́n máa fún àwọn aráàlú ní ìtọ́sọ́nà ìlera tó ṣe kedere, bíi:

Fífọ ọwọ́ déédéé pẹ̀lú ọṣẹ àti omi.
Mímu omi tó mọ́ àti jíjẹ oúnjẹ tó mọ́.
Wíwá ìtọ́jú ìlera kíákíá tí ààmì àìsàn bá farahàn.
Títẹ̀lé ìmòràn àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ ìlera àti àwọn aláṣẹ ìlera.

Ìbánisọ̀rọ̀ tó ṣí sílẹ̀, tó ní ọ̀wọ̀, tí ó sì dá lórí ẹ̀rí lè dín agbára àwọn àhesọ kù, kí ó sì mú kí àwọn ènìyàn gbẹ́kẹ̀ lé ìsọfúnni ìlera àwùjọ.

Ozi gbasara ahụike ọha kwesịrị ịza asịrị ngwa ngwa, n’ụzọ nkwanye ùgwù, ma jiri ozi ziri ezi e nyochara. Ịkwa ndị mmadụ emo ma ọ bụ ịkatọ ha nwere ike ime ka ntụkwasị obi belata.

Ndị na-ahụ maka ahụike kwesịrị:

Buru ụzọ gee ntị: Chọpụta kpọmkwem asịrị a na-agba, ebe ọ na-agbasa, na egwu ma ọ bụ enweghị ozi kpatara ya.
Zaghachi ngwa ngwa: Dozie ozi ụgha nwere ike imerụ mmadụ tupu ọ gbasaa. Ma ekwughachila asịrị ahụ ugboro ugboro n’ụzọ ga-eme ka ọtụtụ mmadụ nụ ya.
Buru eziokwu ụzọ: Malite na ihe ndị ọrụ ahụike kwadoro, kọwaa ihe akaebe ahụ nkenke ma gwa ndị mmadụ ihe ha kwesịrị ime.
Kwupụta ihe a na-amabeghị: Kewaa ihe e kwadoro na ihe ndị ọkachamara ka na-enyocha. Kwuo oge na ebe a ga-enye ozi ọhụrụ.
Jiri ndị obodo tụkwasịrị obi: Soro ndị ọrụ ahụike mpaghara, ndị isi obodo, ndị isi okpukpe, ndị nkuzi na ndị ọzọ a tụkwasịrị obi rụkọọ ọrụ.
Jiri asụsụ dị mfe: Nye ozi n’asụsụ obodo site na redio, nzukọ obodo, ozi ekwentị, akwụkwọ mmado na ụzọ ndị ndị nwere nkwarụ nwekwara ike iji.
Nye ntụziaka bara uru: Kọwaa mgbaàmà, otú ọrịa si agbasa, ụzọ mgbochi, na ebe a ga-aga maka nyocha, ọgwụgwọ ma ọ bụ enyemaka mberede.
Kpọọ isi mmalite: Gosi ndị mmadụ ụlọ ọrụ ahụike, nọmba ekwentị, ebe nrụọrụ weebụ ma ọ bụ ụlọọgwụ ha nwere ike iji nyochaa ozi ahụ.
Mee ka ozi kwekọọ: Ụlọ ọrụ ahụike na ndị ha na ha na-arụkọ ọrụ kwesịrị ịnye otu eziokwu ahụ. Ọ bụrụ na ndụmọdụ agbanwe, ha kwesịrị ịkọwa ihe kpatara ya.
Nye ohere maka ajụjụ: Mepụta ụzọ ndị mmadụ ga-esi jụọ ajụjụ, kọọ asịrị ma nweta azịza.
Zere ịta mmadụ ụta: Ejikọtala ọrịa ahụ na agbụrụ, okpukpe, obodo, ọrụ ma ọ bụ ndị mbịarambịa. Chekwaa nzuzo ndị ọrịa.
Dozie mmejọ n’ihu ọha: Ọ bụrụ na ndị ọrụ ahụike nyere ozi na-ezughị oke ma ọ bụ nke na-ezighi ezi, ha kwesịrị ikweta ya, kọwaa ihe gbanwere ma nye ozi ziri ezi.

Usoro ozi dị mfe bụ: eziokwu e kwadoro, nkọwa dị nkenke, ihe a ga-eme, isi mmalite a pụrụ ịtụkwasị obi na oge ozi ọhụrụ ga-apụta.

Kwupụta ihe a na-amabeghị: Kewaa ihe e kwadoro na ihe ndị ọkachamara ka na-enyocha. Kwuo oge na ebe a ga-enye ozi ọhụrụ.
Jiri ndị obodo tụkwasịrị obi: Soro ndị ọrụ ahụike mpaghara, ndị isi obodo, ndị isi okpukpe, ndị nkuzi na ndị ọzọ a tụkwasịrị obi rụkọọ ọrụ.
Jiri asụsụ dị mfe: Nye ozi n’asụsụ obodo site na redio, nzukọ obodo, ozi ekwentị, akwụkwọ mmado na ụzọ ndị ndị nwere nkwarụ nwekwara ike iji.
Nye ntụziaka bara uru: Kọwaa mgbaàmà, otú ọrịa si agbasa, ụzọ mgbochi, na ebe a ga-aga maka nyocha, ọgwụgwọ ma ọ bụ enyemaka mberede.
Kpọọ isi mmalite: Gosi ndị mmadụ ụlọ ọrụ ahụike, nọmba ekwentị, ebe nrụọrụ weebụ ma ọ bụ ụlọọgwụ ha nwere ike iji nyochaa ozi ahụ.
Mee ka ozi kwekọọ: Ụlọ ọrụ ahụike na ndị ha na ha na-arụkọ ọrụ kwesịrị ịnye otu eziokwu ahụ. Ọ bụrụ na ndụmọdụ agbanwe, ha kwesịrị ịkọwa ihe kpatara ya.
Nye ohere maka ajụjụ: Mepụta ụzọ ndị mmadụ ga-esi jụọ ajụjụ, kọọ asịrị ma nweta azịza.
Zere ịta mmadụ ụta: Ejikọtala ọrịa ahụ na agbụrụ, okpukpe, obodo, ọrụ ma ọ bụ ndị mbịarambịa. Chekwaa nzuzo ndị ọrịa.
Dozie mmejọ n’ihu ọha: Ọ bụrụ na ndị ọrụ ahụike nyere ozi na-ezughị oke ma ọ bụ nke na-ezighi ezi, ha kwesịrị ikweta ya, kọwaa ihe gbanwere ma nye ozi ziri ezi.

Usoro ozi dị mfe bụ: eziokwu e kwadoro, nkọwa dị nkenke, ihe a ga-eme, isi mmalite a pụrụ ịtụkwasị obi na oge ozi ọhụrụ ga-apụta.

Otu ozi Gbasara Ahụike Ọha Ga-esi Lebara Asịrị n'Oge Ọrịa Ifufe na-Agbasa
1. Izi Mma nke Ozi Gbasara Ahụike Ọha

Mgbe ọrịa ifufe na-agba ma na-agbasa n'ebe, ozi gbasara ahụike ọha ga-ebu:

Ezi Uche nke Ọrịa

Kedu ka a si maụta ozi mgbe mmadu ji ya
Kedu ihe na-atụtụ ya, na ọnọdu ịma ya
Otu ọ si agbasa site na mmadu gaa n'ọzọ
Kedu oge ịda ịda (incubation period) na mgbe mmadu na-ewu òkè ọrịa

Azi Mma

Ịza ajụjụ ndị mmadu n'ụzọ ma-ama ama n'Igbo
Ịkọwa ihe pụrụ ịmụta uju ma ọ bụ iji mmiri na-eka asa
Ịkọwa otú ọ si elezi mmụọ n'ogbe mgbe mmadu nọ n'ọghọm
2. Kedu Ihe Ga-abụ n'Ozi a

Ọ kwesịrị ka:

Ịkọwa ihe ụkọ ọrịa — kedu ịda ịda, kedu mgbe a ga-ahụ izu, kedu oge mmadu dị mma
Ịkọwa ọnọdu na-akpali mma — ụfọdụ ihe dị mma (ọnọdu ịhụ, agbasa nke ọrịa, iru olu mmadu)
Ịkọwa kedu oge aga-akpo onye oshi — mgbe a ga-ejikọ ndị ogwu, mgbe a ga-eziga mmadu n'ụlọ ọgwu
3. Ezi Usoro maka Ozi a

N'ogbe ịgbasa ozi:

Gụzie ezi uche — mezie ka mmadu ghara ịtụ ụjụ, ma ma na-aga aba ama, o kwesịrị ka ọ rute ndị ogwu
Ịkọwa usoro nke ịzọgide ọrịa — iji mmiri ezuzo, ịza ọnụ mgbe ịkụ ọkụkụ, ịkpụ akwa mmadu nke siri ike
Ịgbasa ozi n'ụlọ — ezi ụzọ iji kpọọ ndị mmadu, ezi ụzọ iji guzobe mmadu nọ n'ụlọ ebe ha nọ
Ịkụ aka ndị ogwu — ọgbụgbụ ọrịa, kedu ndị a ga-akpọ, kedu ebe ha nọ
4. Ihe Pụrụ Ịmanya

Ozi gbasara ahụike ọha ga-abụ:

Ezi uche ma ọ bụ n'Igbo — ka mmadu ghara ịgha ụka na ọ na-agụ
Ebi ma ọ bụ n'echi echi — ọ kwesịrị ka mmadu rapụ anya site na ndụ mmadu ndị ọzọ
Nyere aka n'ụzọ ọ karị — iji ihe mma, iji mmiri akpụkpọ ụkwụ, ịkpụ akwa

Nkọwapụtara: N'oge ọrịa na-agbasa dị ka ifufe, ozi gbasara ahụike ọha ga-abụ ihe pụrụ ịmanya, ihe na-emeru eme, ma ihe na-enye mmadu obi ike ịga n'akwa ogwu. Ozi a ga-agbasa n'ụzọ ma-ama ama, site na ndị oshi, ndị ụlọ ọgwu, na ọhọ uche mmada nile.

Kedu Ka Ozi Gbasara Ahụike Ọha Ga-Esi Lebara Asịrị Na-Agba Mgbe Ọrịa Na-Efe Efe Na-Agbasa
Gịnị Mere Asịrị Ji Bụrụ Nsogbu Dị Oke Njọ Nke A Gaghị Elefu Anya

Asịrị n'oge ọrịa na-efe efe abụghị naanị okwu ọnụ efu. Ha na-arụ ọrụ dịka nkọwa ọzọ na-asọ mpi na nkọwa ziri ezi, ha na-agbasakwa site n'otu njikọ ọha ahụ nke ozi ahụike kwesịrị iji. Mgbe asịrị na-agba ma ọ dịghị onye na-azaghachi, ha na-eme ka ndị mmadụ jụ ọgwụgwọ, wakpoo ndị ọrụ ahụike, gbalaga n'ebe nkewa, ma nọgide na-eme ihe ndị dị ize ndụ nke na-agbasa ọrịa.

Nke a abụghị naanị echiche. Ihe ndị a emehụrụla n'ezie. N'oge Ebola na West Africa (2014–2016), asịrị na-ekwu na ụlọ ọgwụgwọ na-egbu ndị mmadụ mere ka ndị ama wakpoo ndị ọrụ ahụike, zoo ndị ezinụlọ ha na-arịa arịa. N'oge Ebola na DRC (2018–2020), enweghị ntụkwasị obi na ozi na-ezighị ezi gbochiri nzaghachi ahụike niile. N'oge COVID-19, ozi na-ezighị ezi gbasara ụwa niile, mee ka ndị mmadụ jụ ogwu agbọghọ nje (vaccine), were ụzọ ọgwụgwọ dị ize ndụ nke na-enweghị isi sayensị. N'ihi ahịrịụnụ ndị a niile, WHO wepụtara usoro njikwa ozi na-ezighị ezi (infodemic management framework) site na afọ 2020, na-emeso ozi na-ezighị ezi dịka ihe egwu nke nwere ike ịha nhata dịka ọrịa ahụ n'onwe ya.

Ọ bụrụ na ị hapụ asịrị, ọ gaghị efu n'onwe ya. Ọ ga-ejupụta ebe ozi ziri ezi kwesịrị ịnọ, ọ bụrụkwa na o nọọ oge, ọ ga-aghọ akụkụ nke ihe ndị ama niile kwenyere, ọ ga-esikwa ike ịwepụ ya.

Ụkpụrụ Ndị Kwesịrị Ịdụzi Nzaghachi Maka Asịrị

Kweta na asịrị ahụ dị tupu ị mezie ya. Nyocha n'ozi ahụike, gụnyere ihe WHO tinye n'ime ntụzịaka ha gbasara Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE), gosiri na ndị mmadụ kwesịrị ịnụ na a ghọtara nchegbu ha tupu ha emeghe obi ha ịnụ nkọwa ọzọ. Ọ bụrụ na ozi ahụ amalite na nzikarịta na-akpọghị nkwenye ahụ na-agba aha, ndị kwenyere n'asịrị ahụ agaghị enwe mmetụta na a na-agwa ha okwu. Ụzọ ziri ezi bụ: buru ụzọ kwuo ihe a na-ekwu n'ama, kweta na o nwere ihe mere o ji yiri ka o nwere isi maọbụ ihe mere ndị mmadụ ji nwee nchegbu, wee nye nzikarịta ahụ ziri ezi na ihe akaebe kwadoro ya.

Mana a ga-eji nlezianya eme nke a. Ọ bụrụ na ị kwughachi okwu ụgha ahụ ọtụtụ mgbe maọbụ nye ya ọnọdụ dị elu, ị nwere ike ime ka ndị mmadụ cheta ụgha ahụ karịa eziokwu ahụ n'amaghị ama. Nzikarịta ahụ ziri ezi kwesịrị inweta ohere karịa, ntesissi ike karịa, na nkwughachi karịa asịrị ahụ n'onwe ya. Nyocha n'ụdị mmụọ ọpọlọ (cognitive psychology) gbasara ihe a na-akpọ "continued influence effect" na-akwado ụzọ a. Iwu a ga-eso bụ: buru ụzọ kwuo eziokwu, jiri asịrị ahụ dịka ihe ntụaka, mana emela ka asịrị bụrụ ihe kacha pụta ìhè n'uche ndị mmadụ.

Nye nkọwa zuru oke, ejula sè naanị. Ịsị naanị "nke ahụ abụghị eziokwu" bụ otu n'ime ụzọ nzikarịta asịrị kacha adịghị arụ ọrụ. Ndị mmadụ na-ekwenye n'asịrị n'ihi na asịrị ahụ na-enye ha nkọwa maka ihe ha na-ahụ maọbụ ihe ha na-atụ egwu ya. Iji wepụ asịrị n'uche mmadụ, ị kwesịrị inye ha nkọwa ọzọ nke na-akọwa otu ihe ahụ ha na-ahụ.

Dịka ọmụmaatụ, ọ bụrụ na asịrị bụ "gọọmenti kere ọrịa a iji chịkwaa anyị," ịsị naanị "mba, gọọmenti emeghị" na-azaghachi okwu ahụ mana ọ naghị azaghachi enweghị ntụkwasị obi nke mere ka mmadụ kwee ya na mbụ. Ozi ka mma ga-akọwa ihe sayensị mara n'ezie banyere ebe ọrịa ahụ si pụta, ihe akaebe na-akwado nkọwa ahụ, ihe gọọmenti na-eme n'ezie na nzaghachi, ma kweta na enweghị ntụkwasị obi na gọọmenti nwere isi kwụ n'akụkọ ihe mere eme. Ị na-edochi otu akụkọ na akụkọ ọhụrụ nke bụ eziokwu, ị naghị ehichapu akụkọ ochie naanị.

Hụ na onye kwesịrị ekwesị na-ebu ozi ahụ site n'ụzọ kwesịrị ekwesị. Nzikarịta ziri ezi nke ụlọọrụ ahụike wepụtara site n'ọgbakọ ndị nta akụkọ agaghị eru ama ndị na-atụkwasịghị gọọmenti obi, ndị na-enweta ozi ha site n'aka ndị ndu ụka, ahịa, otu WhatsApp, maọbụ redio obodo. Ntụzịaka nzaghachi asịrị nke WHO na CDC na-arụsị ike mgbe ọbụla na a ga-achọta ndị ama na-atụkwasị obi, nye ndị ahụ ozi ziri ezi, wee kwado ha iji okwu nke ha jiri mee nzikarịta site n'ụzọ ndị ha na-eji eme ihe n'ezie.

Ndị rụrụ ọrụ nke ọma dịka ndị ozi ama na-atụkwasị obi n'oge nzaghachi ọrịa ndị e dere n'akwụkwọ gụnyere ndị ọrụ ahụike obodo, ndị ụkọchukwu na ndị imamụ, ndị eze ala, ndị nkụzi, na ndị na-agba ozi redio obodo. Ihe dị mkpa bụ na ama ahụ atụkwasịla onye a obi na mbụ. Ntụkwasị obi abụghị ihe a na-emepụta na mberede n'oge mberede. Ọ dabere na mmekọrịta ndị dị na mbụ.

Zaghachi ngwa ngwa. Asịrị na-esike ngwa ngwa. Asịrị nke na-agba ụbọchị maọbụ izu na-enweghị onye na-emezie ya ga-abanye n'ime ihe ama niile kwekọrịtara, ọ ga-esikwa ike ịgbanwe ya. Usoro RCCE nke WHO na ụdị CERC nke CDC ha abụọ na-arụsị ike na ọsọ nzaghachi mbụ dị mkpa, ọ bụladị mgbe ozi ezubeghị okè.

Ịsị "anyị anụla nchegbu a, nke a bụ ihe anyị maara ruo ugbu a, anyị ga-ekekọrịta karịa ka anyị gosipụtachara ya" ka mma karịa ịnọ jụụ ruo mgbe ị nwetara ozi zuruoke mgbe asịrị na-agbasa n'enweghị ndị na-emegide ya.

Jiri asụsụ na ụzọ ndị ama si ekwurịta okwu. Ozi e dere n'asụsụ gọọmenti, asụsụ ọkachamara, maọbụ asụsụ ọfịs na-agafe n'etiti ndị mmadụ nke nsogbu na-enyere ha nsogbu n'enweghị mmetụta. Nzikarịta asịrị nke na-arụ ọrụ na-eji ụzọ ama si ekwurịta okwu, na-atụ aka n'ahụmịhe obodo, ma na-akọwa ihe n'ụzọ jikọtara na ihe ndị mmadụ maara na mbụ.

Nke a abụghị naanị maka ime ka ihe dị mfe. Ọ bụ ịghọta na ozi ga-enwerịrị ike ịbanye n'uche ndị mmadụ n'okpuru ọnọdụ egwu, ọgba aghara, na ọtụtụ okwu ndị na-asọ mpi. N'ama ndị na-asụ asụsụ dị iche iche, ozi kwesịrị ịbụ nke e mere n'asụsụ ọbụla, ọ bụghị naanị nsụgharị site n'otu ozi mbụ. A kwesịrị ịhazi ozi ahụ ka o kwekọọ na ụzọ ama asụsụ ọbụla si ekwurịta okwu na echiche.

Usoro Njikwa Asịrị Dịka Ọrụ Na-aga N'ihu, Ọ Bụghị Ihe Otu Oge

Guzobe usoro nlekọta asịrị. Ọrụ ozi ọrịa na-efe efe dị mma ekwesịghị ichere ruo mgbe asịrị emere ihe ọjọọ a pụrụ ịhụ anya tupu ha azaghachi. Ha kwesịrị na-elekọta ihe ama na-ekwu site n'iji ntị na ngalaba ọha mmekọrịta (social media), ozi sitere n'aka ndị ọrụ ahụike obodo, akụkọ sitere n'aka ndị na-esochi ndị metụrụ onye ọrịa aka (contact tracers), ndekọ ụlọ oku ekwentị (call-centre), na mmekọrịta na ama ozugbo. WHO, UNICEF, na IFRC jikọtara aka wepụta usoro nzaghachi ama (community feedback mechanism) maka nke a n'oge nzaghachi Ebola na DRC, usoro yiri ya wee rụọkwa ọrụ n'oge COVID-19. Ebumnobi bụ ịchọta asịrị oge, kee ha dịka etu ihe egwu ha si dị, wee hazie nzaghachi dịka ọkwa egwu.

Kee asịrị dịka etu ihe ize ndụ ha pụrụ ịdị. Ọ bụghị asịrị niile chọrọ otu ụdị nzaghachi. Asịrị na-ekwu na otu nri na-egbochi ọrịa bụ ihe egwu nta, ọ pụrụ ịdị naanị mkpọsa nke ọma nkenke. Mana asịrị na-ekwu na ndị ọrụ ahụike na-agbasa ọrịa kpọmkwem, maọbụ na ụlọ ọgwụgwọ na-egbu ndị ọrịa, nke ahụ na-eyi nzaghachi ahụ niile ihe egwu na nchekwa ndị ọrụ ahụike. Ụdị asịrị dị otú ahụ chọrọ nzikarịta nke dị ngwa, siri ike, na-aga site n'ọtụtụ ụzọ, yana mmekọrịta na ama ozugbo. Ọ bụrụ na ị kee asịrị dịka etu ihe egwu ha dị, ị ga-enwe ike iji akụ gị mee ihe ebe ha kacha dị mkpa.

Mepụta usoro nzaghachi na-alaghachi azụ. Imezie asịrị abụghị ihe a na-eme otu oge. Mgbe e zigachara ozi nzikarịta, ndị ọrụ ozi kwesịrị ịnọ na-elekọta ma nzikarịta ahụ ò na-eru ndị kwesịrị ịnụ ya, ma ha ò na-ekwenye na ya, ma asịrị ahụ ò ka dị, ọ gbanwela ụdị, maọbụ asịrị ọhụrụ anọchitela anya ya. Usoro a nke ịnụ, inyocha, ịzaghachi, na ịnọ na-elekọta bụ isi ihe dị n'usoro njikwa ozi na-ezighị ezi nke WHO.

Ihe Ndị Na-ahazi Ozi Ahụike Ekwesịghị Ime

Achịla ọchị maọbụ eledala anya ndị kwenyere n'asịrị. Nlelị na-eme ka ndị mmadụ jide nkwenye ha sie ike karịa. Ndị na-enwe mmetụta na a na-eme ha ihe ọchị ga-eguzogide nzikarịta karịa, ọ bụghị na ha ga-anabata ya. Ebumnobi bụ ịgbanwe gburugburu ozi, ọ bụghị ịmeri arụmụka maọbụ igosi na ị maara ihe karịa ha.

Ekwela nkwa ihe ị gaghị enwe ike imezu, ekwula okwu nke nwere ike ịghọ ụgha mgbe e mesịrị. Ọ bụrụ na ụlọọrụ ahụike mezie asịrị site n'iji okwu siri ike nke mechara bụrụ na o zighị ezi maọbụ ezughị okè, mmebi nke ntụkwasị obi ha ga-adị njọ ma ga-adịkwa ogologo oge. Ọ ka mma igosi n'ụzọ doro anya ihe ị na-amaghị karịa igosi ntụkwasị obi ụgha. Okwu ndị dịka "dabere na ihe akaebe anyị nwere ugbu a" na "anyị ga-emelite nke a ma ọ bụrụ na ozi ọhụrụ pụta" na-echekwa ntụkwasị obi ọ bụladị mgbe ọnọdụ na-agbanwe.

Adabanyekwala naanị otu nzikarịta. Nyocha n'ụdị mmụọ ọpọlọ na-egosi mgbe niile na otu nzikarịta ezughị iji wepụ nkwenye ụgha nke guzosiri ike n'uche ndị mmadụ. A ga-akwughachi nkọwa eziokwu site n'ụzọ dị iche iche, site n'aka ndị ozi dị iche iche, n'oge dị iche iche. Nke a apụtabeghị na ị na-akwughachi asịrị ahụ. Ọ pụtara na ị na-akwughachi nkọwa eziokwu site n'ụdị dị iche iche, olu dị iche iche, na ọnọdụ dị iche iche.

Etinyela ozi niile n'otu olu ụlọọrụ naanị. Ozi gọọmenti maọbụ ngalaba ahụike nwere ọrụ ya, mana o zubeghị n'onwe ya, karịsịa n'ebe ndị mmadụ na-atụkwasịghị ụlọọrụ obi. Nzaghachi asịrị nke na-arụ ọrụ bụ nke a kesara: ọ na-enye ndị ozi dị iche iche otu eziokwu bụ isi, mana na-ahapụ onye ọbụla ka o were olu nke ya kwurịta okwu site na mmekọrịta nke ya na ama.

Ebe Ndụmọdụ A Si Pụta

Ụkpụrụ ndị dị n'elu sitere na usoro WHO Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE), usoro njikwa ozi na-ezighị ezi nke WHO (nke e mere site na afọ 2020), akwụkwọ nduzi CDC Crisis and Emergency Risk Communication (CERC), nyocha ndị e bipụtara gbasara mmekọrịta ama n'oge ọrịa Ebola na West Africa 2014–2016 na ọrịa Ebola DRC 2018–2020, yana akwụkwọ ọgụgụ sayensị gbasara ozi ahụike na ụdị mmụọ ọpọlọ banyere ịmezi ozi na-ezighị ezi. Mpaghara nyocha ndị bụ isi nke nyere aka gụnyere continued influence effect (Johnson na Seifert, 1994, na ọrụ sochiiri ya), akwụkwọ nyocha debunking nke Lewandowsky na ndị ibe ya (2012, "Misinformation and Its Correction") nyochara, yana nyocha n'ọhịa gbasara usoro nzaghachi ama nke WHO, UNICEF, na IFRC mere.

Usoro ọrụ nke pụrụ iche dị iche site na mba ruo mba na site na ọrịa na-efe efe ruo ọrịa na-efe efe. Ụlọọrụ ahụike mba na ọfịs WHO nọ n'otu mba ọbụla na-echekwa ntụzịaka kwekọrọ na ọnọdụ ha nke kwesịrị inyocha tupu mmejupụta.

Kedu Ka Ozi Ahụike Ọha Ga-Esi Lebara Asịrị Na-Agba Mgbe Ọrịa Na-Efe Na-Agbasa

Asịrị bụ otu n'ime ihe kacha egbu egbu mgbe ọrịa ifufe na-efe na-agbasa. Ọ bụrụ na a naghị eleba ha anya nke ọma, ha nwere ike mebie ihe niile a na-eme iji kwụsị ọrịa ahụ. Nke a bụ ụzọ dị iche iche e kwesịrị isi mee ya:

1. Chọpụta Asịrị Ahụ Tupu Ọ Gbaa Ụzọ Niile

Tupu i nwee ike izaghachi asịrị, ị ga-amalite mara na ọ na-agba. Nke a pụtara:

Gee ntị n'ihe ndị mmadụ na-ekwu n'ahịa, n'ụlọ uka, n'ụlọ nzukọ, na n'elu WhatsApp na ọwa nkwurịta okwu ndị ọzọ.
Chịkọtaa asịrị ndị ahụ, dee ha, chọpụta nke na-agba karịa.
Ghọta ihe kpatara asịrị ahụ ji malite — ọ bụ egwu ka ọ bụ, ọ bụ enweghị ntụkwasị obi n'aka gọọmentị ka ọ bụ, ka ọ bụ na ndị mmadụ enweghị ozi zuru ezu?
2. Kwuo Eziokwu N'ụzọ Doro Anya, Kwuo Ya Ọsịịsọ

Ịgba nkịtị bụ nri asịrị. Ọ na-eme ka asịrị dịkwuo ike. Kama ịgba nkịtị maọbụ ịgọnarị asịrị, ndị ọrụ ahụike kwesịrị:

Zaghachi asịrị ahụ kpọmkwem. Dịka ọmụmaatụ: "Anyị anụla na ndị mmadụ na-ekwu na ọgwụ a na-egbu mmadụ — ka anyị gwa unu ihe anyị maara n'ezie..."
Kọwaa ihe kpatara ọnụọgụ maọbụ akụkọ ji dị iche na ihe ndị mmadụ na-ahụ n'obodo ha. Ọ bụrụ na ndị mmadụ na-ahụ ọtụtụ ndị ọrịa ma gọọmentị na-asị na ọ dị ntakịrị, kọwaa etu e si agụ ọnụọgụ kama ịsị naanị "unu echegbula onwe unu."
Kwupụta ihe ị maara na ihe ị na-amaghị. Ikwu sị "anyị amabeghị ihe niile maka ọrịa a, mana ihe anyị maara ugbu a bụ nke a..." na-eweta ntụkwasị obi karịa ime ka ọ dị ka ị maara ihe niile.
3. Jiri Ndị Obodo Ntụkwasị Obi Kwusaa Ozi

N'ọtụtụ obodo, ndị mmadụ anaghị atụkwasị ndị gọọmentị maọbụ ndị dọkịta ha na-amaghị obi. Ndị ha na-atụkwasị obi karịa bụ:

Ndị eze na ndịisi obodo — Ọ bụrụ na eze maọbụ onye isi obodo ekwuo na ọrịa a dị njọ n'ezie, ndị obodo ga-ege ntị.
Ndị ụkọchukwu na ndị Imam — Ha nwere olu dị ike n'obodo. Ọ bụrụ na ha kwadoo ozi ahụike, ọ ga-aba uru nke ukwuu.
Ndị rịara ọrịa wee dị mma — Nke a bụ ihe akaebe kacha sie ike. Onye nke sị "mụ onwe m, echere m na ọ bụ asịrị, mana m gara ụlọ ọgwụ, ha gwọọ m, ugbu a adị m mma" — okwu ya ga-adị ire karịa nke gọọmentị kwuru.
Ndị ọrụ ahụike obodo (Community Health Workers) — Ha bụ ndị obodo, ha na-asụ asụsụ obodo, ha makwaara omenala ebe ahụ.
4. Kwuo Okwu N'asụsụ Ndị Mmadụ Na-anụ Anya

Nke a apụtaghị naanị ịsụgharị Bekee. Ọ pụtara:

Jiri asụsụ ndị mmadụ ji ekwurịta okwu kwa ụbọchị — Igbo, Pidgin, Yorùbá, maọbụ asụsụ ndị ọzọ — ọ bụghị naanị asụsụ oyibo.
Jiri okwu ụka na ilu ndị mmadụ maara ama. Dịka ọmụmaatụ, "ọrịa adịghị ele mmadụ anya n'ihu" — okwu dị otu a na-abanye n'obi ndị mmadụ.
Asịrị na-agba n'asụsụ obodo; ọ bụrụ na azịza gị dị naanị na Bekee, ọ gaghị erute ndị asịrị ahụ rutere.
5. Gwa Ndị Mmadụ Ihe Ha Nwere Ike Ime Kpọmkwem

Asịrị na-adịkwu ike mgbe ndị mmadụ nọ n'ọnọdụ mgbagwoju anya ma ha amaghị ihe ha ga-eme. Kama ịsị naanị "gaa ụlọ ọgwụ," gwa ha nke a kpọmkwem:

Ụlọ ọgwụ ole? Ọ dị ebee?
Ego ole ka ọ ga-efu? Ka ọ bụ n'efu?
Gịnị bụ ihe ịrịba ama nke ọrịa ahụ nke kwesịrị ime ka ha gbaga ọsịịsọ?
Gịnị ka ha nwere ike ime n'ụlọ tupu ha erute ụlọ ọgwụ?
Olee ụzọ ha ga-esi chekwaa onwe ha na ndị ezinụlọ ha?

Mgbe ndị mmadụ mara ihe ha ga-eme kpọmkwem, ha anaghị achọkwa asịrị iji chọta azịza.

6. Akwala Ndị Mmadụ Emo Maọbụ Chịa Ha Ọchị

Ụzọ kacha njọ isi lebara asịrị bụ ịsị ndị kwenyere na ya bụ ndị nzuzu maọbụ ndị amaghị ihe. Nke a ga-eme ka ha jidekwuo asịrị ahụ ike, n'ihi na:

Onye a kpọrọ onye nzuzu anaghị agbanwe echiche ya; ọ na-ajidekwu ihe o kwenyere na mbụ.
Ọtụtụ asịrị nwere ntọala — ikekwe ndị mmadụ nwere ahụmịhe ọjọọ ha nwetara n'aka ndị ọrụ ahụike na mbụ, maọbụ akụkọ ochie nke obodo.
Kama ịkwa ha emo, gbalịa ghọta ihe mere ha ji kwenye asịrị ahụ, si n'ebe ahụ malite ikwurịta okwu ha.
7. Jiri Ụzọ Ozi Dị Iche Iche

Ọ bụghị onye ọ bụla ka na-eji WhatsApp. Ọ bụghị onye ọ bụla ka na-anụ redio. Ya mere:

Jiri redio maka ndị okenye na ndị bi n'ime obodo.
Jiri WhatsApp na social media maka ụmụ okorobịa na ụmụ agbọghọ.
Kwusaa ozi n'ahịa, n'ụlọ nzukọ, na n'ebe ndị mmadụ na-ezukọ.
Zipụ ndị ọrụ ahụike ka ha na-aga n'ụlọ n'ụlọ, na-akọwa ihe ziri ezi.
8. Nọgidenụ Na-ekwu Okwu — Otu Oge Ezughị

Ịza asịrị otu oge ekwughị okwu. Asịrị ga-agbanwe ụdị, ọhụrụ ga-apụta. Ya mere:

Nọgidenụ na-enyocha ihe ndị mmadụ na-ekwu kwa ụbọchị.
Mgbe asịrị ọhụrụ pụtara, zaghachi ya ngwa ngwa tupu ọ gbaa ụzọ niile.
Nyekwanụ ndị mmadụ ozi ọhụrụ mgbe ihe ọhụrụ gbasara ọrịa ahụ pụtara.

N'ikpeazụ, ihe kacha mkpa bụ nke a: Asịrị abụghị naanị nsogbu amaghị ihe — ọ bụ nsogbu enweghị ntụkwasị obi. Ọ bụrụ na ndị mmadụ atụkwasịghị onye na-ekwu okwu obi, ha agaghị anabata ihe ọ na-ekwu, ọ bụladị ma ọ bụrụ eziokwu. Ya mere, iwu ntụkwasị obi — site n'ikwu eziokwu n'ụzọ doro anya, ige ndị obodo ntị, na inye ndị mmadụ nsọpụrụ — bụ ntọala ihe niile e ji alụso asịrị ọgụ.

Ndị otu ahụike ọha kwesịrị ịza asịrị ahụ ngwa ngwa, n’eziokwu, na n’enweghị ịkatọ ndị na-ajụ ajụjụ.

Otu esi wulite ntụkwasị obi
Kweta na ndị mmadụ nwere ezi nchegbu, ma kọwaa ihe a maara, ihe a na-amabeghị, na ihe a ka na-enyocha.
Bipụta ọnụ ọgụgụ ikpe a na-enyo enyo, nke enyochara n’ụlọ nyocha, ọnwụ, ebe e si nata akụkọ, na ụbọchị e mechiri data. NCDC na-ebipụta akụkọ ọnọdụ kọlera nke ọha nwere ike ileba anya.
Kọwaa na ọnụ ọgụgụ nwere ike ịgbanwe n’ihi akụkọ ọhụrụ, nyocha ụlọ nyocha, ma ọ bụ iwepụ ndekọ e tinyere ugboro abụọ. Nke a bụ aro nkwukọrịta maka ido anya.
Nye mmelite n’oge a kara aka, ma dozie njehie n’ihu ọha ozugbo.
Jiri Igbo na asụsụ obodo ndị ọzọ, redio, WhatsApp, ụlọ ụka, ahịa na ndị ndu obodo a tụkwasịrị obi. WHO kwuru na ozi kwesịrị ịdabere n’ọnọdụ obodo, asụsụ mpaghara, ogo ọgụgụ isi na ụzọ ozi ndị mmadụ tụkwasịrị obi.
Meghee ụzọ ndị mmadụ ga-esi zipụta ajụjụ ma ọ bụ akụkọ ọhụrụ, ma gbochie ihere na ịkpa oke. WHO na-atụ aro ka obodo metụta atụmatụ, mmejuputa na nlekota nzaghachi.
Ndụmọdụ ahụike doro anya
Onye nwere afọ ọsịsa mmiri mmiri ma ọ bụ ịgbọ agbọ kwesịrị ịmalite ORS ozugbo ma gaa ụlọọgwụ ngwa ngwa.
Gwakọta otu akpa ORS n’ime lita mmiri dị ọcha 1. Ọ bụrụ na akpa ORS adịghị, jiri ngaji shuga isii na ọkara ngaji nnu n’ime lita mmiri dị ọcha 1.
Ṅụọ naanị mmiri esiri esi ma ọ bụ mmiri e tinyere chlorine; jiri mmiri dị ọcha sie nri.
Jiri ncha na mmiri saa aka mgbe ụlọ mposi gasịrị, mgbe ilekọtachara onye ọrịa, na tupu isi nri.
Sie nri nke ọma, kpuchie ya, rie ya ozugbo.

Ihe kachasị mkpa: ndị ọrụ ahụike ekwesịghị naanị ịsị, “asịrị ahụ abụghị eziokwu.” Ha kwesịrị igosi data ha nwere, kọwaa oke data ahụ, ma nye ndị mmadụ ihe ha ga-eme ozugbo iji chebe ndụ.

Ndị ọrụ ahụike ọha kwesịrị ịza ozi WhatsApp ahụ ngwa ngwa, n’eziokwu, na n’enweghị ịkatọ ndị mmadụ.

Iwulite ntụkwasị obi
Kweta na nchegbu ndị mmadụ dị mkpa.
Bipụta data mgbe niile, kewapụ ndị a na-enyo enyo, ndị akwadoro, na ọnwụ, tinyekwa ụbọchị e mechiri data. NCDC nwere ibe akụkọ ọnọdụ kọlera.
Kọwaa ihe a maara, ihe a na-amabeghị, na ihe mere ọnụ ọgụgụ nwere ike iji gbanwee.
Dozie njehie n’ihu ọha ma mee ka ụlọ ọrụ niile na-enye otu ozi.
Gee ntị n’ajụjụ obodo, tinye ndị ndu obodo n’ọrụ, ma jiri Igbo na ụzọ nkwukọrịta ndị mmadụ tụkwasịrị obi. WHO na-akwado itinye obodo n’atụmatụ, mmejuputa na nlekota nzaghachi.
Nye ebe doro anya ndị mmadụ ga-esi nyochaa ozi ma ọ bụ kọọ ọrịa.
Ndụmọdụ ahụike
Onye nwere afọ ọsịsa mmiri mmiri ma ọ bụ ịgbọ agbọ kwesịrị ịmalite ORS ozugbo ma gaa ụlọọgwụ.
Gwakọta otu akpa ORS na lita mmiri dị ọcha 1. Ọ bụrụ na ORS adịghị, gwakọta ngaji shuga isii na ọkara ngaji nnu n’ime lita mmiri dị ọcha 1.
Ṅụọ naanị mmiri esiri esi ma ọ bụ mmiri e tinyere chlorine.
Jiri ncha na mmiri dị ọcha saa aka mgbe ụlọ mposi gasịrị na tupu isi nri.
Sie nri nke ọma, kpuchie ya ma rie ya ozugbo.

Ihe kacha mkpa abụghị naanị ịsị na asịrị ahụ bụ ụgha. Ndị ọrụ ahụike kwesịrị igosi data, kọwaa oke ya, ma nye ndụmọdụ ndị mmadụ nwere ike ime ozugbo.

Ndị ọrụ ahụike ọha kwesịrị ịza ozi WhatsApp ahụ ngwa ngwa, n’eziokwu, na nkwanye ùgwù, ọ bụghị naanị ịkpọ ya “asịrị”.

Otu esi ewulite ntụkwasị obi
Kweta na nchegbu ndị mmadụ ziri ezi ma kọwaa ihe a maara na ihe a ka na-enyocha.
Na-ebipụta mmelite oge niile, kewapụ ndị a na-enyo enyo, ndị nyocha kwadoro, na ọnwụ, tinyekwa ụbọchị data ahụ ruru. NCDC nwere ibe maka akụkọ ọnọdụ kọlera.
Kọwaa ihe mere ọnụ ọgụgụ nwere ike iji gbanwee, dịka akụkọ ọhụrụ ma ọ bụ nsonaazụ nyocha.
Dozie njehie n’ihu ọha, ma hụ na ụlọ ọrụ niile na-enye ozi kwekọrọ.
Gee ntị n’ajụjụ ndị mmadụ; jiri Igbo, WhatsApp, redio na ndị ndu obodo a tụkwasịrị obi. WHO na-akwado itinye obodo n’atụmatụ na mmejuputa nzaghachi iji mee ka ntụkwasị obi sie ike.
Nye nọmba ekwentị na ebe gọọmentị doro anya ndị mmadụ ga-esi nyochaa ozi ma ọ bụ kọọ ọrịa.
Ndụmọdụ ahụike doro anya
Onye nwere afọ ọsịsa mmiri mmiri ma ọ bụ ịgbọ agbọ kwesịrị ịmalite ORS ozugbo ma gaa ụlọọgwụ.
Gwakọta otu akpa ORS na lita mmiri dị ọcha 1. Ọ bụrụ na ORS adịghị, gwakọta ngaji shuga isii na ọkara ngaji nnu n’ime lita mmiri dị ọcha 1.
Ṅụọ naanị mmiri esiri esi ma ọ bụ mmiri e tinyere chlorine.
Jiri ncha na mmiri dị ọcha saa aka mgbe ụlọ mposi gasịrị na tupu isi nri.
Sie nri nke ọma, kpuchie ya ma rie ya ozugbo.

Isi ihe bụ igosi data, ịkọwa oke ya, ịza ajụjụ, na inye omume ndị mmadụ nwere ike ịgbaso ozugbo.

Fever, weakness and unexplained bleeding require urgent medical assessment and could indicate a serious infectious or non-infectious condition. The community should not assume a particular disease, but should act cautiously.

Immediate actions:

Contact the local health authority, emergency medical service or outbreak-response team immediately. Report the symptoms, recent travel, healthcare exposure, animal contact, funeral attendance and contact with sick people.
Keep the person in a separate, well-ventilated area away from unnecessary visitors while awaiting instructions.
Do not transport the person by public transport or a shared vehicle unless health authorities direct this.
Avoid direct contact with blood, vomit, diarrhoea, urine, saliva, clothing, bedding or other potentially contaminated materials.
Do not share food utensils, towels, clothing or bedding with the person.
Limit essential care to the smallest possible number of people. They should follow health-worker instructions and use appropriate protective equipment.
Wash hands thoroughly with soap and water after any possible contact. Do not use unapproved chemicals on the person or inside the home.
If the person dies, do not touch, wash or prepare the body. Notify the appropriate health team for safe and dignified handling.

The family should not be abandoned or attacked. Neighbours can safely provide practical support by leaving food, safe water and necessary supplies at an agreed distance, while following public-health instructions. Being related to or living near the person does not automatically mean someone is infected.

Health officials should identify and advise anyone who had direct contact with the person or their bodily fluids. Community leaders should stop rumours, protect privacy and share only verified information from health authorities.

Community Response When a Person Returns with Signs of Serious Illness
1. Immediate Safe Assessment

The community should:

Avoid panic while taking precautions

Do not isolate the family completely or deny them support
Recognise that fear is understandable, but the situation requires careful action, not abandonment
Assign one or two designated people to manage contact safely

Get accurate information quickly

Establish what the person has actually experienced (where they were, what symptoms started when)
Do not assume diagnosis based on appearance or rumour
Determine if medical evaluation has already occurred
2. Immediate Actions

Seek professional medical assessment without delay

Contact the nearest health facility or call the local health authority immediately
Do not wait for symptoms to progress
If transport is difficult, ask health workers to visit or advise on safe transport
Be honest with health workers about all symptoms, including bleeding

Establish safe isolation while awaiting assessment

The person should stay in a separate room or area if possible
Limit contact to one or two care-givers who use basic precautions
Provide clean water, soap, and clean cloths for the person to use
Do not share eating utensils, bedding, or personal items
3. Protect the Family and Community

Basic infection control anyone can do

Caregivers should wash hands thoroughly with soap and water before and after contact
Keep the person's immediate area clean and separate from shared spaces
If there is vomit, blood, or body fluids, clean with dilute bleach solution (1 part bleach to 9 parts water) or soap and water
Avoid touching blood or body fluids with bare hands

Support the family

Deliver food, water, and supplies to the household without entering
Check on their wellbeing regularly
Do not spread fear or shame—illness is not shameful, and the family needs support, not rejection
4. What Fever + Weakness + Bleeding Means

This combination requires urgent medical diagnosis because it can indicate:

Malaria with complications
Typhoid fever
Dengue or other viral fevers
Lassa fever or other haemorrhagic fevers
Severe infection (sepsis)
Other serious conditions

The point: None of these can be diagnosed by appearance. Confirmed diagnosis must come from a health worker—through history, examination, and ideally testing. Treatment depends entirely on what the actual illness is. Guessing is dangerous.

5. Reporting to Health Authorities
Notify the local health centre or district health office immediately
Describe the symptoms clearly: when fever started, whether bleeding has occurred and where, other symptoms
Ask for guidance on isolation and safety measures
If the person cannot reach a health facility, ask about home visits or emergency transport
Do not delay reporting out of fear of blame or stigma
6. Protect Children and Vulnerable People
Keep children away from close contact unless they are caregivers under supervision
Pregnant women should avoid contact until diagnosis is confirmed
Elderly people with existing illness should stay at a distance
7. What NOT to Do
Do not deny the family food, water, or basic care
Do not assume it is a specific disease—let health workers diagnose
Do not use traditional treatments alone while delaying medical evaluation
Do not prevent the person from reaching medical care
Do not spread fear publicly before facts are established

Why this matters: Fever with bleeding is a medical emergency. The community's job is to act fast, safely, and with compassion. Fear makes people hide symptoms or delay treatment, which makes everything worse. Health workers need accurate information to diagnose and treat. The family needs support, not isolation.

What a Community Should Do When Someone Returns With Fever, Weakness, and Unexplained Bleeding, and Neighbours Are Afraid
Why This Situation Requires Both a Medical Response and a Social Response

The combination of fever, weakness, and unexplained bleeding in someone who has recently travelled raises legitimate concern about viral haemorrhagic fevers, most notably Ebola virus disease. These symptoms also overlap with other serious conditions including severe malaria, leptospirosis, meningococcaemia, severe dengue, and certain bacterial infections. Only laboratory testing can confirm the cause. The community's fear is understandable, but fear left unmanaged becomes a second crisis: it leads to isolation of the family, concealment of illness, delayed treatment, and breakdown of the social cooperation that outbreak response depends on.

Both problems, the potential medical emergency and the social rupture, must be addressed simultaneously. Treating one while ignoring the other has failed in every major outbreak where it has been tried.

Immediate Medical Response

Alert health authorities before any other action. Contact the nearest health facility, disease surveillance officer, or national disease reporting channel. In Nigeria, this means contacting the NCDC or the state disease surveillance and notification officer. Provide a clear description: the person's symptoms (fever, weakness, bleeding), when symptoms began, where the person travelled from, and any known contact with sick individuals or with deceased persons in the area they returned from. This notification is the single most important action because it initiates the chain of laboratory confirmation, case management, and contact tracing that determines outcomes for both the individual and the community.

Do not touch the person or their body fluids. Until health workers arrive and provide guidance, no community member should have direct skin-to-skin contact with the sick person, handle their blood, vomit, stool, sweat, or urine, or touch clothing, bedding, or utensils contaminated with these fluids. Ebola and other viral haemorrhagic fevers transmit through direct contact with body fluids. This precaution is not rejection of the person. It is the medically correct action that protects both the community and the sick individual's chances of survival by keeping the situation contained until professional care arrives.

If care is absolutely necessary before health workers arrive, designate one person to assist. That person should cover all exposed skin as completely as possible (long sleeves, trousers, covered shoes, and if available, gloves or plastic bags over the hands). They should avoid touching body fluids, and wash hands immediately and thoroughly with soap and water or 0.05% chlorine solution after any contact. This person should also be registered as a contact for subsequent monitoring.

Do not attempt traditional treatment or remedies. No traditional preparation has demonstrated efficacy against viral haemorrhagic fevers in any clinical or laboratory study. Administering traditional remedies delays medical referral, and the physical contact involved in administering them creates direct transmission risk.

Prepare for transport. If health workers instruct the family to bring the person to a health facility, the person should be transported with minimal physical contact. Ideally, an ambulance equipped for infectious disease transport should be requested. If the person must be moved by the family, those assisting should follow the same protective measures described above and should avoid public transport where the sick person would be in close proximity to others.

Addressing the Fear and Protecting the Family from Harmful Isolation

Fear is a rational response, but its consequences must be managed. Neighbours who avoid the family are responding to a real risk. They are not wrong to be cautious about direct physical contact. However, there is a critical distinction between appropriate infection-prevention behaviour and harmful social exclusion. The community must understand this distinction clearly, because collapsing the two has caused preventable deaths in documented outbreaks.

What appropriate precaution looks like: avoiding direct physical contact with the sick person and their body fluids, maintaining distance during the acute illness, and monitoring oneself for symptoms if prior contact occurred.

What harmful exclusion looks like: refusing to speak to the family, refusing to supply them with food and water, blocking them from accessing health services, spreading their identity with stigmatising language, threatening or attacking the family, refusing to allow their other (non-symptomatic) family members to participate in community life.

The second set of behaviours does not reduce transmission risk. It increases overall risk by driving concealment. In the 2014–2016 West Africa Ebola outbreak, fear-driven stigma caused families to hide sick members, avoid health facilities, and conduct secret burials, all of which directly amplified transmission chains. The same pattern recurred in the 2018–2020 DRC Ebola outbreaks. WHO, UNICEF, and IFRC post-outbreak evaluations consistently identify stigma-driven concealment as one of the most dangerous dynamics in outbreak response.

What the Community Should Do for the Family

Maintain communication. Speak to the family from a safe distance or by phone. Inform them of what steps are being taken, that health authorities have been contacted, and what to expect. Isolation from information compounds fear and distrust on both sides.

Ensure the family has access to essentials. Food, clean water, and other necessities can be delivered to the household without physical contact. Items can be left at the entrance of the home. Cutting a family off from basic supplies during a health emergency is not a protective measure. It is abandonment that worsens outcomes for everyone, because a desperate family is more likely to flee, conceal illness, or refuse cooperation with health authorities.

Protect the family's other members. Household members who are not showing symptoms are not infectious. Ebola and other viral haemorrhagic fevers are not airborne under normal conditions. They spread through direct contact with body fluids of a person who is actively symptomatic. Non-symptomatic family members should be monitored (daily temperature checks for 21 days in the case of suspected Ebola), but they should not be treated as though they are already sick. They can interact with the community with appropriate hygiene precautions. Excluding healthy family members from work, school, markets, or social life without medical justification causes economic and psychological harm that erodes cooperation with the response.

Do not spread the family's identity with stigmatising language. Referring to the family as "the Ebola family" or similar labels entrenches stigma and makes it harder for them and for future sick individuals to seek care. Health information should focus on the disease and on protective actions, not on identifying and blaming specific households.

Community Self-Protection While Maintaining Solidarity

Practise standard infection prevention. Every household in the community should increase handwashing with soap and water, avoid touching other people's body fluids, avoid contact with items visibly soiled with blood or other fluids, and avoid handling or consuming bushmeat (particularly bats and primates) during periods of concern. These measures protect the community without requiring the social exclusion of any family.

Cooperate fully with contact tracing. When health authorities arrive, they will identify every person who had direct contact with the sick individual. Those contacts need to be monitored daily for 21 days (for suspected Ebola). Contacts are not contagious unless they develop symptoms, but daily monitoring allows rapid detection and isolation if symptoms appear. Community members should provide honest and complete information about their interactions. Lying to contact tracers to avoid monitoring is one of the most dangerous individual actions during an outbreak, because it allows an undetected case to seed new transmission chains.

Prepare an isolation area. If the community does not already have a designated space for separating sick individuals, identify one now: a well-ventilated room or structure away from common areas, with access to water and a latrine. This is not a punishment space. It is a medical measure that protects both the sick person and the community.

Attend to community information needs. Fear thrives in information vacuums. Community leaders, health workers, or other trusted figures should hold a meeting (outdoors if possible, maintaining distance) to explain what is known, what is being done, what community members should and should not do, and how to get updated information. Questions should be answered directly. Rumours should be addressed by name with factual corrections. Telling people to "not be afraid" without giving them concrete, actionable information is ineffective, because it asks them to suppress a rational emotion without providing the knowledge that would make the emotion unnecessary.

What the Community Must Not Do

Do not attack, threaten, or forcibly expel the family. Violence against affected families has occurred in multiple documented outbreaks and has never improved outcomes. It drives concealment, scatters potentially exposed individuals into other communities, and destroys the trust that health authorities need to operate.

Do not conduct traditional burial washing if the person dies. The viral load in the body of a person who has died from a viral haemorrhagic fever is extremely high. Traditional burial preparation involving washing and touching the body has been one of the most significant transmission amplifiers in every major Ebola outbreak documented by WHO. Only trained burial teams should handle the body. Safe and dignified burial protocols exist that respect cultural values while preventing transmission, and health authorities can facilitate these.

Do not block health workers from reaching the family. In several outbreaks, community resistance has prevented health teams from accessing patients, conducting testing, and performing safe burials. Every hour of delay increases the risk to the entire community.

Do not flee the community. Leaving the area before knowing whether you have been exposed risks carrying the infection to other communities. Movement out of an affected area should follow guidance from health authorities, not panic.

The Relationship Between Fear and Outcome

The evidence from major outbreaks consistently demonstrates that communities which maintain social cohesion while implementing appropriate infection-prevention measures achieve better outcomes than communities fractured by fear and stigma. This is not because cohesion is emotionally preferable, though it is. It is because outbreak response is a collective action problem. Contact tracing requires honesty. Isolation requires community support for the isolated. Safe burial requires trust between families and burial teams. Surveillance requires that sick people present to health facilities rather than hide. Every one of these functions breaks down when stigma makes the cost of being identified as a potential case higher than the cost of concealment.

The community's task is to hold two things simultaneously: genuine caution about a potentially lethal infectious disease, and genuine solidarity with a family in crisis. These are not contradictory. Caution without solidarity produces concealment. Solidarity without caution produces transmission. Both together produce the conditions under which outbreaks are controlled.

Contact person no dey contagious unless dem begin show symptoms themselves, but daily monitoring go make dem catch any new case early-early. Community members suppose give honest and complete information about who don near the person. To lie to contact tracers so that you go avoid monitoring na one of the most dangerous things any individual fit do during outbreak, because e go allow case wey nobody detect to start new chain of transmission.

Prepare isolation area. If the community never get place wey dem set aside to separate sick person, find one now: room or structure wey get good ventilation, wey dey far from where everybody dey gather, wey get access to water and toilet. This one no be punishment. Na medical measure wey dey protect both the sick person and the community.

Address community information needs. Fear dey grow well-well where information no dey. Community leaders, health workers, or other trusted people suppose hold meeting (outside if possible, keep distance) to explain wetin dem know, wetin dem dey do, wetin community members suppose do and wetin dem no suppose do, and how to get updated information. Answer questions directly. Address rumours by name with factual correction. To tell people "make una no fear" without giving them concrete, practical information no dey work, because you dey ask them to suppress emotion wey make sense without giving them the knowledge wey go make the fear unnecessary.

Wetin Community No Suppose Do At All

No attack, threaten, or drive the family comot by force. Violence against affected families don happen for plenty documented outbreaks and e never improve outcome for any of them. E dey drive people to hide sickness, scatter people wey fit don already dey exposed to go other communities, and destroy the trust wey health authorities need to do their work.

No wash body or do traditional burial preparation if the person die. The amount of virus wey dey inside body of person wey die from viral haemorrhagic fever dey extremely high. Traditional burial washing and touching of dead body don be one of the biggest things wey dey amplify transmission for every major Ebola outbreak wey WHO don document. Na only trained burial team suppose handle the body. Safe and dignified burial protocol dey wey respect cultural values but still prevent transmission, and health authorities fit help arrange these.

No block health workers from reaching the family. For several outbreaks, community resistance don prevent health teams from reaching patients, doing testing, and doing safe burial. Every hour of delay dey increase the risk for the entire community.

No run comot from the community. To leave the area before you know whether you don dey exposed dey carry risk say you fit take the infection go another community. Movement out of affected area suppose follow guidance from health authorities, no be panic.

How Fear and Outcome Connect

Evidence from major outbreaks dey consistently show say communities wey maintain social cohesion while dem dey practise correct infection-prevention measures dey get better outcomes pass communities wey fear and stigma don scatter. This no be just because togetherness dey feel better, even though e dey. Na because outbreak response be collective action problem. Contact tracing need honesty. Isolation need community support for the person wey dem isolate. Safe burial need trust between families and burial teams. Surveillance need sick people to show themselves for health facility instead of hiding. Every single one of these functions go break down when stigma make the cost of people knowing say you fit be a case higher than the cost of hiding.

The work wey community get be to hold two things at the same time: genuine caution about disease wey fit kill, and genuine solidarity with family wey dey in crisis. These two no dey fight each other. Caution without solidarity go produce hiding. Solidarity without caution go produce transmission. Both together go produce the conditions wey make outbreak dey controlled.

Where This Information Come From

This guidance dey based on WHO protocols on Ebola virus disease case management and community engagement, the WHO Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE) framework, CDC Ebola response guidelines, published evaluations of community engagement and stigma dynamics during the 2014–2016 West Africa Ebola outbreak and the 2018–2020 DRC Ebola outbreaks, WHO/UNICEF/IFRC joint guidance on community feedback mechanisms, and the broader public-health literature on stigma and infectious disease. Infection-prevention measures (barrier precautions, chlorine concentrations, 21-day monitoring period) follow WHO clinical and environmental health guidance. The transmission characteristics described (direct contact with body fluids, not airborne under normal conditions, highest viral load at and after death) reflect the established virology and epidemiology of Ebola virus disease as documented in peer-reviewed literature.

Make community verify current protocols with their national health authority or WHO country office, because specific procedures fit don update between outbreaks and fit different depending on the pathogen.

Dis kain sickness wey dey bring fever, weakness, and blood wey dey comot from body without reason — e fit be serious wahala like Ebola or Lassa fever. Di fear wey neighbours get dey understandable, but fear alone no go protect anybody. Na quick action go save life.

No touch di sick person or anything wey comot from im body with bare hand. Blood, vomit, sweat, saliva — all dis ones fit carry di sickness. So e correct say make people no dey touch am anyhow. But to abandon di family, refuse give dem food and water, or chase dem comot — dat one go only make tins worse. E go make di next person wey sick hide, and dat one go spread di sickness pass.

Report am sharp sharp. Somebody for di community — whether na community health worker, village head, pastor, imam, or any person wey people trust — make dem contact di nearest health centre or call di public health emergency number immediately. If DSNO (Disease Surveillance Officer) dey for di area, make dem reach am. Di faster wey dem report, di faster wey health workers go come confirm wetin dey happen and begin protect everybody.

Separate di sick person, but treat am like human being. While dem dey wait for health workers, make di person stay for one room wey dey get breeze. One person — just one — fit dey look after am. If gloves dey, make di person wear am. If gloves no dey, plastic bag fit cover hand, but after, make di person wash hand well well with soap or chlorine water. Nobody else suppose enter dat room.

No wash im clothes, bed sheet, or clean im vomit without protection. All dis tins fit carry di virus. Leave am for di health team, or follow wetin dem tell you do.

No carry di sick person go native doctor or prayer house wey go touch im body. Dis one na one of di biggest way wey dis kain sickness dey take spread. Herbalist and spiritual healer wey dey touch sick people body without protection — dem don dey among di people wey dey catch am pass for previous outbreaks. E no mean say prayer no good — but prayer no need body contact. You fit pray from distance.

If di person die before health workers reach, no touch di body. No wash am. No dress am. No prepare am for burial. Dis one hard, especially for our culture wey we dey respect our dead. But dead body of person wey die from dis kain sickness carry di highest risk. Wait for trained burial team. Dis single action don save whole communities before.

Support di family — but do am with sense. Drop food and water for dia door. Call dem for phone. Talk to dem from distance. Encourage dem. Community wey don handle outbreak well before, na di ones wey mix caution with compassion — dem protect demself but dem no abandon di family.

Watch di people wey don touch di sick person before. Anybody wey don touch am or touch anything wey comot from im body — make dem dey check dia temperature every day for up to 21 days. Dem no need to isolate unless dem start show signs. But if fever start, make dem report immediately — no wait, no hide.

Di main message na dis: fear no be protection — action na protection. Report quick. Isolate with care. Protect yourself but no stigmatise di family. Make health workers do dia work. Every hour wey pass without reporting na extra danger for di whole community.
