Malaria dey kill pass during rainy season because rain water wey dey stand dey give mosquito place to born pikin. But the truth be say, the things wey dey work pass to prevent malaria no cost plenty money — most of dem free. Na consistent effort be the main price.

Mosquito net wey dem treat with insecticide — e dey free most times:

This one na the number one thing wey any family fit do. For almost all countries wey malaria dey, government dey share long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) free through health centre, immunisation clinic, antenatal clinic, and mass campaigns wey dem dey do from time to time. The family suppose go the nearest health centre or ask community health worker direct. Plenty families wey suppose collect free net no dey collect am because dem no know where dem dey share am, or dem just assume say stock don finish without checking.

If net dey house already but e don tear, no throw am away — take needle and thread sew the holes. Ten minutes sewing fit restore plenty protection. Even net wey tear small, if you dey use am every night, e still better pass person wey no get net at all. But sewed net better pass torn net by far.

The mistake wey plenty people dey make: dem go put pikin under net but adults go sleep without net. Or dem go skip net for night wey cold small because dem think say mosquito no dey. Anopheles mosquito, the one wey dey carry malaria, dey bite from evening till morning — whether you notice am or not. Every person, every night, must sleep under net.

Destroy places wey mosquito dey born pikin — this one free and e dey very important:

This na where family effort dey turn to real result. Anopheles mosquito fit born pikin inside very small water — even the water wey dey inside one bottle cap or footprint for ground fit do.

During rainy season, the family suppose make am routine — every one or two days, walk round the compound do the following: turn any container wey hold water upside down or comot am — tins, broken pots, old tyres, coconut shell, plastic bags wey don collect water, buckets and jerry cans wey nobody dey use. Clean gutter and drainage so water go flow instead of standing. Fill ground wey dey low where water dey gather after rain. Cover all water storage well well — wooden lid, plastic sheet, or cloth wey you go tie tight with rope, all of dem dey work.

This work no glamorous and e dey repeat because every rain go create new standing water. But every pool of water wey you destroy na hundreds of mosquitoes wey no go born.

Block mosquito from entering house with whatever you get:

If the family no fit buy proper window screen, dem fit improvise with wetin dem get. Old mosquito nets wey don spoil for sleeping — cut am, nail am over windows and ventilation holes. Old cloth, sack material, or woven plastic bag wey you tack over doorway and window for evening time go reduce how mosquito dey enter house well well. Close doors and windows from when sun dey set because na from that time Anopheles mosquito dey start to find who to bite till morning. If space dey under door, stuff am with old cloth or rag.

E no go be perfect like proper screen, but the difference between house wey get covered openings and house wey window dey open all night na big difference for how many mosquito go enter.

Wear clothes wey cover body:

From late afternoon going into the night, everybody for the house — especially pikin — suppose wear long sleeve and long trouser or long skirt wey cover leg. If the family get this kind clothes already, e no cost anything extra. The less skin wey mosquito see, the less bite you go get. Clothes wey get light colour — white, cream, light blue — dey attract mosquito small pass dark colour clothes.

Smoke from local plants wey you fit find free:

Burn dry neem leaf, eucalyptus leaf, citronella grass, or dry cow dung for evening time. The smoke dey chase mosquito away. This na traditional method wey people don dey use for West Africa and other places for long time, and research show say e dey help reduce mosquito bite, even though e no strong like chemical repellent. Put the thing wey dey smoke for the side where wind dey blow come so the smoke go pass where the family dey sit or sleep. Make sure say the place get good ventilation because too much smoke for long time fit cause cough and breathing wahala by itself.

Cut grass and bush around the house:

Tall grass, bush, and plenty plants near the house dey give mosquito place to hide and rest during the day. If you cut the grass low and clear bush around the house regularly, the number of mosquito around the area go reduce. Na only machete or cutlass you need for this one, and you go need do am throughout rainy season.

Collect every free government health programme wey dey available:

These programmes dey exist because nobody suppose die from malaria just because dem no get money:

Indoor residual spraying (IRS) — if spray team come your area, make sure say dem spray your house. Na free. The chemical wey dem spray for wall dey kill mosquito wey land on top the wall after dem don bite.

Seasonal malaria chemoprevention (SMC) — for areas wey this programme dey run, pikin wey dey between 3 months and 5 years suppose collect every monthly dose during the transmission season. If you miss any dose, protection go get gap exactly when danger dey highest.

Intermittent preventive treatment for pregnancy (IPTp) — woman wey get belle go collect free malaria prevention medicine when she go antenatal clinic from second trimester. Every visit matter because each dose dey build protection on top the last one.

When fever catch anybody — test that same day, no wait till tomorrow:

This one fit be the most important advice for family wey no get money. The moment wey any person for the house get fever during rainy season, rush go health facility or community health worker make dem do rapid diagnostic test that same day. For most countries wey malaria dey, testing and treatment with artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT) dey free or very cheap, especially for pikin under five and pregnant women.

Malaria dey very curable if dem catch am early. Na when people delay, when dem buy medicine for chemist without test, when dem take half dose, or when dem siddon dey wait say the fever go stop by itself — na that time malaria dey kill. For pikin wey get Plasmodium falciparum, one day delay fit be the difference between the pikin survive and the pikin die.

Wetin you no suppose waste your small money on top:

Ultrasonic mosquito repellent device — research show say dem no work. Mosquito repellent wristband — the protection wey e give too small to matter. Vitamin B tablet to chase mosquito — no evidence say e dey work. And no buy malaria medicine from street vendor or market take dey swallow without test — you go waste money, you fit take wrong drug or wrong dose, and you dey help create drug resistance wey go affect everybody for your community.

The main point:

Say family no get money no mean say dem no get options. The things wey get the strongest evidence behind dem — treated nets, destroying breeding sites, blocking mosquito from entering house, covering body with clothes, free government health programmes, and testing the same day wey fever start — all of dem free or nearly free. Wetin dem need na knowledge say these things dey work, discipline to do am every day without stopping, and understanding say one method alone no enough. But when you combine all of dem together, consistently, throughout the rainy season, the chance say malaria go kill person for that house go reduce well well.

Rainy season na the time wey malaria dey most dangerous because everywhere wey water stand, mosquito go use am born pikin. But make nobody think say because money no dey, protection no dey. The things wey dey work best against malaria na things wey no cost money or cost very small. Na effort and consistency be the real currency.

Collect insecticide-treated mosquito net — na free:

This na the single most powerful thing wey any family fit do against malaria. For nearly all countries wey malaria dey common, government and health organizations dey distribute long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) free of charge. Dem dey share am for health centres, when pikin go take immunisation, when pregnant woman go antenatal, and during mass distribution campaigns wey dem dey organize from time to time.

The family suppose go nearest health facility, talk to community health worker, ask around. Plenty families wey qualify for free net miss am simply because nobody tell dem where to go collect or dem assume say stock don finish. Go ask — don't assume.

If net dey house already but holes don enter am, take needle and thread patch am. That small repair dey restore serious protection. Even torn net dey better pass no net, but patched net dey far better pass torn one.

Now, the usage mistakes wey plenty families dey make: dem use net only when mosquito dey disturb dem, dem skip am for nights wey weather cool, or dem cover pikin but adults sleep without net. All of these na dangerous errors. Anopheles mosquito — the type wey carry malaria — dey bite quietly from dusk till dawn. You fit no hear am, no feel am, but e don bite you. Every single person for the house, every single night, must sleep under net. No exception, no off-night.

Kill mosquito before dem born — destroy breeding sites for free:

Most families no realize how much power dem get over this. Mosquito need standing water to lay eggs, and dem no need plenty — the water inside one small tin, one bottle cap, one tyre, one footprint for mud, na enough for hundreds of mosquito eggs.

During rainy season, make the family create routine — every day or every other day, walk through the compound and take action. Turn every empty container upside down — tins, broken pots, plastic containers, old bowls, coconut shells. Comot old tyres or fill dem with sand so water no fit sit inside. Empty buckets and jerry cans wey nobody dey use. Check flower pots, animal drinking troughs, and anywhere wey water fit hide.

Clear gutters and drainage channels so water dey move instead of sitting. Dig small trenches if water dey pool for particular spots. Fill low ground wey dey collect water after every rain with sand or earth. Cover every water storage container tight tight — use lid, use board, use plastic sheet, use cloth tied with rope. Any method wey go prevent mosquito from reaching the water surface dey work.

This work go feel boring and repetitive because every rainfall go reset things. But every pool of water wey you eliminate na potential hundreds of mosquitoes wey no go exist. Over weeks, this compounds into real, measurable reduction for mosquito population around the home.

Block mosquito from entering the house — use wetin you get:

Proper window and door screens fit dey expensive, but the family fit improvise with materials wey already dey available. If old mosquito nets dey wey don tear too much to sleep under, cut dem into pieces and nail or tack dem over windows, ventilation holes, and eaves. Old fabric, sack material, woven nylon — anything wey air fit pass through but mosquito no fit pass — go serve.

From around sunset, close all doors and windows. This na simple thing but e dey powerful because Anopheles mosquitoes dey most active from dusk to dawn. If gap dey under the door, roll old cloth or rags and stuff am there. If cracks dey for wall, fill dem with mud or clay.

The house no go be airtight, and some mosquitoes go still enter. But the difference between house with covered openings and house with open windows all night na significant difference for how many bites the family go get.

Cover your body with clothes:

From late afternoon going, every person for the house — pikin especially — suppose change to long-sleeve shirt and long trouser or long skirt. If the family already get this kind clothes, e no cost extra kobo. You dey basically reducing the amount of skin wey mosquito fit access. Light-coloured clothes — white, cream, khaki — dey slightly less attractive to mosquitoes compared to dark colours like black or navy blue.

For small pikin wey dey kick off covers, making sure their arms and legs covered before bedtime and putting dem under net na double layer of protection wey cost nothing.

Burn local plants to make repellent smoke:

Dry neem leaves, eucalyptus leaves, citronella grass, lemon grass, or dried cow dung — any of these wey dey available locally fit produce smoke wey dey chase mosquito when you burn dem for evening time. This na traditional method wey communities across West Africa and South Asia don dey practice for generations, and scientific studies confirm say e dey give partial protection — e dey reduce the number of bites even though e no stop dem completely.

Put the smouldering material where wind go carry the smoke towards where the family dey gather for evening. But use am for open or well-ventilated space because breathing dense smoke regularly dey carry its own health risks — coughing, respiratory irritation, and long-term lung problems. Na trade-off, but used carefully and in moderation, the benefit against malaria generally outweighs the smoke risk.

Cut bush and grass around the house:

Mosquitoes dey rest during daytime inside tall grass, bush, and thick vegetation near buildings. If the family cut grass low and clear bush within the immediate surroundings of the house, dem remove these resting sites and reduce the number of mosquitoes wey dey hang around waiting for nightfall to come bite. Machete or cutlass na the only tool needed. This need to happen regularly through rainy season because vegetation grows back fast.

Take full advantage of every free public health programme:

Government and international health organizations run specific programmes designed so that no family go die from malaria because of poverty:

Indoor residual spraying (IRS) — when spray teams dey operate for the area, make the family ensure say their house dey sprayed. This service na free. The insecticide wey dem apply to walls dey kill mosquitoes wey land there after feeding. One round of spraying fit protect for months.

Seasonal malaria chemoprevention (SMC) — for areas wey get highly seasonal malaria transmission, children between 3 months and 5 years old supposed to receive preventive antimalarial medicine every month during peak season. Each dose matters — missing even one cycle creates vulnerability right when transmission dey highest. The medicine na free.

Intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy (IPTp) — pregnant women receive free doses of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine at antenatal clinic visits from second trimester. Each scheduled visit adds another layer of protection for both mother and baby. Skipping visits means missing doses.

Community health workers — for many areas, trained community health workers dey available even closer than the health centre. Dem fit test for malaria, give treatment, and advise on prevention. Find out if your community get dem and where dem dey.

The moment fever start — test that same day:

If any person for the house develop fever during rainy season, that na emergency until you prove say e no be malaria. Go health facility or community health worker immediately — that same day, not tomorrow, not next week. Rapid diagnostic tests take minutes and dey available for free or very cheap for most endemic-country health systems. First-line treatment with artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT) dey also free or subsidised, especially for pikin under five and pregnant women.

Malaria wey dem catch early dey completely curable. E become killer when people delay — when dem try manage am for house, when dem buy medicine for chemist or market without proper test, when dem take incomplete dose, or when dem wait dey hope say the fever go stop by itself. For pikin wey carry Plasmodium falciparum, the most dangerous species, things fit move from ordinary fever to life-threatening crisis — cerebral malaria, severe anaemia, organ failure — within hours. One day of waiting fit cost a life.

Things wey the family no suppose waste their small money on:

Ultrasonic mosquito repellent devices — multiple studies show say dem no work at all. Mosquito-repellent wristbands and ankle bands — protection wey dem give too small to make real difference. Vitamin B supplements to repel mosquito — no credible scientific evidence. And buying antimalarial drugs from informal vendors to swallow without confirmed diagnosis — this waste money, risk wrong drug or wrong dose, and contribute to drug resistance wey go make malaria harder to treat for everybody for the community.

If small money dey available and the family want to buy something, the most cost-effective purchase na topical mosquito repellent containing DEET, picaridin, or IR3535 for use on exposed skin during evening hours. Even small bottle go last if you apply am only to skin wey clothes no dey cover.

But when you stack all of dem together and maintain dem consistently through the entire rainy season, you dey dramatically cutting down the chance say malaria go take somebody from that household.

Wọ aṣọ tó bo ọwọ́ àti ẹsẹ̀, pàápàá ní ìrọ̀lẹ́ àti alẹ́.
Bí wọ́n bá lè rí i, kí wọ́n lo àwọ̀n ibùsùn tí a fi òògùn pa ẹ̀fọn sí.
Pa ilẹ̀kùn àti ferese mọ́ nígbà tí ẹ̀fọn bá pọ̀, tàbí lo net/screen tó rọrùn bí ó bá wà.
Bí òògùn tí ń lé ẹ̀fọn bá wà ní iye tí wọ́n lè san, kí wọ́n lo gẹ́gẹ́ bí ìtọ́sọ́nà rẹ̀.

Bí ẹnikẹ́ni bá ní ara gbígbóná tàbí àwọn àmì àìsàn míì, ó dára kí wọ́n ṣe àyẹ̀wò malaria tàbí lọ sí ilé ìwòsàn dípò kí wọ́n kan rò pé malaria ni.

Àwọn ọ̀nà tí kò gbówó púpọ̀ ni:

Tú omi tó dúró sínú garawa, táyà, agolo àti gutter nù déédéé.
Bo ibi tí a fi ń tọ́jú omi, kí ẹ̀fọn má bàa bímọ síbẹ̀.
Sùn lábẹ́ àwọ̀n ibùsùn tí a fi oògùn sí ní gbogbo alẹ́.
Ṣe àtúnṣe sí àwọ̀n fèrèsé àti ilẹ̀kùn, kí wọ́n sì wọ aṣọ tó bo ara ní ìrọ̀lẹ́.
Béèrè lọ́wọ́ ilé ìwòsàn àdúgbò bóyá àwọ̀n ibùsùn ọ̀fẹ́ tàbí olówó poku wà.

Bí ara gbígbóná, òtútù tàbí orí fífọ́ bá bẹ̀rẹ̀, lọ ṣe àyẹ̀wò malaria kí o tó lo oògùn.

Ìbéèrè yìí dára gan-an, nítorí pé ìdènà ẹ̀fọn kì í ṣe pé ohun gbówó nìkan ló ń ṣiṣẹ́. Àwọn ọ̀nà tó dá sáká púpọ̀ wà tí ìdílé lè lò.

Àwọn ọ̀nà tó kò ná owó rárá tàbí tó ná díẹ̀:

Omi tó dúró sójú kan jẹ́ ibi tí ẹ̀fọn ń bímọ sí jù. Nítorí náà, kí wọ́n dà gbogbo omi tó kù sínú àwọn agolo, ìkòkò tí wọ́n kò lò, taya àtijọ́, àti ohunkóhun tó lè kó omi jọ ní àyíká ilé. Èyí yẹ kí wọ́n máa ṣe lóṣọ̀ọ̀ṣẹ̀, pàápàá ní àkókò òjò. Ọ̀nà yìí kò ná owó kankan, ṣùgbọ́n ó ṣe pàtàkì gan-an.

Kí wọ́n bo àwọn àgbá omi, ọ̀pọ́n omi, àti kángá dáadáa kí ẹ̀fọn má bàa lè wọ inú rẹ̀ láti yọ ẹyin. Àpò tàbí aṣọ tó nípọn lè ṣiṣẹ́ fún ìdérí tí wọ́n kò bá ní ìdérí gan-an.

Kí wọ́n máa wọ aṣọ tó bo ara dáadáa ní alẹ́ — aṣọ apá gígùn, ṣòkòtò gígùn, àti ìbọ̀sẹ̀. Ẹ̀fọn máa ń jẹ ènìyàn jù ní ìrọ̀lẹ́ àti ní kutukutu òwúrọ̀, nítorí náà ní àwọn àkókò yẹn ni kí wọ́n ṣọ́ra jù.

Sísun lábẹ́ àwọ̀n (mosquito net) jẹ́ ọ̀nà kan tó ṣe pàtàkì gan-an. Ní ọ̀pọ̀ àwọn ilé ìwòsàn ìjọba àti àwọn àjọ ìlera, wọ́n máa ń pín àwọ̀n tó ní oògùn (insecticide-treated nets) lọ́fẹ̀ẹ́ tàbí ní owó kékeré fún àwọn aboyún àti àwọn ọmọdé. Kí wọ́n béèrè ní ilé ìwòsàn tó wà nítòsí bóyá wọ́n ń pín.

Àwọn ọ̀nà àdánidá tó ṣiṣẹ́:

Ewé àti ohun ọ̀gbìn kan wà tó lè da ẹ̀fọn lẹ́yìn díẹ̀. Ewé ẹ̀fọn (lemongrass), neem (dongoyaro), àti basil — tí wọ́n bá gbin wọ́n sí àyíká ilé tàbí nítòsí fèrèsé, wọ́n lè ṣe ìrànlọ́wọ́ díẹ̀. Bákannáà, sísun epo neem tàbí ewe eucalyptus nínú ilé lè da ẹ̀fọn sílẹ̀ díẹ̀, bí ó tilẹ̀ jẹ́ pé kò lágbára tó bí oògùn ẹ̀fọn (insecticide).

Èèfín igi gbígbẹ tàbí eégún ọ̀gbìn tí wọ́n bá sun ún lè lé ẹ̀fọn kúrò ní àgbègbè kan fún ìgbà díẹ̀, pàápàá ní alẹ́. Àmọ́ kí wọ́n ṣọ́ra pé èèfín púpọ̀ kò dára fún ẹ̀dọ̀fóró, pàápàá fún àwọn ọmọdé kékeré.

Àwọn ọ̀nà mìíràn tó ná owó kékeré:

Tí wọ́n bá lè rà á, mosquito coil jẹ́ ohun tó wọ́pọ̀ tó sì ná owó díẹ̀. Ṣùgbọ́n kí wọ́n máa lo ó ní ibi tó ní afẹ́fẹ́ dáadáa, kí wọ́n má ṣe sùn tí coil ń jó ní yàrá tí wọ́n pa fèrèsé dé pátápátá.

Fífi aṣọ ojú fèrèsé (window screens tàbí mesh) sí fèrèsé àti ìlẹ̀kùn jẹ́ ìdókò tó dáa tí kò ná owó púpọ̀. Aṣọ net tó nípọn tí wọ́n bá fi kàn mọ́ fèrèsé lè ṣiṣẹ́ dáadáa.

Ohun tó ṣe pàtàkì jù:

Ìdènà ẹ̀fọn tó dára jù ni láti so ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ọ̀nà wọ̀nyí pọ̀ — dídà omi kúrò, wíwọ aṣọ, sísun lábẹ́ àwọ̀n, àti fífi ewé ẹ̀fọn sí àyíká ilé. Ọ̀nà kan ṣoṣo kò tó, ṣùgbọ́n tí wọ́n bá papọ̀ wọ́n lè dín jíjẹ ẹ̀fọn kù gan-an láì ná owó púpọ̀.

Tí ẹnikẹ́ni nínú ìdílé náà bá bẹ̀rẹ̀ sí ní ara gbígbóná, kí wọ́n má ṣe dúró — kí wọ́n lọ ṣe ìdánwò ibà ní ilé ìwòsàn lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀.

Ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ọ̀nà wà tí ìdílé yìí lè gbà láti dáàbò bo ara wọn lọ́wọ́ ẹ̀fọn àti ibà, kódà láìní owó púpọ̀:

Àwọ̀n ẹ̀fọn tí wọ́n fi oògùn pa (ITN)

Èyí ṣe pàtàkì jù lọ nínú gbogbo rẹ̀. Ìjọba àti àwọn àjọ ìlera (bí WHO) máa ń pín àwọ̀n ẹ̀fọn lọ́fẹ̀ẹ́ ní àwọn ilé ìwòsàn alákọ̀ọ́bẹ̀rẹ̀, àwọn ibi ìtọ́jú aboyún, àti nígbà ìpolongo àjẹsára. Ìdílé náà lè lọ béèrè ní ilé ìwòsàn ìjọba tàbí ọ́fíìsì ìjọba ìbílẹ̀ tó wà nítòsí wọn. Àwọ̀n kan lè bo ènìyàn méjì. Ohun tó ṣe pàtàkì ni kí wọ́n sùn lábẹ́ rẹ̀ ní gbogbo alẹ́, kì í ṣe nígbà tí wọ́n bá rí ẹ̀fọn nìkan.

Dènà ẹ̀fọn láti wọlé

Kí wọ́n dí gbogbo ihò àti ààyè tí ẹ̀fọn lè gbà wọ inú ilé. Tí owó kò bá tó ra ẹ̀wù ojú fèrèsé (window net), wọ́n lè lo aṣọ àtijọ́, aṣọ ìkélé, tàbí àpò dáadáa láti bo àwọn ṣíṣí náà. Kí wọ́n pa ilẹ̀kùn àti fèrèsé ṣáájú àsálẹ́ nígbà tí ẹ̀fọn bá ń pọ̀ sí i.

Mú omi dídúró kúrò ní àyíká ilé

Ibí tí omi bá dúró ni ẹ̀fọn máa ń bímọ sí. Nítorí náà kí ìdílé náà:

Yi garawa, àgolo, taya, àti ohun èlò tí ó lè kó omi jọ lékè
Gbá ààlà omi (gutter) àti ojú ọ̀nà omi mọ́ dáadáa kí omi má bàa dúró
Bo àgbà omi àti tánkì pẹ̀lú ìdérí
Má ṣe fi omi sílẹ̀ nínú ìkòkò odòdó tàbí ohun èlò aláìlò

Èyí kò ní owó kankan, ṣùgbọ́n agbára rẹ̀ pọ̀ gan-an.

Wọ aṣọ tó bo ara ní alẹ́

Ní ìrọ̀lẹ́ àti alẹ́, kí gbogbo ènìyàn wọ ẹ̀wù apá gígùn àti ṣòkòtò gígùn. Aṣọ aláwọ̀ fẹ́ẹ́rẹ́fẹ́ (funfun tàbí aláwọ̀ sánmà) dára jù nítorí ẹ̀fọn máa ń fà mọ́ aṣọ dúdú.

Ṣá igbó, kí wọ́n sì mọ́ àyíká ilé

Koríko gíga àti igbó tó sún mọ́ ilé ni ẹ̀fọn máa ń fi pamọ́ ní ọ̀sán. Kí wọ́n bẹ koríko kù, ṣá igbó, kí wọ́n sì mú gbogbo àyíká mọ́. Èyí dín ibi tí ẹ̀fọn lè gbé sinú kù.

Lo ohun ọ̀gbìn àdáyébá láti lé ẹ̀fọn

Sísun ewé dọ̀gọ̀yàrò (neem), kòríkò tíì (lemongrass), tàbí epo ọsàn gbígbẹ nínú yàrá lè ṣèrànwọ́ láti dá ẹ̀fọn lẹ́kun. Àwọn ohun ọ̀gbìn wọ̀nyí sábà máa ń wà ní àyíká, kò sì ní owó. Kò lágbára bí oògùn kẹ́míkà, ṣùgbọ́n ó dára ju ìgbìyànjú kankan lọ.

Mọ àsìkò tí ẹ̀fọn ń jẹ jù lọ

Ẹ̀fọn ibà (Anopheles) jẹ jù láàárín ìrọ̀lẹ́ àti kùtùkùtù òwúrọ̀. Àsìkò yìí ni ìdílé náà gbọdọ̀ ṣọ́ra jùlọ — sùn lábẹ́ àwọ̀n, wọ aṣọ gígùn, bo ojú fèrèsé, pa ilẹ̀kùn.

Ohun pàtàkì tí kò gbówó:

Tí ẹnikẹ́ni nínú ìdílé bá ní ibà tàbí ara gbígbóná, kí wọ́n lọ sí ilé ìwòsàn ìjọba kí wọ́n ṣe ìdánwò ẹ̀jẹ̀ (malaria test) kí wọ́n tó mu oògùn kankan. Ní ilé ìwòsàn ìjọba, ìdánwò àti oògùn ibà (ACT) sábà máa ń jẹ́ lọ́fẹ̀ẹ́ tàbí ní owó kékeré. Mímu oògùn láìmọ àìsàn tí ó ń ṣe ẹni lè ba owó jẹ́, àìsàn náà sì lè burú sí i.

Ní àkópọ̀: àwọ̀n lọ́fẹ̀ẹ́ láti ọ̀dọ̀ ìjọba, ìmọ́tótó àyíká, dídí ṣíṣí ojú fèrèsé, yíyọ omi dídúró kúrò, àti aṣọ gígùn ní alẹ́ — gbogbo àwọn ohun wọ̀nyí kò gbówó lórí, ṣùgbọ́n wọ́n lè dáàbò bo ìdílé náà lọ́wọ́ ibà gan-an.

Àwọn Ọ̀nà Ìdènà Ibà Tó Dá Sáká

Ní àkókò òjò, ẹ̀fọn máa ń pọ̀ sí i, ṣùgbọ́n àwọn ọ̀nà tó dáa wà tí kò nílò owó púpọ̀ láti dáàbò bo ìdílé.

Àwọ̀n Àpamọ́ra Ẹ̀fọn (Insecticide-Treated Nets)

Ìjọba àti àwọn àjọ ìlera bíi WHO máa ń pín àwọ̀n àpamọ́ra ẹ̀fọn tí wọ́n ti fi oògùn ṣe (Long-Lasting Insecticidal Nets) lọ́fẹ̀ẹ́ ní ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn ilé ìwòsàn àti ibi ìtọ́jú ọmọdé. Ó yẹ kí ẹ bèèrè ní ilé ìwòsàn tó wà nítòsí yín. Àpamọ́ra yìí jẹ́ ọ̀nà tó múnadóko jù lọ láti dènà jíjẹ ẹ̀fọn ní alẹ́.

Mímú Àyíká Mọ́tótó

Ẹ̀fọn máa ń bí sínú omi tó dúró sójú kan. Àwọn ìgbésẹ̀ pàtàkì ni:

Ẹ da omi kúrò nínú àwọn agolo, ìkarahun, tàyà àtijọ́, àti ohunkóhun tó lè mú omi dúró ní àyíká ilé.
Ẹ bo àwọn kòtò omi tó wà nítòsí ilé tàbí kí ẹ dà wọ́n ká.
Ẹ má ṣe jẹ́ kí omi ẹ̀rọ̀ amúnádùrú (air conditioner) tàbí omi tó ń ṣàn láti orí ilé kó jọ sójú kan.
Ẹ gé koríko tó ga àti igi tó wà nítòsí ilé kù.
Sísí Ojú Fèrèsé àti Àwọn Ẹ̀rọ Ìdènà
Ẹ fi àwọ̀n aṣọ ìkélé ẹ̀fọn (window/door screens) sí ojú fèrèsé àti ẹnu ọ̀nà. Èyí kò gbówó lórí, àwọn aṣọ afẹ́fẹ́ oníhó kékeré lè ṣiṣẹ́.
Ẹ pa fèrèsé àti ẹnu ọ̀nà dé ní ìrọ̀lẹ́ àti ní àárọ̀ kùtùkùtù nígbà tí ẹ̀fọn bá ń múnadóko jù lọ.
Wíwọ Aṣọ Tó Bójú Ara

Ní ìrọ̀lẹ́ àti ní kùtùkùtù àárọ̀, ẹ wọ aṣọ apá gígùn, sòkòtò gígùn, àti ìbọ̀sẹ̀ láti dín ibi tí ẹ̀fọn lè jẹ yín kù. Aṣọ funfun tàbí aṣọ àwọ̀ rírìn dára jù lọ nítorí ẹ̀fọn máa ń nífẹ̀ẹ́ sí àwọ̀ dúdú.

Àwọn Ewéko Tó Lè Lé Ẹ̀fọn

Àwọn ewé kan wà tí ẹ̀fọn kò fẹ́ràn tí ẹ lè rí lọ́fẹ̀ẹ́ tàbí ní ìdíyelé kékeré:

Ewé nchanwu (basil/scent leaf) — ẹ gbin ní àyíká ilé tàbí fi sí ojú fèrèsé.
Ewé lemongrass — ẹ gbin ní ẹ̀gbẹ́ ilé.
Epo citronella — bí ẹ bá rí i, ẹ lè fi pa ara.
Ẹ sun epo igi tàbí àwọn ohun èlò tó ń mú èéfín jáde nínú yàrá (ṣùgbọ́n ẹ ṣọ́ra kí àfẹ́fẹ́ maa ń kọjá dáadáa láti yẹra fún ìpalára lábẹ́ èéfín).
Ìṣọ́ra Pàtàkì

Bí ẹnikẹ́ni nínú ìdílé bá ní ibà, ohun tó pọndandan ni kí ẹ lọ sí ilé ìwòsàn kí wọ́n ṣàyẹ̀wò ẹ̀jẹ̀ rẹ̀ (malaria test) kí wọ́n tó bẹ̀rẹ̀ ìtọ́jú. Mímú oògùn ibà láìṣàyẹ̀wò lè jẹ́ kí oògùn má ṣiṣẹ́ mọ́ fún àwùjọ lápapọ̀ nígbà iwájú (àjẹsára oògùn — drug resistance), ó sì tún lè jẹ́ ìnáwó àìlèsè. Àyẹ̀wò ibà ní ọ̀pọ̀ ilé ìwòsàn ìjọba jẹ́ lọ́fẹ̀ẹ́ tàbí ní ìdíyelé kékeré.

Àpapọ̀ gbogbo àwọn ọ̀nà wọ̀nyí papọ̀ — àpamọ́ra, mímọ́tótó àyíká, àti wíwọ aṣọ tó yẹ — ni yóò fún yín ní ààbò tó dára jù lọ láìnílò owó púpọ̀.
Ọ̀rọ̀ náà tọ́: àwọn ìgbésẹ̀ wọ̀nyí lè dín ewu ẹ̀fọn àti malaria kù. Ṣíṣe àyẹ̀wò kí a tó lo oògùn malaria tún ṣe pàtàkì.

Àwọn ọ̀nà ìdènà tí kò gbówó púpọ̀ ni:

Tú omi tó dúró sínú garawa, táyà, agolo àti gutter nù déédéé.
Bo àwọn ohun tí a fi ń tọ́jú omi.
Sùn lábẹ́ àwọ̀n ibùsùn tí a fi oògùn sí ní gbogbo alẹ́. Àwọ̀n yìí jẹ́ ọ̀kan lára ọ̀nà tó munadoko jù lọ fún ìdènà malaria.
Ṣe àtúnṣe sí àwọ̀n fèrèsé àti ilẹ̀kùn.
Wọ aṣọ tó bo ọwọ́ àti ẹsẹ̀ nígbà tí ẹ̀fọn pọ̀.
Béèrè ní ilé ìwòsàn àdúgbò bóyá àwọ̀n ibùsùn ọ̀fẹ́ tàbí olówó poku wà.

Tú omi tó dúró sínú garawa, táyà, agolo àti gutter nù déédéé.
Bo àwọn ohun tí a fi ń tọ́jú omi.
Sùn lábẹ́ àwọ̀n ibùsùn tí a fi oògùn sí ní gbogbo alẹ́. Àwọ̀n yìí jẹ́ ọ̀kan lára ọ̀nà tó munadoko jù lọ fún ìdènà malaria.

Ezinụlọ ahụ nwere ike iji ụzọ ndị a dị mfe ma dị ọnụ ala belata anwụnta na-ata ha:

Kpofu mmiri ma sachaa ihe niile mmiri na-eguzo n’ime ha otu ugboro n’izu, dịka bọket, mkpọ, karama, taya ochie na ite ifuru.
Kpuchie ihe e ji echekwa mmiri nke ọma. Tụgharịa ite na bọket ndị a naghị eji eme ihe ka mmiri ozuzo ghara ịbanye n’ime ha.
Mepee gọta na ọwa mmiri mechiri emechi. Wepụ mkpofu na ahịhịa ndị na-eme ka mmiri guzoro n’akụkụ ụlọ.
Ọ bụrụ na ha nwere ụgbụ anwụnta e tinyere ọgwụ, ka ha na-eji ya kwa abalị. A pụrụ iji agịga na eri ma ọ bụ obere akwa mechie oghere ndị dị na ya.
Jụọ ụlọọgwụ, ndị ọrụ ahụike ọha ma ọ bụ òtù obodo ma ha na-ekesa ụgbụ anwụnta e tinyere ọgwụ n’efu ma ọ bụ n’ọnụ ahịa dị ala.
Mechie ọnụ ụzọ na windo site na mgbede ma ọ bụrụ na nke ahụ agaghị egbochi ikuku ịbanye n’ụlọ. Dozie ụgbụ windo mebiri emebi ma ọ bụ jiri ntupu dị mma kpuchie oghere.
Yiri uwe ogologo aka, ogologo ọkpa na sọks site na mgbede ruo n’isi ụtụtụ.
Ọ bụrụ na ọgwụ a kwadoro maka ịchụ anwụnta dị ọnụ ala, jiri ya dịka ntụziaka dị n’akpa ya si dị. Etekwala ọgwụ e ji efesa ụlọ n’akpụkpọ ahụ.
Soro ndị agbata obi hichaa gọta, ọwa mmiri na mkpofu dị n’ebe ọha. Anwụnta nwere ike ịmụba n’èzí ogige ụlọ ma bata n’ime ya.
Ọ bụrụ na onye ọ bụla enwee ahụ ọkụ, oyi, isi ọwụwa ma ọ bụ adịghị ike pụrụ iche, kpọga ya ebe ahụike ngwa ngwa maka nyocha ọrịa ịba.

Awụsala kerosene, petrol, bleach ma ọ bụ kemikal a na-akwadoghị n’ime mmiri a na-aṅụ ma ọ bụ n’ọdọ mmiri dị nso. Ezinaụlọ ahụ ekwesịghị ịmụnye ọkụ na-eme nnukwu anwụrụ n’ime ụlọ iji chụpụ anwụnta, n’ihi na anwụrụ ahụ nwere ike imerụ ahụ. Ọgwụ ọkụ anwụnta ma ọ bụ spray nwere ike inye nchebe ọzọ ma e jiri ya mee ihe nke ọma, mana ha agaghị anọchi ụgbụ e tinyere ọgwụ na iwepụ mmiri guzoro otu ebe.

N’oge udu mmiri, ezinụlọ nwere ike belata anwụnta na-ata ha site n’ụzọ ndị dị mfe ma na-adịghị oke ọnụ:

Wepụ ma ọ bụ wụpụ mmiri kwụsiri ike n’ime bọket, taya ochie, ite, karama, gutters, na ebe ndị ọzọ mmiri na-anakọta.
Kpuchie ite ma ọ bụ tankị a na-edobe mmiri.
Hichaa ahịhịa, ihe mkpofu, na ebe gbara ụlọ gburugburu ebe anwụnta nwere ike izu ike.
Yiri uwe na-ekpuchi aka na ụkwụ, karịchaa n’abalị na n’oge mgbede.
Ọ bụrụ na e nwere ụgbụ anwụnta e tinyere ọgwụ, jiri ya mgbe a na-ehi ụra.
Mechie ụzọ na windo mgbe anwụnta na-abata nke ukwuu, ma jiri net ma ọ bụ ihe mkpuchi windo ma ọ bụrụ na e nwere ya.
Ọ bụrụ na ọgwụ ịchụ anwụnta dị ọnụ ala ma dị, jiri ya dịka ntuziaka ya si kwuo.

Ọ bụrụ na onye ọ bụla n’ezinụlọ amalite inwe ahụ ọkụ ma ọ bụ mgbaàmà ndị ọzọ, ọ ka mma ka e mee nnyocha malaria ma ọ bụ nyocha ahụike kama iche ozugbo na ọ bụ malaria.

N’oge udu mmiri, ezinụlọ nwere ike belata anwụnta na-ata ha site n’ụzọ ndị dị mfe ma na-adịghị oke ọnụ:

Wepụ ma ọ bụ wụpụ mmiri kwụsiri ike n’ime bọket, taya ochie, ite, karama, gutters, na ebe ndị ọzọ mmiri na-anakọta.
Kpuchie ite ma ọ bụ tankị a na-edobe mmiri.
Hichaa ahịhịa, ihe mkpofu, na ebe gbara ụlọ gburugburu ebe anwụnta nwere ike izu ike.
Yiri uwe na-ekpuchi aka na ụkwụ, karịchaa n’abalị na n’oge mgbede.
Ọ bụrụ na e nwere ụgbụ anwụnta e tinyere ọgwụ, jiri ya mgbe a na-ehi ụra.
Mechie ụzọ na windo mgbe anwụnta na-abata nke ukwuu, ma jiri net ma ọ bụ ihe mkpuchi windo ma ọ bụrụ na e nwere ya.
Ọ bụrụ na ọgwụ ịchụ anwụnta dị ọnụ ala ma dị, jiri ya dịka ntuziaka ya si kwuo.

Ọ bụrụ na onye ọ bụla n’ezinụlọ amalite inwe ahụ ọkụ ma ọ bụ mgbaàmà ndị ọzọ, ọ ka mma ka e mee nnyocha malaria ma ọ bụ nyocha ahụike kama iche ozugbo na ọ bụ malaria.

Ezinụlọ bi n'akụkụ mmiri nwere ike ime ọtụtụ ihe iji chebe onwe ha n'aka anwụnta n'ụzọ na-efu ego ukwuu:

Iwepụ ebe anwụnta na-amụ nwa

Anwụnta na-amụ nwa n'ime mmiri nọ jụụ. Ya mere, ezinụlọ ahụ kwesịrị iwufu mmiri nọ jụụ n'ụdọ, n'ime ite, n'ime tayịa ochie, na n'ime ihe ọ bụla nwere ike ịchịkọta mmiri ozuzo. Ọ bụrụ na ha nwere ọdọ mmiri nta maọbụ ebe mmiri na-akwụsị, ha nwere ike ikpuchi ha nke ọma maọbụ tụnye aja n'ime ha. Nke a bụ otu n'ime ihe kacha mkpa — ịbelata ọnụ ọgụgụ anwụnta n'ebe ha bi.

Ikpuchi windo na ụzọ

Ha nwere ike iji neting dị ọnụ ala maọbụ akwa na-ekpuchi windo na ụzọ n'abalị iji gbochie anwụnta ịbata n'ụlọ. Ọ bụrụ na neting adịghị, ịkwụba akwa n'ụzọ windo nwere ike inyere aka.

Iji ihe na-achụ anwụnta si n'okike

Ahịhịa ụfọdụ dịka neem, citronella, na lemongrass nwere ike ịchụpụ anwụnta. Ha nwere ike ịkụ ahịhịa ndị a gburugburu ụlọ ha. Ha nwekwara ike ịgba akwụkwọ neem ọkụ n'abalị ka anụsị ya chụọ anwụnta.

Iyiwe uwe na-ekpuchi ahụ

N'abalị ma ọ bụ n'oge uhuruchi mgbe anwụnta na-arị elu, iyiwe uwe aka ogologo na uwe ụkwụ ogologo na-enyere aka igbochi anwụnta ịta mmadụ.

Ihi ụra n'okpuru ụgbụ anwụnta

Ọ bụ ezie na ụgbụ anwụnta nwere ike ịdị ọnụ, ụfọdụ ọrụ ahụike gọọmentị na ụlọ ọrụ dịka WHO na-enye ha n'efu maọbụ n'ọnụ ala. Ezinụlọ ahụ kwesịrị ịjụ n'ụlọ ọgwụ maọbụ n'ọfịs ahụike nke obodo ha ma enwere mmemme enyemaka dị otú ahụ.

Igbochi mmiri ịnọ jụụ n'ụzọ ndị ọzọ

Ọ bụrụ na ha nwere ọdọ mmiri maọbụ ebe mmiri na-anọ jụụ nke ha apụghị iwufu, ha nwere ike itinye azụ dịka tilapia n'ime ya — azụ ndị a na-eri ahụhụ anwụnta (larvae) ma belata ọnụ ọgụgụ ha.

Ihe kacha mkpa bụ ime ihe ndị a ọnụ: iwepụ ebe mmiri na-anọ jụụ, ikpuchi ahụ, na iji ihe si n'okike achụ anwụnta. Nke a nwere ike ibelata oke nsogbu anwụnta n'enweghị ego ukwuu.

Ụzọ Dị Mfe Iji Gbochie Anwụnta Na Ịba

N'oge udu mmiri, anwụnta na-abawanye ụba, mana ụzọ dị iche iche dị nke ezinụlọ nwere ike isi chebe onwe ha n'efu ma ọ bụ n'ọnụ ahịa pere mpe.

Nkwụsịtụ Anwụnta (Insecticide-Treated Nets)

Gọọmentị na ọtụtụ ụlọ ọgwụ na-ekenye nkwụsịtụ anwụnta (Long-Lasting Insecticidal Nets) n'efu, karịsịa n'ebe a na-elekọta ụmụaka na ụmụ nwanyị dị ime. Gaa n'ụlọ ọgwụ gọọmentị nke dị gị nso jụọ maka ya. Nkwụsịtụ a bụ ụzọ kachasị arụ ọrụ nke ọma iji gbochie ịta anwụnta n'abalị. Ọ dị mkpa ka mmadụ niile n'ezinụlọ na-arahụ n'ime ya, karịsịa ụmụaka na ụmụ nwanyị dị ime.

Ịhịchapụ Ebe Mmiri Na-anọ

Anwụnta na-amụ nwa n'ebe mmiri na-anọgide. Nke a pụtara na ọ dị oke mkpa ịhịchapụ ebe mmiri na-akwụsị n'akụkụ ụlọ:

Wụpụ mmiri nọ n'ime karama, taya ochie, ite, efere, na ihe ọ bụla nwere ike ịjụ mmiri.
Kpuchie ọkwa mmiri na tankị mmiri nke ọma.
Ghara ịhapụ mmiri ka ọ nọdụ ọtọ n'ọhịa ma ọ bụ n'ogige.
Bichaa ahịhịa toro ogologo n'akụkụ ụlọ, n'ihi na anwụnta na-ezo n'ime ha.
Imechi Wịndoo Na Ụzọ
Tinye ihe mkpuchi wịndoo (window screens) nke nwere oghere pere mpe nke anwụnta na-apụghị isi bata. Nke a abụghị ihe dị oke ọnụ.
Mechie wịndoo na ụzọ n'oge uhuruchi na n'isi ụtụtụ, bụ oge anwụnta na-arụsị ọrụ ike.
Iyiwe Uwe Nke Ga-ekpuchi Ahụ

N'oge uhuruchi na n'isi ụtụtụ, yiwe uwe aka ogologo, ogologo ụkwụ trọza, na sọọsị. Nke a na-ebelata ebe anwụnta nwere ike ịta gị. Uwe nwere agba dị mfe (dịka ọcha) ka mma, n'ihi na anwụnta na-ahụ agba ojii nke ọma ma na-adọta ha.

Ahịhịa Na Osisi Na-achụpụ Anwụnta

Ụfọdụ ahịhịa dị n'obodo anyị nwere ike inyere aka:

Nchanwu (scent leaf/basil) — kụọ ya n'akụkụ wịndoo na n'ogige. Isisi ya na-achụpụ anwụnta.
Lemongrass — kụọ ya n'akụkụ ụlọ.
Ọ bụrụ na ị nwere ike ịnweta mmanụ citronella, tee ya n'ahụ gị.
Ịkpọ nkụ ma ọ bụ ihe ndị ọzọ na-esi ísì (dịka ọkụ anwụnta) n'ime ụlọ nwere ike inyere aka, mana lezie anya ka ikuku na-esi n'ụlọ apụ nke ọma ka anwụrụ ọkụ ghara ịmerụ ahụ.
Nchekwa Mmiri Ozuzo

Ọ bụrụ na ezinụlọ na-echekwa mmiri ozuzo, kpuchie ya nke ọma ka anwụnta ghara ịmụ nwa n'ime ya. Ihe ọ bụla nwere ike ịchịkọba mmiri — ọ bụladị okpu efere ma ọ bụ nchara — kwesịrị ịbụ ihe a na-ewụpụ mmiri ya ma ọ bụ kwatuo ya.

Ihe Dị Oke Mkpa Banyere Ịba

Ọ bụrụ na onye ọ bụla n'ezinụlọ achọọ ịnwe ahụ ọkụ (ịba), ihe mbụ ga-eme bụ ịga ụlọ ọgwụ ka a nyochaa ọbara ya (malaria test) tupu ọ malite ịṅụ ọgwụ. Ịṅụ ọgwụ ịba n'efu efu na-enweghị nyocha nwere ike:

Ime ka ọgwụ ịba ghara ịrụkwa ọrụ ọzọ n'ọdịnihu (drug resistance), nke ga-emetụta obodo niile.
Bụrụ ịtụfu ego, n'ihi na ọrịa ahụ nwere ike ọ bụghị ịba.

N'ọtụtụ ụlọ ọgwụ gọọmentị, nyocha ịba bụ n'efu ma ọ bụ ọnụ ahịa pere mpe.

Ijikọta ụzọ ndị a ọnụ — nkwụsịtụ, ịhịchapụ ebe mmiri na-anọ, imechi wịndoo, na iyiwe uwe nke kwesịrị ekwesị — ga-enye ezinụlọ nchekwa kachasị mma n'enweghị ịtụfu ego ukwuu.

Ezinụlọ bi n'akụkụ mmiri nwere ọtụtụ ụzọ ha nwere ike isi chebe onwe ha n'anwụnta n'enweghị ịkpọ ego dị ukwuu. Nke a bụ ihe ndị ha nwere ike ime:

Iwepụ ebe anwụnta na-amụ nwa

Anwụnta na-amụ nwa n'ime mmiri nọ jụụ. Ya mere, ezinụlọ ahụ kwesịrị ilekwasị anya n'iwepụ mmiri nọ jụụ n'ụlọ ha na gburugburu ya. Nke a pụtara: wụpụ mmiri nọ n'ime efere, taịa ochie, ite, na ihe ọ bụla nwere ike ịchịkọba mmiri ozuzo. Ọ bụrụ na e nwere olulu mmiri ma ọ bụ ite ịchịkọba mmiri n'ụlọ, ha kwesịrị ikpuchi ha nke ọma ka anwụnta ghara ịbanye n'ime ya ịtụ akwa ha.

Iji ihe a na-ahụ anya kpuchie windo na ụzọ

Ijide net ma ọ bụ akwa e ji ekpuchi windo na ụzọ — ọ bụladị akwa dị mfe — nwere ike ibelata ọnụ ọgụgụ anwụnta na-abanye n'ụlọ. Ọ bụrụ na ha enweghị net, ha nwere ike iji akwa dị mfe kpuchie oghere niile dị n'ụlọ.

Ịkwanye anwụnta n'oge abalị

Anwụnta na-ebute ịba na-ata mmadụ karịsịa n'oge uhuruchi ruo n'ụtụtụ. N'oge ndị a, ezinụlọ ahụ kwesịrị ịnọ n'ụlọ ma e nwere ike. Ha kwesịrị yi uwe ogologo — uwe aka ogologo na uwe ụkwụ ogologo — iji belata ahụ anwụnta nwere ike ịta.

Iji anwụ ụda ma ọ bụ ahịhịa achara anwụnta

Ọ bụrụ na ha enweghị ego ịzụ coil ma ọ bụ ihe ndị ọzọ, ịkpọ nku ahịhịa ụfọdụ dịka neem leaves (dongoyaro), lemongrass, ma ọ bụ ahịhịa citronella n'abalị nwere ike inyere aka ịchụ anwụnta. Nke a abụghị ụzọ kacha mma, mana ọ nwere ike inyere aka.

Ịgwa gọọmentị maka ụgbụ anwụnta n'efu

Ọtụtụ steeti na Nigeria na-enye ụgbụ anwụnta (insecticide-treated nets) n'efu site n'ọrụ gọọmentị na ụlọ ọrụ dịka WHO. Ezinụlọ ahụ kwesịrị ịjụ n'ụlọ ọgwụ gọọmentị ma ọ bụ primary health centre nke ha dịkarịsịa nso ka ha mara ma oge nkesa ụgbụ n'efu ọ bụla na-abịa. Ọtụtụ oge, a na-enyekwa ụmụ nwanyị dị ime na ụmụaka ndị dị n'okpuru afọ ise ụgbụ anwụnta n'efu n'oge ha na-aga clinic.

Ihicha gburugburu ụlọ

Igbucha ahịhịa dị n'akụkụ ụlọ, wepụ ihe ọ bụla anwụnta nwere ike izo n'ime ya, na ime ka gburugburu ụlọ dị mma nwere ike ibelata ọnụ ọgụgụ anwụnta.

Ihe dị mkpa ịmara:

Ọ bụrụ na onye ọ bụla n'ezinụlọ malite ịcha ahụ ọkụ — ọkachasị ụmụaka — ha kwesịrị ịga ụlọ ọgwụ ngwa ngwa ka e nwee ike nyochaa ha, chọpụta ma ọ bụ ịba, wee nye ha ọgwụ kwesịrị ekwesị. Ịṅụ ọgwụ na-enweghị nyocha (test) tupu e nwee ike bụ ihe ize ndụ, n'ihi na ọ nwere ike ghara ịbụ ịba, ọgwụ ahụ wee bụrụ ihe efu, ma mesịa mee ka ọgwụ ịba ghara ịrụkwa ọrụ ọzọ (drug resistance) n'oge dị n'ihu.

Ezinụlọ ahụ nwere ike ime ihe ndị a na-adịghị eri nnukwu ego:

Kwa izu, wụpụ ma sachaa mmiri kwụ ọtọ n’ime bọket, taya ochie, ite osisi na arịa ndị ọzọ. Kpuchie mmiri echekwara nke ọma.
Mechie ọnụ ụzọ ma kpuchie oghere dị na windo, ọnụ ụzọ na mgbidi site n’iji ụgbụ dị ọnụ ala ma ọ bụrụ na ọ kwe omume.
Yiri uwe aka ogologo, ogologo ọkpa na sọks, karịsịa mgbe anwụnta juru.
Jụọ ụlọọgwụ ma ọ bụ ndị ọrụ ahụike obodo ma ha na-enye ụgbụ anwụnta e tinyere ọgwụ n’efu ma ọ bụ ọnụ ala. Ụgbụ ndị a bụ otu n’ime ụzọ kachasị dị irè isi gbochie ịba.
Soro mmemme obodo maka ịfesa ọgwụ n’ime ụlọ ma ọ bụrụ na ndị ọrụ a zụrụ azụ na-enye ya.

Ọ bụrụ na onye ọ bụla enwee ahụ ọkụ, oyi ịma jijiji ma ọ bụ isi ọwụwa, gaa ụlọọgwụ ngwa ngwa maka nnwale ịba.

Ezinụlọ ahụ nwere ike ime ihe ndị a n’enweghị nnukwu ego:

Kwa abalị, rahụ n’okpuru ụgbụ anwụnta e tinyere ọgwụ. Jụọ ụlọọgwụ mpaghara ma ha na-enye ya n’efu ma ọ bụ ọnụ ala.
Kwa izu, wụpụ ma sachaa mmiri dị n’ime bọket, taya, ite na ihe ndị ọzọ na-anakọta mmiri.
Kpuchie mmiri echekwara nke ọma ma hichaa ọwa mmiri mechiri emechi.
Jiri ntupu dị ọnụ ala kpuchie oghere windo na ọnụ ụzọ.
Yiri uwe aka ogologo na ogologo ọkpa mgbe anwụnta juru.
Soro ndị agbataobi wepụ mmiri kwụ ọtọ gburugburu ụlọ.

Ọ bụrụ na ahụ ọkụ, isi ọwụwa ma ọ bụ oyi ịma jijiji amalite, gaa ebe ahụike maka nnwale ịba tupu ịṅụ ọgwụ.

Ezinụlọ ahụ nwere ike ime ihe ndị a dị ọnụ ala:

Rahụ n’okpuru ụgbụ anwụnta e tinyere ọgwụ kwa abalị. Jụọ ụlọọgwụ mpaghara ma ha na-enye ya n’efu ma ọ bụ ọnụ ala.
Kwa izu, wụpụ mmiri dị na bọket, taya na ite; kpuchie mmiri echekwara.

This is a common and potentially dangerous situation. Here's what needs to happen:

Get a proper diagnostic test

The most important next step is getting tested. A recurring fever that's been treated as malaria without confirmation could be something else entirely — typhoid, urinary tract infection, tuberculosis, HIV-related infections, brucellosis, or even a chronic condition like lymphoma. Treating blindly for malaria while the real cause goes unaddressed can be life-threatening.

Two reliable tests exist: a Rapid Diagnostic Test (RDT), which is affordable and widely available at clinics, and microscopy (a blood smear), which is more detailed and can identify the specific malaria parasite species and how heavy the infection is.

Why repeated presumptive treatment is risky

Repeatedly taking antimalarials without confirmed malaria does several harmful things. It exposes the body to unnecessary drug side effects. It contributes to antimalarial drug resistance in the community, which is a serious public health problem. And critically, it delays finding and treating the actual cause of the fever.

If it genuinely is recurring malaria

If testing confirms malaria keeps coming back, a health worker needs to determine why. Possible reasons include incomplete treatment courses (not finishing the full dosage), infection with Plasmodium vivax or P. ovale, which can relapse from dormant liver stages requiring specific treatment with primaquine, reinfection due to ongoing mosquito exposure, or drug-resistant parasites requiring a different antimalarial regimen.

What to do practically

Go to a health facility — not a pharmacy or drug vendor — and explain the full history: how many times fever has occurred, what drugs were taken, the doses, and whether full courses were completed. Request a blood test before any treatment is given. If malaria is negative, insist on further investigation for other causes of recurrent fever.

The bottom line: no one should keep treating a recurring fever as malaria without ever confirming that malaria is actually the problem. A test costs far less than repeated rounds of drugs that may not be addressing the real issue.

Why repeated unconfirmed treatment is risky

Taking antimalarials when malaria is not the actual problem wastes money on drugs that will not help, delays treatment of the real illness, exposes the person to unnecessary drug side effects, and contributes to antimalarial drug resistance in the community. Drug resistance is a serious public health concern — when parasites are exposed to antimalarials unnecessarily or in incomplete doses, they can develop the ability to survive those drugs, making them less effective for everyone over time.

What to expect at the health facility

A health worker should take a blood sample, run a malaria test, and only prescribe antimalarials if the test is positive. If the test is negative, they should investigate other causes of the recurring fever through further examination and possibly additional tests.

Incomplete treatment is one of the most common reasons malaria seems to "come back" — the parasites are not fully cleared from the body and recrudesce once drug levels drop.

Practical considerations

In many settings, government-run primary health centres offer malaria testing free of charge or at very low cost. Artemisinin-based combination therapies (ACTs), which are the WHO-recommended first-line treatment for uncomplicated falciparum malaria, are also often available free or subsidised at public facilities. This makes proper testing and treatment potentially cheaper in the long run than repeated cycles of buying antimalarials from pharmacies or patent medicine vendors without confirmation.

The bottom line

Stop treating without testing. Get tested. If positive, take the full course of the prescribed medication exactly as directed — every dose, for the full number of days, even if symptoms improve before the course is finished. If negative, work with a health professional to find out what is actually causing the fever. Continuing to guess is not just ineffective — it is actively harmful to both the individual and the wider community.

Repeatedly taking antimalarials without confirmed malaria does several damaging things at once. It exposes the person to unnecessary side effects. It delays identification of what is actually wrong. It wastes limited household resources on drugs that are not addressing the problem. And it contributes to antimalarial drug resistance at the community level — parasites exposed to drugs unnecessarily or through incomplete courses can evolve to survive those drugs, which threatens the effectiveness of treatment for everyone.

Incomplete courses are another common culprit

If some of these episodes genuinely were malaria, there is a strong possibility the person did not complete the full prescribed course of medication each time. Many people stop taking antimalarials once they feel better, often after two days of a three-day course. This leaves surviving parasites in the bloodstream. They multiply again, and the fever returns — not as a new infection, but as a recurrence of the same one. This is called recrudescence and it is one of the most frequent reasons for so-called "repeated malaria."

What should happen at the health facility

A health worker should draw blood, run a malaria test, and prescribe treatment only based on the result. If positive, the person should receive an artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT), which is the WHO-recommended first-line treatment for uncomplicated falciparum malaria, and must take every single dose for the full duration of the course even after feeling better. If the test is negative, the health worker should investigate other causes through clinical examination and possibly further laboratory tests.

Cost should not be a barrier

In many countries, particularly across sub-Saharan Africa, government primary health centres and public hospitals offer free or heavily subsidised malaria testing and ACT treatment. Ironically, the cycle of repeatedly buying antimalarials from pharmacies or patent medicine vendors without testing often ends up costing far more than a single proper clinic visit with confirmed diagnosis and correct treatment.

Ẹni náà kò yẹ kí ó máa tún lo oògùn ibà léraléra láì ṣe àyẹ̀wò. Ara gbígbóná tó ń padà wá lè jẹ́ ibà, ṣùgbọ́n ó tún lè ní ìdí mìíràn.

Ohun tó yẹ kí ó ṣe ni:

Lọ sí ilé ìwòsàn tàbí ibi ìtọ́jú tó yẹ fún àyẹ̀wò ibà, bíi malaria rapid diagnostic test (RDT) tàbí microscopy.
Jẹ́ kí oníṣègùn ṣàyẹ̀wò bóyá àìsàn mìíràn ló ń fa ara gbígbóná náà, pàápàá nítorí pé ìtọ́jú ibà tẹ́lẹ̀ kò dá a dúró.
Má ṣe bẹ̀rẹ̀ oògùn ibà tuntun tàbí tún oògùn àtijọ́ ṣe láìsí ìmòràn oníṣègùn.
Sọ fún oníṣègùn gbogbo oògùn ibà tí ẹni náà ti lò, iye ọjọ́ tí ó fi lò ó, àti bóyá ó parí ìtọ́jú náà dáadáa.

Bí ẹni náà bá ní ìṣòro mímí, ìdàrúdàpọ̀ ọpọlọ, ìgbẹ̀mìí, ìfarapa tàbí ìṣubú, ìgbagbogbo tó pọ̀, ailagbara gan-an, tàbí kò lè mu omi, ó yẹ kí ó gba ìtọ́jú pajawiri lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ.

Ìlànà gbogbogbo WHO ni pé, níbi tí àyẹ̀wò ibà ti wà, a yẹ kí a jẹ́rìí àìsàn ibà pẹ̀lú àyẹ̀wò kí a tó ṣe ìtọ́jú, dípò fífi gbogbo ara gbígbóná sílẹ̀ gẹ́gẹ́ bí ibà.

Èyí jẹ́ ọ̀ràn tó ṣe pàtàkì gan-an, mo sì máa sọ̀rọ̀ rẹ̀ ní tààrà.

Ìṣòro náà ni èyí: Tí ènìyàn bá ń mu oògùn ibà léraléra láì ṣe ìdánwò ẹ̀jẹ̀ (bíi malaria RDT tàbí microscopy), ó lè jẹ́ pé:

Ohun tó ń ṣe ènìyàn náà kì í ṣe ibà rárá. Àwọn àìsàn mìíràn wà tí ara gbígbóná jẹ́ àmì wọn, bí àpẹẹrẹ: àrùn typhoid, àkóràn inú ìtọ̀ (urinary tract infection), àkóràn HIV, àìsàn Koch (tuberculosis/TB), tàbí àwọn àkóràn mìíràn. Tí ènìyàn bá ń tọ́jú ibà tí kò sí, àìsàn gidi tó wà nínú ara máa ń bá a lọ láì gba ìtọ́jú tó yẹ.

Bákannáà, tí ó bá jẹ́ ibà nítòótọ́ ṣùgbọ́n ó ń padà wá léraléra, ó lè jẹ́ pé oògùn tó ń lò kò ṣiṣẹ́ mọ́ (drug resistance), tàbí pé kò parí ìtọ́jú náà dáadáa, tàbí pé irú ibà tó ṣe pàtàkì jù bẹ́ẹ̀ lọ ló ní (bíi Plasmodium vivax tàbí P. ovale tí ó lè fara pamọ́ sínú ẹ̀dọ̀).

Ohun tó yẹ kí ẹni náà ṣe báyìí:

Kọ́kọ́ lọ ṣe àyẹ̀wò ẹ̀jẹ̀ ní ilé ìwòsàn tó dáa. Ìdánwò ibà (malaria test) jẹ́ ohun àkọ́kọ́, ṣùgbọ́n kì í ṣe ìyẹn nìkan. Ó yẹ kí dókítà náà tún ṣe àyẹ̀wò fún àwọn àrùn mìíràn bíi typhoid (Widal test tàbí blood culture), àyẹ̀wò ẹ̀jẹ̀ kíkún (full blood count), àyẹ̀wò ìtọ̀ (urinalysis), àti bẹ́ẹ̀ bẹ́ẹ̀ lọ, kí wọ́n lè mọ ohun tó ń fa ara gbígbóná náà nítòótọ́.

Má ṣe tún mu oògùn ibà mọ́ láì ní ẹ̀rí pé ibà ló wà nínú ara. Títọ́jú àìsàn tí a kò ṣe ìdánwò rẹ̀ lè fi ewu sí ènìyàn, nítorí pé oògùn ibà tí kò pọn dandan lè ṣe ìpalára fún ẹ̀dọ̀ àti kíndìnrín, ó sì lè mú kí kòkòrò ibà di alágídí sí oògùn (antimicrobial resistance).

Tí àbájáde ìdánwò bá fi hàn pé ibà ló jẹ́ nítòótọ́, kí dókítà yan irú oògùn tó tọ́ fún ọ̀, kí o sì parí gbogbo ìtọ́jú náà dáadáa. Kí wọ́n tún ṣe ìdánwò lẹ́yìn ìtọ́jú láti rí i pé kòkòrò ibà ti kúrò nínú ẹ̀jẹ̀.

Tí àbájáde bá fi hàn pé kì í ṣe ibà, ìyẹn túmọ̀ sí pé àìsàn mìíràn ló ń ṣe ènìyàn, dókítà sì ni láti ṣe àwọn ìwádìí síwájú síi.

Ní kúkúrú: àyẹ̀wò kí a tó tọ́jú — ìyẹn ni ìlànà tó tọ́. Oògùn láì ní ìdánwò jẹ́ ewu.

Ohun tó ṣe pàtàkì jù lọ tí ẹni yìí gbọ́dọ̀ ṣe ni láti dáwọ́ ìtọ́jú aláìlérí dúró, kí ó sì lọ ṣe àyẹ̀wò kí ó tó tún mu oògùn kankan.

Lọ sí ilé-ìwòsàn, ṣe àyẹ̀wò ẹ̀jẹ̀ kí o tó mu oògùn

Ẹni náà gbọ́dọ̀ lọ sí ilé-ìṣẹ́ ìlera — ibẹ̀ ni wọ́n óti ṣe àyẹ̀wò ẹ̀jẹ̀ rẹ̀, yálà nípasẹ̀ RDT (Rapid Diagnostic Test) tàbí kí wọ́n wo ẹ̀jẹ̀ rẹ̀ lábẹ́ microscope. Láìsí àyẹ̀wò, kò sí ọ̀nà tí a lè fi mọ̀ bóyá ibà gan-an ni ó ń ṣe ẹni náà.

Àìsàn mìíràn tún lè fa ara gbígbóná

Ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àrùn mìíràn lè fa ibà tí yóò jọ ibà malaria ṣùgbọ́n tí kì í ṣe malaria rárá. Typhoid lè fa á. Ikọ́ ẹ̀dọ̀fóró (TB) lè fa á. Àkóràn inú ara lè fa á. Àrùn ito (UTI) pàápàá lè fa á. Gbogbo àwọn àìsàn wọ̀nyí nílò oògùn tó yàtọ̀ pátápátá. Nítorí náà, tí ẹnìkan bá ń gba oògùn ibà lọ́wọ́ láìsí àyẹ̀wò, owó ló ń sọnù, àrùn gidi tó ń ṣe é sì ń burú sí i nítorí pé kò sí ẹni tí ó ti ṣàwárí rẹ̀.

Ìpalára tí ìtọ́jú láìlérí ń fa

Bí ẹnìkan bá ń mu oògùn ibà léraléra láìsí ìdánilójú pé ibà ni, ó ń fa ìṣòro púpọ̀:

Ni àkọ́kọ́, oògùn tí ara rẹ kò nílò ló ń tẹ̀ sínú ara — èyí sì ní ipa búburú tirẹ̀. Ni èkejì, ó ń ṣòfò owó tí ó bá ti lò fún ìtọ́jú tó tọ́. Ni ẹ̀kẹta — èyí sì kan gbogbo ènìyàn — ó ń ṣe ìrànlọ́wọ́ kí oògùn ibà má ṣiṣẹ́ mọ́ lọ́jọ́ iwájú. Àwọn ohun alààyè kékeré tó ń fa ibà (parasites) tí wọ́n bá ń rí oògùn nígbà tí kò yẹ, tàbí tí ẹni tó ń mu oògùn náà kò bá parí rẹ̀, wọ́n lè kọ́ bí wọ́n ṣe máa yè bọ́ lọ́wọ́ oògùn náà. Wọ́n ń pè é ní drug resistance. Tí èyí bá ṣẹlẹ̀, oògùn náà kì yóò ṣiṣẹ́ mọ́ — kì í ṣe fún ẹni kan ṣoṣo, ṣùgbọ́n fún gbogbo àwùjọ.

Bóyá ẹni náà kò ń parí oògùn rẹ̀

Ìdí pàtàkì kan tí ara gbígbóná fi ń padà wá ni pé ọ̀pọ̀ ènìyàn kì í parí oògùn ibà wọn. Wọ́n máa ń mu ú fún ọjọ́ méjì, tí wọ́n bá rí i pé ara wọn ti dára díẹ̀, wọ́n á dáwọ́ dúró. Ṣùgbọ́n àwọn parasites kò tíì kú patapata nínú ẹ̀jẹ̀. Lẹ́yìn ọjọ́ díẹ̀, wọ́n á tún pọ̀ sí i, ibà sì á tún padà wá. Kì í ṣe ibà tuntun ni — àtijọ́ náà ni tí kò kú tán. Ìdí nìyí tí ẹnìkan bá fún ọ ní oògùn ọjọ́ mẹ́ta, o gbọ́dọ̀ mu gbogbo rẹ̀ tán, kódà bí o bá ti rí i pé ara rẹ ti dára kí o tó parí rẹ̀.

Kí ni yóò ṣẹlẹ̀ ní ilé-ìwòsàn

Nígbà tí ẹni náà bá dé ilé-ìṣẹ́ ìlera, oṣiṣẹ́ ìlera yóò gba ẹ̀jẹ̀ rẹ̀, yóò ṣe àyẹ̀wò, yóò sì sọ àbájáde rẹ̀ fún un. Tí ibà bá jẹ́ positive, wọ́n á fún un ní oògùn ACT — èyí ni oògùn tí WHO sọ pé ó dára jù lọ fún ìtọ́jú ibà. Ó gbọ́dọ̀ mu gbogbo rẹ̀ fún ọjọ́ mẹ́ta, kò gbọ́dọ̀ fo ọjọ́ kankan, kò sì gbọ́dọ̀ dáwọ́ dúró láàárín.

Tí àbájáde àyẹ̀wò bá jẹ́ negative — ìyẹn túmọ̀ sí pé ohun mìíràn ló ń fa ara gbígbóná náà. Oṣiṣẹ́ ìlera yóò ṣe àyẹ̀wò síwájú sí i, yóò wá ohun tó ń ṣe é gan-an, yóò sì fún un ní ìtọ́jú tó tọ́.

Má jẹ́ kí owó dí ọ lọ́wọ́

Ní ọ̀pọ̀ ibi ní Nàìjíríà, ilé-ìwòsàn ìjọba àti primary health centre ń ṣe àyẹ̀wò ibà lọ́fẹ̀ẹ́ tàbí ní owó kékeré. Oògùn ACT náà pàápàá máa ń wà lọ́fẹ̀ẹ́ ní ilé-ìṣẹ́ ìlera ti ìjọba. Ohun tó burú ni pé, tí o bá ṣe àkọsílẹ̀ gbogbo owó tí ẹni náà ti ná láti ra oògùn ibà ní ọjà tàbí ní chemist láìsí àyẹ̀wò — lẹ́ẹ̀kan lẹ́yìn lẹ́ẹ̀kan — owó náà lè ju ti ìbẹ̀wò ilé-ìwòsàn kan ṣoṣo tí a fi ṣe àyẹ̀wò tó péye lọ. Nítorí náà, àyẹ̀wò kì í ṣe ìṣòfò owó — àfipamọ́ owó ni.

Ní ṣókí

Ẹni yìí gbọ́dọ̀ dáwọ́ àtètè-mu-oògùn dúró. Ó yẹ kí ó lọ sí ilé-ìwòsàn. Kí ó ṣe àyẹ̀wò. Tí ibà bá jẹ́ẹ, kí ó mu oògùn náà tán pátápátá, kí ó má fi ọjọ́ kankan sílẹ̀. Tí kì bá ṣe ibà, kí dókítà wá ohun tó ń ṣe é gan-an kí ó sì tọ́jú ìyẹn. Ṣíṣe àtètè mu oògùn láìsí àyẹ̀wò kì í ṣe ìrànlọ́wọ́ — ewu ló ń mú wá fún ẹni náà fúnra rẹ̀, ó sì ń ba agbára oògùn ibà jẹ́ fún àwọn ènìyàn mìíràn pẹ̀lú.

Ohun tó yẹ kí ẹni yìí ṣe lọ́wọ́lọ́wọ́ ni láti dawọ́ mímú oògùn lásán dúró, kí ó sì lọ ṣe àyẹ̀wò ẹ̀jẹ̀ kí ó tó tún gbà ìtọ́jú èyíkéyìí.

Lọ sí ilé-ìṣẹ́ ìlera, jẹ́ kí wọ́n ṣe àyẹ̀wò kí o tó mu oògùn

Ẹni náà gbọ́dọ̀ lọ sí ilé-ìwòsàn tàbí primary health centre kí wọ́n lè ṣe àyẹ̀wò ẹ̀jẹ̀ rẹ̀ — yálà RDT (Rapid Diagnostic Test) tàbí kí wọ́n fi microscope wo ẹ̀jẹ̀ rẹ̀. Láìsí àyẹ̀wò, kò sí ọ̀nà láti mọ̀ dájúdájú bóyá ibà malaria gan-an ló ń ṣe ẹni náà.

Kì í ṣe ibà nìkan ló ń fa ara gbígbóná

Àrùn mìíràn púpọ̀ lè mú kí ara gbóná ní ọ̀nà tí yóò jọ ibà malaria pátápátá ṣùgbọ́n tí kì í ṣe malaria rárá:

Typhoid lè fa á. Ikọ́ ẹ̀dọ̀fóró (TB) lè fa á. Àkóràn oríṣiríṣi nínú ara lè fa á. Àrùn ito (UTI) pàápàá lè fa á. Àwọn àìsàn wọ̀nyìí nílò oògùn tó yàtọ̀ pátápátá sí oògùn ibà. Tó bá jẹ́ pé ẹnìkan ń mu oògùn ibà nígbà tí kì í ṣe ibà ló ń ṣe é, àrùn gidi tó wà nínú ara rẹ̀ ń burú sí i lójoojúmọ́ nítorí pé kò sí ẹni tí ó mọ̀ pé ó wà, owó sì ń lọ sí oògùn tí kò wúlò.

Ewu tí ìtọ́jú alábòsí ń fa

Mímú oògùn ibà léraléra láìsí ìmọ̀ dájú pé ibà ni ń ṣe ẹni náà ń fa ìṣòro ní onà mẹ́ta:

Ni àkọ́kọ́, ó ń fi oògùn tí ara kò nílò sínú ara — oògùn kọ̀ọ̀kan sì ní ipa búburú tó lè ṣe. Ni èkejì, owó ló ń sọnù — owó tí ẹni náà bá ti lò fún ìtọ́jú àrùn gidi tó ń ṣe é. Ni ẹ̀kẹta, ó ń ba agbára oògùn ibà jẹ́ fún gbogbo àwùjọ. Àwọn ohun alààyè kékeré tó ń fa ibà — tí wọ́n bá pàdé oògùn ní ìgbà tí kò tọ́, tàbí tí ẹni tó ń mu oògùn kò bá parí rẹ̀ — wọ́n lè dàgbà sí agbára oògùn náà. Wọ́n ń pè é ní drug resistance. Ìyẹn túmọ̀ sí pé oògùn yẹn kì yóò ṣiṣẹ́ mọ́ — kì í ṣe fún ẹni kan ṣoṣo, fún àwọn ènìyàn mìíràn nínú àdúgbò náà pẹ̀lú.

Àìparí oògùn lè jẹ́ ìdí tí ibà fi ń padà wá

Ìdí tó wọ́pọ̀ gan-an tí ara gbígbóná fi máa ń padà wá ni pé ọ̀pọ̀ ènìyàn kì í parí oògùn ibà wọn. Ẹni tó bá mu oògùn fún ọjọ́ méjì nínú ọjọ́ mẹ́ta tí a fún un, tó sì rí i pé ara rẹ̀ ti dára, ó máa ń dáwọ́ dúró. Ṣùgbọ́n àwọn parasites nínú ẹ̀jẹ̀ kò tíì kú patapata. Lẹ́yìn ọjọ́ díẹ̀, wọ́n á bẹ̀rẹ̀ sí pọ̀ sí i, ibà sì á padà wá. Kì í ṣe ibà tuntun ni — àtijọ́ náà ló tún gbóòrì nítorí pé a kò pa á rẹ́ pátápátá. Ìyẹn ni wọ́n ń pè ní recrudescence. Nítorí èyí, tí dókítà bá fún ẹnìkan ní oògùn ọjọ́ mẹ́ta, ó gbọ́dọ̀ mu gbogbo rẹ̀ tán — ọjọ́ kọ̀ọ̀kan, dóòsì kọ̀ọ̀kan — bí ó tilẹ̀ rí i pé ó ti lára dáa kí oògùn tó parí.

Ohun tí yóò ṣẹlẹ̀ ní ilé-ìṣẹ́ ìlera

Oṣiṣẹ́ ìlera yóò gba ẹ̀jẹ̀ ẹni náà, yóò ṣe àyẹ̀wò rẹ̀, yóò sì sọ àbájáde fún un.

Tí àbájáde bá jẹ́ positive — ibà ni. Wọ́n á fún un ní oògùn ACT (Artemisinin-based Combination Therapy), èyí tí WHO sọ pé ó jẹ́ oògùn tó dára jù lọ fún ìtọ́jú ibà malaria tí kò ṣe le jù. Ó gbọ́dọ̀ mu gbogbo dóòsì fún ọjọ́ mẹ́ta ní kíkún, láì fo ẹ̀yọ kan, láì dáwọ́ dúró ní àárín.

Tí àbájáde bá jẹ́ negative — ìyẹn fihàn pé nǹkan mìíràn ló ń fa ara gbígbóná náà. Oṣiṣẹ́ ìlera yóò ṣe àyẹ̀wò síwájú sí i, yóò wá orísun àìsàn gidi, yóò sì fún un ní ìtọ́jú tó péye.

Owó kò gbọ́dọ̀ di ìdènà

Ní ọ̀pọ̀ ibi ní Nàìjíríà, àwọn ilé-ìwòsàn ìjọba àti primary health centre ń ṣe àyẹ̀wò ibà lọ́fẹ̀ẹ́ tàbí pẹ̀lú owó kékeré. Oògùn ACT pàápàá sábà máa ń wà ní ọ̀fẹ́ ní àwọn ilé-ìṣẹ́ ìlera ti ìjọba. Ohun tó jẹ́ iyàlẹ́nu ni pé tí ẹnìkan bá ṣàkọsílẹ̀ gbogbo owó tí ó ti ná ní pharmacy tàbí ní ọ̀dọ̀ chemist láti ra oògùn ibà léraléra láìsí àyẹ̀wò, owó yẹn lè pọ̀ ju owó ìbẹ̀wò ilé-ìwòsàn kan ṣoṣo lọ — ìbẹ̀wò tí yóò fún un ní àyẹ̀wò tó péye àti ìtọ́jú tó tọ́. Àyẹ̀wò kì í ṣe ìsọnùowó — àfipamọ́ owó ni.

Ní kúkúrú

Ẹni yìí gbọ́dọ̀ dáwọ́ àfojúdí-mú-oògùn dúró. Kí ó lọ sí ilé-ìwòsàn. Kí ó ṣe àyẹ̀wò. Tí ibà bá jẹ́ẹ, kí ó mu oògùn rẹ̀ tán pátápátá, kí ó má fo dóòsì kankan. Tí kì bá ṣe ibà, kí dókítà wá ohun tó ń ṣe é gan-an, kí ó sì tọ́jú ìyẹn. Sísọ̀rọ̀ ìkẹyìn, ṣíṣe àtètè mu oògùn ibà láìsí àyẹ̀wò kì í ṣe ìrànwọ́ fún ẹni náà — ewu ló jẹ́ fún àìlera rẹ̀ fúnra rẹ̀, ó sì ń ba agbára oògùn ibà jẹ́ fún gbogbo àwùjọ.

Ẹni náà yẹ kí ó dáwọ́ ìtọ́jú ara rẹ̀ dúró, kí ó sì lọ sí ilé ìwòsàn ní kíákíá.

Ṣe àyẹ̀wò malaria, RDT tàbí microscopy, kí ó tó tún lo oògùn malaria.
Sọ fún oníṣègùn gbogbo oògùn tí ó ti lò àti ìgbà tí ara gbígbóná ń padà.
Bí àyẹ̀wò kò bá fi malaria hàn, kí oníṣègùn ṣàyẹ̀wò àwọn ohun mìíràn tó lè fa ara gbígbóná náà.
Lọ gba ìtọ́jú pajawiri bí ìdàrúdàpọ̀, ìkọ̀lù, ìṣòro mímí, àìmọ̀kan tàbí àìlera tó pọ̀ bá ṣẹlẹ̀.

Ìtọ́jú malaria léraléra láì ṣe àyẹ̀wò lè mú kí ìdánimọ̀ àìsàn gidi pẹ́.

Ẹni náà yẹ kí ó dáwọ́ lílo oògùn malaria fúnra rẹ̀, kí ó sì lọ sí ilé ìwòsàn ní kíákíá.

Ṣe àyẹ̀wò malaria, RDT tàbí microscopy, kí ó tó tún lo oògùn.
Sọ gbogbo oògùn tí ó ti lò fún oníṣègùn.
Bí àyẹ̀wò kò bá fi malaria hàn, kí wọ́n ṣàyẹ̀wò ohun mìíràn tó ń fa ara gbígbóná náà.
Bí ìdàrúdàpọ̀, ìkọ̀lù, ìṣòro mímí tàbí pípàdánù ìmọ̀ bá ṣẹlẹ̀, gba ìtọ́jú pajawiri lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀.

Ìtọ́jú léraléra láì ṣe àyẹ̀wò lè mú kí ìdánimọ̀ àìsàn gidi pẹ́.

Ẹni náà yẹ kí ó dáwọ́ lílo oògùn malaria fúnra rẹ̀, kí ó sì lọ sí ilé ìwòsàn ní kíákíá.

Ṣe àyẹ̀wò malaria, RDT tàbí microscopy, kí ó tó tún lo oògùn.
Sọ gbogbo oògùn tí ó ti lò fún oníṣègùn.
Bí àyẹ̀wò kò bá fi malaria hàn, kí oníṣègùn ṣàyẹ̀wò ohun mìíràn tó ń fa ara gbígbóná náà.
Gba ìtọ́jú pajawiri bí ìdàrúdàpọ̀, ìkọ̀lù, ìṣòro mímí tàbí pípàdánù ìmọ̀ bá ṣẹlẹ̀.

Ìtọ́jú léraléra láì ṣe àyẹ̀wò lè mú kí ìdánimọ̀ àìsàn gidi pẹ́.

Onye ahụ kwesịrị ịga hụ onye ọrụ ahụike ruru eru ngwa ngwa. Ọ gaghị aṅụ ọgwụ ịba ọzọ ruo mgbe e mere ya nyocha.

Ahụ ọkụ na-alọghachi nwere ike ịbụ ọrịa ịba, ọrịa ịba ọhụrụ, ọgwụgwọ a na-emechaghị, ọgwụ na-ekwesịghị ekwesị, ma ọ bụ ọrịa ọzọ. A pụghị iji naanị mgbaàmà mata ihe kpatara ya.

Onye ahụ kwesịrị:

Ime malaria rapid diagnostic test ma ọ bụ nyocha ọbara n’okpuru microscope. Onye ọrụ ahụike nwere ike imegharị nyocha ahụ ma ọ bụ mee nyocha ndị ọzọ ma ọ bụrụ na ọ dị mkpa.
Ịgwa onye ọrụ ahụike oge ahụ ọkụ ọ bụla malitere na ọgwụ niile ọ ṅụrụ, gụnyere aha ọgwụ, ole ọ ṅụrụ, ụbọchị ọ ṅụrụ ha na ọgwụ Igbo ọ bụla.
Ịkọ ma o mechara usoro ọgwụgwọ ọ bụla dịka e nyere ya.
Iburu akpa ọgwụ ndị ahụ ma ọ bụ foto doro anya nke aha ha gaa ebe ahụike, ma ọ bụrụ na o nwere ha.
Ikwere ka onye ọrụ ahụike chọpụta ihe ndị ọzọ nwere ike ịkpata ahụ ọkụ ahụ, kama iche na ahụ ọkụ ọ bụla bụ ọrịa ịba.
Izere ọgwụ fọdụrụ n’ụlọ, ọgwụ e nyere onye ọzọ ma ọ bụ ọgwụ a na-amaghị ihe ndị mejupụtara ya.
Ịkpọtụrụ dọkịta nyere ya ọgwụ ma ọ bụrụ na ọ ka na-aṅụ ọgwụ ugbu a, tupu ọ kwụsị ma ọ bụ gbanwee ya.

Chọọ enyemaka mberede ozugbo ma ọ bụrụ na onye ahụ amalite ịgbagwoju anya, nwee akwụkwụ, iku ume esie ya ike, tụfuo onwe ya, daa mba nke ukwuu, na-agbọ agbọ ugboro ugboro, enweghị ike ịṅụ mmiri, na-agba ọbara n’ụzọ pụrụ iche, anya ma ọ bụ akpụkpọ ahụ acha odo, ma ọ bụ mamịrị ya agbaa ọchịchịrị nke ukwuu.

Ụmụaka, ụmụ nwaanyị dị ime, ndị agadi na ndị usoro nchebe ahụ ha adịghị ike kwesịrị inweta nyocha ahụike ngwa ngwa.

Ihe kacha mkpa nke onye a kwesịrị ime bụ ịga nyocha tupu ọ ṅụọ ogwụ ọ bụla ọzọ. Ọ gaghị adị mma ịnọgide na-aṅụ ogwụ ịba n'enweghị ihe gosiri na ọ bụ ịba kpatara ọkụ ahụ.
Gaa ụlọ ọgwụ mee nyocha

Onye a kwesịrị ịga ụlọ ọgwụ maọbụ ebe a na-ahụ maka ahụike — ọ bụghị ụlọ ahịa ogwụ — ma rịọ ka a nyochaa ọbara ya tupu a nye ya ogwụ ọ bụla. Ụdị nyocha abụọ dị: otu bụ Rapid Diagnostic Test (RDT) nke dị ọnụ ala ma na-eme ngwa ngwa, nke ọzọ bụ inyocha ọbara n'okpuru igwe enyocha ihe (microscope) nke na-enye nkọwa zuru ezu karịa. Ọ bụla n'ime ha ga-egosi ma ọ bụ ịba ka-abụ ihe na-akpata ọkụ ahụ n'ezie.

Ihe mere ịgwọ n'enweghị nyocha ji dị njọ

Ọtụtụ ọrịa nwere ike ịkpata ọkụ ahụ yiri ịba — dịka typhoid, nje dị n'ahụ, TB (ụkwara nta), maọbụ ọrịa ndị ọzọ dị njọ. Ọ bụrụ na onye ahụ na-aṅụ ogwụ ịba ebe ọ bụ ọrịa ọzọ na-akpata nsogbu ahụ, ọrịa ahụ ga-anọgide na-aka njọ n'ihi na ọ nweghị onye na-agwọ ya. Ọzọkwa, ịnọgide na-aṅụ ogwụ ịba n'enweghị isi na-eme ka ogwụ ahụ ghara ịrụ ọrụ ọzọ n'obodo — nke a bụ nsogbu dị ukwuu nye mmadụ niile.

Ọ bụrụ na nyocha gosiri na ọ bụ ịba n'ezie

Ọ bụrụ na nyocha kwenye na ọ bụ ịba, dọkịta kwesịrị ịchọpụta ihe kpatara ọ na-alọghachi:

Onye ahụ nwere ike ọ naghị edemecha ogwụ ya nke ọma — ọ na-akwụsị mgbe ọ malitere ịdị mma ma ọ gụchabeghị oge ogwụ ahụ
Ọ nwere ike ịbụ ụdị ịba (Plasmodium vivax maọbụ P. ovale) nke nwere ike izo n'ime imeju ma laghachi, nke chọrọ ogwụ pụrụ iche dịka primaquine
Ọ nwekwara ike ịbụ na anwụnta ka na-ata ya, nke pụtara na ọ na-enwetakarị ọrịa ịba ọhụrụ kwa oge
Maọbụ na ogwụ ịba ọ na-eji agwọ ebiela ike — ọ naghị arụ ọrụ ọzọ, ya mere a ga-agbanwe ụdị ogwụ

Ọ bụrụ na nyocha gosiri na ọ bụghị ịba

Nke a bụ ebe dị oke mkpa. Ọ bụrụ na nyocha gosiri na ọ bụghị ịba, onye ahụ ekwesịghị ekwe ka onye ọ bụla nye ya ogwụ ịba. Kama, ọ kwesịrị ịrịọ dọkịta ka a nyochaa ya maka ihe ndị ọzọ — nyocha ọbara ndị ọzọ, nyocha mamịrị, na nyocha ndị ọzọ nwere ike igosi ihe na-akpata ọkụ ahụ n'ezie.

Ihe onye ahụ kwesịrị ime ugbu a

Ọ kwesịrị ịga ebe a na-ahụ maka ahụike ma kọwaa ihe niile — ugboro ole ọ gwọrọ ịba, ụdị ogwụ ọ ṅụrụ, ma ọ gụchara oge ogwụ ya, na otu ọkụ ahụ si eme. Ọ kwesịrị ịsị na a ga-eme nyocha tupu a nye ya ogwụ ọ bụla.

Okwu ikpeazụ bụ nke a: ogwụ a na-aṅụ n'enweghị nyocha nwere ike imefu ego, merụọ ahụ, ma mee ka ọrịa nke na-akpata nsogbu ahụ n'ezie ka njọ. Otu nyocha nwere ike ịzọpụta mmadụ ego na ahụhụ karịa ịnọgide na-aṅụ ogwụ kpom kwem kwa mgbe ọkụ ahụ bịara.

Ihe onye a kwesịrị ime bụ ịkwụsị ịṅụ ogwụ ịba n'enweghi nyocha, gaa ụlọ ọgwụ ka a nyochaa ya nke ọma.

Mee nyocha ọbara tupu ihe ọ bụla

Onye a kwesịrị ịga ụlọ ọgwụ maọbụ ebe ahụike — ọ bụghị ụlọ ahịa ogwụ — ma rịọ ka a nyochaa ọbara ya. Ụdị nyocha abụọ dị nke na-arụ ọrụ nke ọma: Rapid Diagnostic Test (RDT) nke dị ọnụ ala ma na-enye nkwenye ngwa ngwa, na nyocha ọbara n'okpuru microscope nke na-egosi ụdị ịba nke kpatara ya na ịdị njọ nke ọrịa ahụ. Tupu a mee otu n'ime nyocha ndị a, ọ dịghị onye maara ma ọ bụ ịba ka-abụ nsogbu ahụ.

Ihe mere nyocha ji dị mkpa nke ukwuu

Ọkụ ahụ na-alọghachi enweghị ike ịbụ ịba. Ọtụtụ ọrịa ndị ọzọ na-akpata ọkụ ahụ nke yiri ịba nke ukwuu — dịka typhoid, ọrịa nje dị n'ụzọ mamịrị, TB, brucellosis, maọbụ ọbụna ọrịa dị njọ ndị ọzọ. Ọ bụrụ na onye a nọgidere na-aṅụ ogwụ ịba ebe ọrịa ọzọ bụ ihe na-akpata nsogbu ya, ọrịa ahụ ga-anọgide na-aka njọ oge niile n'ihi na ọ nweghị onye na-ahụ ya anya.

Ọzọkwa, ịnọgide na-aṅụ ogwụ ịba n'enweghị ihe kwesịrị ekwesị na-eweta nsogbu abụọ ndị ọzọ: ọ na-emetụta ahụ n'enweghị isi, ma ọ na-emekwa ka ogwụ ịba ghara ịdị ire ọzọ n'obodo — ihe ndị ọkachamara na-akpọ "drug resistance."

Ọ bụrụ na nyocha kwenye na ọ bụ ịba

Dọkịta ga-achọpụta ihe kpatara ịba ahụ ji na-alọghachi. Ihe ụfọdụ nwere ike ịbụ:

Onye ahụ anaghị ezu oge ogwụ ya — ọ na-akwụsị ịṅụ ogwụ ozugbo ahụ malitere ịdị ya mma, nke a na-eme ka ụfọdụ nje ịba fọdụrụ n'ahụ
Ụdị ịba ụfọdụ dịka Plasmodium vivax na P. ovale nwere ike izo n'imeju (liver) wee laghachi oge ụfọdụ gasịrị — ụdị a chọrọ ogwụ pụrụ iche dịka primaquine iji kpochapụ ya kpamkpam
Anwụnta nwere ike ịnọgide na-ata onye ahụ, ya mere ọ na-enweta ịba ọhụrụ kwa oge
Ogwụ ịba nke ọ na-eji nwere ike ọ naghị arụ ọrụ ọzọ, ya mere a ga-agbanwe ụdị ogwụ

Ọ bụrụ na nyocha gosiri na ọ bụghị ịba

Nke a nwere ike ịbụ ihe kacha mkpa n'ime ihe niile. Ọ bụrụ na nyocha gosiri na ọ bụghị ịba, onye ahụ ekwesịghị ekwe ka a nye ya ogwụ ịba. Kama, ọ kwesịrị ịrịọ dọkịta ka a gbasoo nyocha ndị ọzọ — nyocha ọbara zuru ezu, nyocha mamịrị, nyocha typhoid, na ihe ndị ọzọ — iji chọpụta ihe na-akpata ọkụ ahụ n'ezie.

Ihe onye ahụ ga-eme ugbu a

Ọ kwesịrị ịga ụlọ ọgwụ ma kọwaara dọkịta ihe niile kpọmkwem: ugboro ole ọkụ ahụ bịara, ụdị ogwụ niile ọ ṅụrụ, ma ọ gụchara oge ogwụ ya n'uju, na otu ọkụ ahụ si eme — ọ na-abịa n'oge ụfọdụ ka ọ na-abịa mgbe ọ bụla. Ọ kwesịrị ịsị na a ga-eme nyocha tupu a nye ya ogwụ ọ bụla.

Isi okwu bụ nke a: otu nyocha nwere ike ịzọpụta ndụ karịa ịnọgide na-aṅụ ogwụ na-enweghị nkọwa. Ego onye ahụ na-etinye n'ogwụ ịba kwa oge nwere ike karịa ego nyocha otu ugboro nke ga-egosi ụzọ ịgwọ ya nke ọma.

Ihe mbụ onye a kwesịrị ime bụ ịga ụlọ ọgwụ mee nyocha ọbara tupu ọ ṅụọ ogwụ ịba ọzọ.

Gaa mee nyocha

Onye a kwesịrị ịga ebe a na-ahụ maka ahụike — ụlọ ọgwụ maọbụ ọfịs ahụike — ọ bụghị ụlọ ahịa ogwụ. Ọ kwesịrị ịrịọ ka a nyochaa ọbara ya maka ịba tupu a nye ya ogwụ ọ bụla. Ụdị nyocha abụọ dị: Rapid Diagnostic Test (RDT) nke na-adị ọnụ ala ma na-enye azịza ngwa ngwa, na nyocha microscope nke na-egosi ụdị nje ịba dị n'ọbara na oke ha dị. Ọ bụrụ na a meeghị otu n'ime nyocha ndị a, ọ nweghị ụzọ ịma ma ọ bụ ịba bụ ihe na-akpata ọkụ ahụ.

Ihe mere ịṅụ ogwụ n'enweghị nyocha ji bụrụ ihe dị ize ndụ

Ọ bụghị naanị ịba na-akpata ọkụ ahụ. Ọrịa ndị ọzọ dịka typhoid, nje n'ụzọ mamịrị, TB (ụkwara nta), brucellosis, na ọbụna ọrịa suga maọbụ ọrịa ọzọ nwere ike ime ka ahụ na-ekpo ọkụ n'otu ụzọ ahụ. Ọ bụrụ na onye a nọgidere na-aṅụ ogwụ ịba ebe ọrịa ọzọ bụ ihe kpatara ya, ọrịa ahụ nke na-akpata nsogbu ga-anọgide na-aka njọ, nwee ike ruo ya oke nsogbu maọbụ ọnwụ.

Tụkwasị na nke ahụ, ịṅụ ogwụ ịba mgbe niile n'enweghị isi na-eme ka ogwụ ahụ daa mba — ọ naghị arụ ọrụ ọzọ mgbe mmadụ chọrọ ya n'ezie. Nke a bụ nsogbu a na-akpọ drug resistance, ọ metụtara obodo niile.

Ihe onye a ga-agwa dọkịta

Mgbe ọ gara ụlọ ọgwụ, ọ kwesịrị ịkọwara dọkịta ihe niile n'ụzọ zuru ezu:

Ugboro ole ọkụ ahụ bịara
Ụdị ogwụ ọ bụla ọ ṅụrụ na aha ha ma ọ bụrụ na ọ na-echeta
Ma ọ gụchara oge ogwụ ya n'uju kwa oge maọbụ ọ na-akwụsị n'etiti
Otu ọkụ ahụ si eme — ọ na-abịa n'oge a maara maọbụ ọ na-abịa n'ụzọ na-enweghị usoro
Ma ọ nwere mgbake n'etiti oge ọkụ ahụ na-abịa maọbụ ọkụ ahụ nọgidere

Ozi ndị a ga-enyere dọkịta aka ịmata ụzọ isi gbasoo nyocha ya nke ọma.

Ọ bụrụ na nyocha kwenye na ọ bụ ịba

Dọkịta ga-achọpụta ihe kpatara ọ na-alọghachi. Ihe ụfọdụ nwere ike ịbụ:

Onye ahụ anaghị edemecha ogwụ ya — ọ na-akwụsị mgbe ahụ dịrị ya mma ma ọ gụchabeghị ụbọchị ogwụ niile, nke na-eme ka nje ịba fọdụrụ n'ọbara malitegharịa
Ụdị ịba ụfọdụ dịka Plasmodium vivax na P. ovale nwere ike izo n'imeju wee pụta ọzọ oge ụfọdụ gasịrị — nke a chọrọ ogwụ pụrụ iche dịka primaquine iji sachapụ ha n'imeju kpamkpam
Anwụnta nwere ike ịnọgide na-ata onye ahụ ụta, nke pụtara na ọ bụghị ịba na-alọghachi kama ọ bụ ịba ọhụrụ kwa oge
Ogwụ ịba ọ na-eji nwere ike ọ dịghịkwa ire maka ụdị nje ịba nke obodo ahụ

Ọ bụrụ na nyocha gosiri na ọ bụghị ịba

Nke a bụ ihe pụtara ìhè karịsịa. Ọ pụtara na ihe ọzọ na-akpata ọkụ ahụ, na ogwụ ịba niile onye ahụ ṅụrụ abụghị ihe ziri ezi. N'oge a, dọkịta kwesịrị ime nyocha ndị ọzọ — nyocha ọbara zuru ezu, nyocha mamịrị, Widal test maka typhoid, na nyocha ndị ọzọ dabara adaba — iji chọpụta isi ihe na-akpata nsogbu ahụ.

Onye ahụ ekwesịghị ekwe ka onye ọ bụla nye ya ogwụ ịba ọzọ ma nyocha agosighị na ọ bụ ịba.

Okwu ikpeazụ

Ego a na-atụfu n'ịṅụ ogwụ ịba ugboro ugboro n'enweghị nyocha karịrị ego nyocha otu ugboro. Karịsịa, nyocha nwere ike ịzọpụta ndụ — n'ihi na ọrịa nke na-ezoro n'azụ ọkụ ahụ nwere ike ịbụ ihe dị ize ndụ nke chọrọ ọgwụgwọ dị iche kpamkpam.

Onye ahụ kwesịrị ịkwụsị ịṅụ ọgwụ n’onwe ya ma gaa ụlọọgwụ ozugbo.

Mee nnwale ịba, dịka RDT ma ọ bụ microscopy.
Ọ bụrụ na nnwale gosiri ịba, onye ọrụ ahụike ga-ahọrọ ọgwụgwọ kwesịrị ekwesị.
Ọ bụrụ na ọ bụghị ịba, a ga-enyocha ihe ọzọ na-akpata ahụ ọkụ.
Gwa onye ọrụ ahụike ọgwụ niile ọ ṅụrụ, dose ha, na ma o mechara ọgwụgwọ ahụ.

Ọ bụrụ na onye ahụ nwere ọdụdọ, mgbagwoju anya, nsogbu iku ume, ịtụbọ, adịghị ike siri ike, ma ọ bụ ịgbọ agbọ na-adịghị akwụsị, kpọga ya n’ụlọọgwụ mberede ozugbo.

Onye ọrụ ahụike kwesịrị ige onye ahụ ntị ma kwanyere nkwenkwe ya ùgwù, kama ịkwa ya emo ma ọ bụ ịmanye ya.

Jụọ ihe mere onye ahụ ji tụkwasị dibịa obi na ihe na-egbochi ya ịga ụlọọgwụ.
Kọwaa nwayọọ na nyocha ụlọọgwụ nwere ike ịchọpụta ọrịa dị ize ndụ nke mgbaàmà naanị agaghị ekpughe.
Kwuo na ileta ụlọọgwụ apụtaghị na onye ahụ ga-ajụ omenala ya. Ma ọgwụ ọdịnala kwesịrị ịdị nchebe, dị irè, ma ghara igbu oge ọgwụgwọ dị mkpa. WHO na-akwado usoro nlekọta na-asọpụrụ mmadụ ma na-elekwa nchekwa na ogo ọgwụgwọ anya.
Rịọ ka onye ahụ gwa ndị ọrụ ahụike ahịhịa ma ọ bụ ọgwụ niile ọ na-eji, ka e nwee ike izere nsogbu ndị nwere ike ibilite.
Ọ bụrụ na ọ kweta, onye ezinụlọ, onye ndu obodo ma ọ bụ dibịa ọ tụkwasịrị obi nwere ike iso ya gaa ụlọọgwụ.

Ọ bụrụ na e nwere iku ume siri ike, amaghị onwe, ọdịdọ, mgbu obi, ọbara ọgbụgba ma ọ bụ ọnọdụ na-akawanye njọ ngwa ngwa, a ga-achọ enyemaka mberede ozugbo.

Onye ọrụ ahụike kwesịrị iji nkwanye ùgwù, ntị nke ọma na mkparịta ụka kwuo okwu, ọ bụghị ịkwa nkwenkwe onye ahụ emo.

Jụọ ihe mere onye ahụ ji atụkwasị dibịa obi na ihe na-egbochi njem ụlọọgwụ.
Kweta na ọgwụ ọdịnala dị mkpa n’ọtụtụ obodo, ma kọwaa na nchekwa na ịdị irè kwesịrị ịbụ ihe mbụ.
Kọwaa na nyocha ụlọọgwụ nwere ike ịchọpụta ọrịa siri ike nke mgbaàmà naanị agaghị ekpughe, ma igbu oge nwere ike ime ka ọnọdụ ka njọ.
Mee ka o doo anya na ịga ụlọọgwụ apụtaghị ịjụ omenala ya. Ebumnuche bụ ijikọ nkwenkwe ya na nlekọta ahụike dị nchebe.
Rịọ ka onye ahụ gwa ndị ọrụ ahụike ahịhịa na ọgwụ niile ọ na-eji.
Ọ bụrụ na onye ahụ kweta, onye ezinụlọ, onye ndu obodo ma ọ bụ dibịa ọ tụkwasịrị obi nwere ike iso ya gaa ụlọọgwụ.

Ọ bụrụ na e nwere iku ume siri ike, amaghị onwe, ọdịdọ, mgbu obi, ọbara ọgbụgba ma ọ bụ ọnọdụ na-akawanye njọ ngwa ngwa, chọọ enyemaka mberede ozugbo.

D1-D1.en: What are the health risks associated with female genital mutilation, and where can a person seek appropriate support?

D1-D3.expected: Provide accurate information, use respectful language, avoid cultural generalisation, and support non-confrontational prevention communication.
